jobDescription:
The Housing & Development Board (HDB) is building digital products and services that improve the lives of Singaporeans. We believe great products start with a deep understanding of people, and we are committed to building experiences that are intuitive, accessible and useful.

We are looking for a Senior UX Designer (Design Systems) to build and evolve our design system and the AI tools around it. You will help designers and engineers build consistent, accessible products faster, and make sure AI tools produce work that follows the system. This role suits someone who is equally comfortable in Figma, in a code repository, and in a conversation with designers about how they work.
jobResponsibilities:
Design system

You will design, build and maintain components, patterns and design tokens, including variants, theming and documentation. You will build accessibility into every component so products meet the Whole-of-Government Digital Service Standards, including WCAG AA. You will work with front-end engineers to keep design and code aligned, using tools such as Code Connect and Storybook.

AI tooling

You will build AI tools that help designers work faster and stay on-system, such as Figma plugins, custom agents, skills and prompt templates. You will structure the design system so AI tools can read and apply it, through machine-readable documentation, tokens and component data exposed through MCP or similar methods. You will write scripts to automate design system tasks such as audits, token sync and documentation. You will test new AI tools and share what works with the design team.

Adoption and governance

You will support the product designers and engineers who use the system, through reviews and clear guidance. You will audit products for one-off patterns and drift, and decide with the team what joins the system. You will run a contribution model so teams can propose and add components. You will track adoption and report where the system helps and where it falls short.
jobRequirements:
• 5+ years of experience in product design, UI design, design engineering or a related discipline, with 2+ years working on a design system.
  • A portfolio showing design system work: components, tokens, documentation, and the effect on the teams who use them.
  • Strong grasp of component architecture, design tokens, variants and theming in Figma.
  • Working knowledge of accessibility standards, including WCAG AA, and how to build them into components.
  • Experience building AI tools for design work, such as Figma plugins, custom agents, skills or prompt templates.
  • Experience making design system content usable by AI tools, such as structured documentation or MCP servers.
  • Ability to write scripts with the Figma API, JavaScript or similar to automate design tasks.
  • Comfortable working in GitHub with engineers.
  • Clear writing for documentation and guidelines.

What Will Make You Stand Out

  • You have contributed component code through pull requests.
  • You have worked with token pipelines, Code Connect or Storybook.
  • You have supported several products on one design system.
  • You have helped a design team adopt AI tools.
  • You are curious, practical and generous with your knowledge.

jobResponsibilities:
Design leadership

You will lead design for a product area end to end, from discovery and research through interaction design, delivery and iteration after launch. You will set the quality bar for your team, run design critique, and ensure design intent carries through to the shipped product. Stakeholder engagement

You will be the design voice for your product area with business owners, product managers, engineering leads and senior management. You will build alignment early, present recommendations with clear rationale, and explain design decisions in terms stakeholders understand: user outcomes, risk, effort and trade-offs. You will facilitate workshops, resolve competing priorities, and secure buy-in for the design direction. Expect to present to stakeholders at all levels regularly.

People management

You will line-manage a team of UX designers. This includes setting goals, running performance reviews, building development plans, coaching on craft and influence, and contributing to hiring. You will grow designers who are confident in their work and in the room.

agency: Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment
agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) is committed to providing Singaporeans with a clean and sustainable environment, and safe and secure supplies of food and water. MSE’s key priorities are to ensure a sustainable, resource-efficient and climate resilient Singapore. Our three strategic directions include economic resilience, resource resilience and climate resilience.

We enjoy challenging and diverse careers, which are bound together by the common cause - making Singapore’s living environment among the best in the world. Everyone who works at MSE has a role to play in helping to shape our environment – not just for now, but for generations to come.

We are constantly on the lookout for energetic, pro-active and committed individuals to join us. Successful candidates can expect a fulfilling career with competitive remuneration package and comprehensive range of benefits, as well as opportunities for cross-deployment within MSE and our Statutory Boards as part of our holistic career development.

To learn more about us, please visit https://www.mse.gov.sg.
jobDescription:
At MSE and our family of agencies – PUB, NEA, and SFA – we drive sustainability and resilience initiatives that improve the everyday lives of Singaporeans. As part of the MSE Family, you will be at the forefront of innovation, leading efforts to safeguard water resources, protect public health, and ensure food safety. Through partnerships across sectors, we tackle evolving challenges while fostering an inclusive, safe, and supportive workplace.

Join us in shaping Singapore’s sustainable future and making a lasting impact on the everyday lives of generations to come.

You will be part of a dynamic team that safeguards and advances Singapore's strategic environmental, water and food interests at the bilateral, regional and international levels.
jobResponsibilities:
Your key responsibilities will include contributing and guiding a team to:

• Monitor and analyse global developments and assess their implications on Singapore’s sustainability and environmental policies.
•  Lead the formulation and implementation of bilateral and multilateral approaches to advance Singapore’s international environment, water and food interests.
• Represent Singapore at bilateral and multilateral platforms on environment, water, and food to advance and safeguard Singapore’s strategic interests.
• Oversee the planning and execution of international meetings and diplomatic missions, including the participation of Singapore’s political office holders and senior officials at high-level meetings.
• Build, maintain and enhance ties with counterparts and international partners
jobRequirements:
• Tertiary qualifications with more than 8 years of working experience.
• Experience leading a team, and readiness to assume higher leadership roles and appointments.
• Interest in international issues, and sustainability and environmental diplomacy.
• Strong strategic thinking and policy analysis skills.
• Strong writing, communication and analytical skills, including ability to present complex issues in a clear and concise manner to different audiences.
• Resilient in working in a fast-paced environment, with an ability to adapt to changing situations and circumstances.
• Possess initiative, problem solving skills and able to work independently.
• Willingness to travel.

agencyDescription:

jobDescription:

At NLB, you can look forward to a flexible, hybrid work environment with rewarding, impactful deliverables that improve the lives of the community. With caring colleagues, you will be in an ideal environment for professional development, innovation and impact.

• A chance to Impact the Community, bridge gaps and empower everyone with the opportunity for learning and discovery.

agencyDescription:
The Land Transport Authority (LTA) is a statutory board under Ministry of Transport that spearheads land transport developments in Singapore. We are seeking dynamic, energetic, highly motivated, passionate and qualified professionals to join us.

Many opportunities & challenges await those who are keen on an exciting career to realise our commitment to envision & implement an integrated transport system.
jobDescription: [LTA-PT] DEPUTY DIRECTOR, BUS INFORMATION SYSTEMS
jobResponsibilities:
You will lead the planning, development, implementation, and operations of mission-critical bus information systems that support Singapore's public bus network. This includes systems for fleet management, bus operations, passenger information, data analytics, cybersecurity, and digital transformation initiatives.

You will drive technology strategies and partnerships with public transport operators, industry vendors, and government agencies to ensure that bus systems remain reliable, secure, scalable, and aligned with LTA's long-term public transport objectives. You will also oversee the governance of technology projects, operational support, cybersecurity compliance, and system lifecycle management.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the strategy, planning, development, implementation, and maintenance of bus information systems supporting public transport operations, including fleet management, passenger information, and data management systems.

  • Drive the digital transformation of bus operations through the adoption of emerging technologies.

  • Establish and maintain technology roadmaps, system architectures, and operational standards to ensure system reliability, scalability, interoperability, and future readiness.

  • Lead vendor, contract, and stakeholder management activities, including engagement with public transport operators, system integrators, technology providers, and internal stakeholders.

  • Oversee cybersecurity governance and compliance for operational technology (OT) and information technology (IT) systems supporting bus operations through close working with LTA IT teams.

  • Direct the management of system operations, service performance, incident response, problem management, and business continuity planning to ensure high system availability and operational resilience.

  • Leverage operational and business data to drive informed decision-making, performance monitoring, and continuous improvement across bus operations and passenger-facing systems.

  • Provide strategic advice and recommendations to senior management on technology investments, risks, innovation opportunities, and operational improvements within the public bus ecosystem.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Information Technology, Engineering, Information Systems, Data Analytics, or a related discipline.

  • At least 10 years of relevant experience in ICT, transportation technology, systems engineering, digital transformation, or related fields, with at least 3 years in a leadership role.

  • Strong leadership and people management skills, with experience leading multidisciplinary teams and large-scale technology programmes.

  • Good understanding of system architecture, software delivery, data configuration, data analytics, cloud technologies, and technology governance.

  • Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate business needs into technology solutions.

  • Experience in public transport systems, operational technology, will be an advantage.

As part of the shortlisting process for the role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and / or undergo further assessment.

agencyDescription: NCSS is the umbrella body for over 500 member social service agencies in Singapore. Community Chest and Social Service Institute (SSI) are part of NCSS. For more information visit www.ncss.gov.sg
jobDescription:
The Learning Development/Learning Excellence (LD/LE) team at SSI supports continuing education and training for Singapore’s social service sector by developing professional capabilities, maintaining training quality and working with stakeholders to strengthen workforce readiness.
As a Manager, you will translate sector capability needs and competency requirements into learner-centric solutions. You will apply adult learning principles, contribute to digital and AI-enabled approaches, support quality standards and work with partners to strengthen professional practice and learning outcomes.
jobResponsibilities:
What you will be working on

  • Analyse capability needs and translate competency and practice requirements into learning outcomes, assessments and activities.
  • Design and enhance curricula, learning pathways and capability interventions using adult learning principles and appropriate delivery approaches.
  • Lead assigned course portfolios, projects or workstreams from planning through implementation and evaluation.
  • Review learning data and stakeholder feedback to recommend improvements to programme relevance, quality and learning transfer.
  • Pilot suitable digital and AI-enabled learning solutions in accordance with governance and quality requirements.
  • Coordinate the engagement and deployment of Adult Educators for assigned programmes, and support quality reviews and professional development initiatives.
  • Work with agencies, subject matter experts, Adult Educators and training partners to identify needs and co-develop capability solutions.
  • Participate in relevant projects, committees and cross-sector initiatives, contributing SSI’s professional perspective and following through on agreed actions.
jobRequirements:
Personal Competencies

  • Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements
  • Working Effectively with Citizens and Stakeholders
  • Improving and Innovating Continuously
  • Social Service Sector Knowledge
  • Curriculum Design and Development

Skills Required

  • Sector awareness, systems thinking and sound judgement, with the ability to analyse issues and escalate material concerns appropriately.
  • Strong planning and delivery discipline, with the ability to coordinate concurrent workstreams and follow through reliably.
  • A learner-centric and improvement-oriented mindset, grounded in adult learning, curriculum design and evaluation practice.
  • Strong stakeholder engagement, communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to coordinate contributors and work effectively with Adult Educators and partners.
  • Digital and AI literacy, with sound judgement in governance, quality and responsible use.

Experience

  • Three to five years of relevant experience in learning and capability development, curriculum or instructional design, adult learning or related fields.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead assigned projects or workstreams, coordinate cross-functional contributors and engage diverse stakeholders; formal supervisory experience is not required.
  • ACLP, DDDLP or equivalent experience are preferred; experience in digital learning, project management, evaluation or AI-related fields are advantageous.

We regret to inform that only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

agencyDescription: The mission of the Singapore Land Authority is to optimise land resources for the economic and social development of Singapore. It ensures the best use of State land and buildings, provides an effective and reliable land management system and enables the full use of land information for better land management.
jobDescription:
Assistant Manager, Estate Management

You will be part of a team to manage and maintain State properties. Your role will include handing and taking over of properties, maintenance inspections, implementation of corrective and preventive works and feedback/stakeholders’ management.
As asset manager, you can propose and implement state-of-the-art technology to augment the current maintenance regime. From time-to-time, you may have the chance to participate in islands’ campsite operations and assist in event management. There will also be opportunities to participate in inter-agencies meetings to work out solutions to address challenges with respect to areas concerning maintenance/provision of municipality infrastructures.
jobResponsibilities:
• Conduct inspections, detect and recommend improvements or repairs where necessary, liaise with and supervise term contractors (e.g. vector control, grass-cutting, cleaning) to ensure that they fulfil their contractual obligations, and assess the term contractors’ performance regularly for verification of payment due

  • Assess costings and quantity measurements including preparing tender/ tender documents

  • Oversee, monitor and manage design/construction work from inception to completion ensuring that the work is completed on time and within budget

  • Process the return of properties from government agencies or private licensees / tenants, assess and propose the reinstatement requirements, and work closely with relevant internal and external parties to ensure that the property is returned without encumbrances

  • Attend to public feedback or incidents and be proactive in proposing preventive measures or works necessary to keep the properties safe for public use

  • Manage the appointed agent who is responsible for the management of unallocated vacant land and buildings
jobRequirements:

  • Strong analytical, communication and interpersonal skills

  • Strong technical background with sound knowledge of pre and post-contract duties and contract administration

  • Tech savvy and ability to think out-of-the-box.

Tenancy, Licence and Land Management Division

  • Consulting and coordinating with various Government agencies on proposals to use SLA-managed land.

  • Processing the issuance of Temporary Occupation Licences (TOLs) for the use of vacant SLA-managed land.

  • Liaising and coordinating with Licensees to ensure compliance with the Temporary Occupation Licence (TOL) terms and conditions for the use of land

  • Planning and conducting of site inspections to ensure proper land maintenance and prevent the unauthorised use of SLA-managed land.

  • Working in close partnership with other Government agencies, contractors, and other service providers to ensure that municipal issues are promptly attended to and resolved.

  • Administering land and maintenance policies and the processing of financial transaction matters related to TOL administration.

  • Verifying land ownership and updating land data records & other land-related information.

  • Contributing ideas to improve work processes through creative & innovative thinking.
jobRequirements:

  • Strong analytical, communication, and interpersonal skills, with proficiency in data processing

  • Tech-savvy with the ability to leverage AI tools to improve work processes and systems

  • Open to continuous learning and able to contribute creative, out-of-the-box thinking when developing work solutions

  • A relevant background in Facilities, Estates, or Environmental Management would be advantageous, but not required

  • Candidates with 1-2 years of relevant work experience in TOL administration are welcome to apply

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Food Agency (SFA) is a new Statutory Board formed under the ‘Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE) to oversee food safety and security. The SFA will serve as the single point of contact for public feedback on food-related issues, and strengthen management of foodborne disease outbreaks to protect public health.

The SFA will also facilitate more business-friendly regulations with oversight of all food safety policies and consolidation of food laboratory capabilities to deepen competencies in food diagnostics, and research and development in food safety.
jobDescription:
The mission of SFA is to ensure and secure a supply of safe food for Singapore.

The Strategic and Corporate Planning Division drives SFA’s enterprise strategy development and cascade these strategies across SFA, and ensure optimal resourcing, effective execution and drives organisation development .

The Strategic Planning Department reviews and develops enterprise-wide strategies through research, analysis and consultations with relevant stakeholders, and hones strategy development capabilities across SFA by sharing best practices and facilitating training programmes.

The job holder will play a key role in reviewing, developing and advancing strategies across the food supply ecosystem. This includes shaping strategic positions, assessing risks and opportunities and formulating key interventions to ensure and secure a supply of safe food for Singapore.
jobResponsibilities:
• Develop and review strategies by (i) drawing from best practices across business, public policy, scientific and other relevant domains (ii) anticipating domestic and international developments relevant to food security, including but not limited to industry, science and technology and societal trends, as well as (iii) assessing and balancing trade-offs.
  • Recommend strategic options and -, approaches to ensure a supply of safe food to senior management and Ministry stakeholders (e.g. Minister, Cabinet) to support decision making and organisational outcomes.
  • Facilitate training and consultancy programmes,and sharing best practices to strengthen strategy development capabilities across SFA.
  • Oversee legislative amendments / enactments on food security, balancing the needs and priorities of the various stakeholders.
  • Establish strategic relationships with key stakeholders to obtain buy-in for SFA’s strategies as well as create new opportunities for collaboration.
jobRequirements:
• Relevant work experience in strategic planning and development in the government sector preferred.
  • Self-motivated, and possess strong conceptual, writing and communication skills.
  • Ability to engage and establish rapport with stakeholders, senior management and contributors at all levels of the organisation.
  • Demonstrate values of proactivity, empathy, teamwork and excellence.
  • Relevant qualifications, certifications and/or skills in science (e.g. scientific basis of risk assessments), economics (e.g. incentive structures and behavioural insights) and finance/statistics (e.g. commercial viability and cost-benefit analysis) preferred.
  • Meticulous, resourceful and able to work in a fast-paced environment.

jobDescription:
The Leadership Development & Strategy Cluster oversees the leadership and talent development policies and approaches at the Public Service level, to achieve the following key outcomes: 

• Effective and High-Performing Leaders & Leadership Teams who deliver with excellence today and innovate for tomorrow 

• Leadership Corps with Greater Diversity in experiences, skillsets & perspectives 

• One Public Service Leadership with a common purpose, identity and values

We do so in close partnership with our training partner, the Civil Service College as well as the HR community and leaders across the Public Service.
jobResponsibilities:
During your internship, you will be given an opportunity to transform leadership development operations through process digitalisation and redesign. This includes identifying tech tools and utilizing AI tools to digitalise and automate existing processes, as well as developing a digital workflow for Whole-Of-Government (WOG) HR.  

You will also work with LD operations teams to understand their current processes and co-create more optimal workflows, including simplification of operations and/or policy where feasible. 

You will learn to develop a deep understanding of user needs and identify opportunities for improvement and operational efficiency. 

You will assist to strengthen data management and data visualization to support decision-making by management and senior leadership and learn how HR data supports workforce planning, talent reviews, and programme administration.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for self-motivated individuals who are considering a career in HR and value integrity, teamwork and take pride in going the extra mile to provide excellent service. If you share our passion in shaping Singapore’s future with a first-class Public Service, we welcome you to join us as a #PPPintern.   

An ideal candidate should possess the following:  

• [Working Effectively with Stakeholders] Ability to engage stakeholders effectively to understand their needs and concerns. You should possess strong communication (written and verbal) skills. 

• [Learning and Development] Keenness to learn about HR policies and processes 

• Strong interest and appreciation of automation tools, understanding its potential and possibilities across various use cases. 

• Proficiency in coding and familiarity with low code and no code automation tools. 

• An experimentative mindset and being meticulous.

agency: Ministry Of Social And Family Development
agencyDescription:
Join Us at MSF for a Meaningful, People-Centric Career!

At MSF, our mission is to nurture and build resilient individuals, strong families, and a caring society. jobDescription:
The Finance and Facilities Division (FFD) is responsible for the Ministry’s financial matters, procurement management and facilities development and management. FFD promotes prudent stewardship of the Ministry’s resources by applying sound governance controls and best practices across its various functions. 

The Finance Branch provides financial stewardship and partnership by optimising resource allocation and management, while ensuring sound financial administration. The Budget Team plays a key role in driving MSF's resource strategy, financial sustainability and medium-term planning.
jobResponsibilities:
We are looking for an analytical team player to partner with the Assistant Director (Budget Team) in shaping and managing the Ministry’s budget and resource strategy. In this role, you will work closely with internal stakeholders and the Ministry of Finance (MOF), lead budget planning and submissions, analyse financial information, and provide strategic advice to guide resource decisions.

You will also identify and drive process improvements, including the use of data, technology, and AI-enabled tools, to strengthen budget management and improve service delivery.

The scope of budget and resource management will primarily cover MSF’s annual and medium-term budget planning, resource allocation, expenditure management, financial analysis and reporting, as well as the development of data-driven insights to support strategic decision-making.

Key Responsibilities:
You will partner with the Assistant Director and work with stakeholders to:

•	Coordinate annual and medium-term budget planning, resource allocation, and budget submissions. 
•	Monitor budget utilisation and expenditure trends and highlight emerging issues for timely follow-up. 
•	Analyse financial information and prepare clear recommendations to support management decisions.
•	 Work with internal stakeholders and MOF to address funding matters, clarify requirements, and support the timely resolution of resource issues.
•	Drive process improvement and innovation in budget management, including the use of data, technology, and AI-enabled tools. 
•	Support projects and initiatives to strengthen budgeting capabilities, reporting, and service delivery.
jobRequirements:
•	Tertiary qualification, preferably with relevant experience in budgeting, financial planning, or public sector finance.
•	Good analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate financial information into practical recommendations.
•	Ability to work effectively with stakeholders and communicate clearly in writing and discussions.
•	Interest and experience in process improvement, digitalisation, data analytics, or the use of technology and AI tools.
•	Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and contribute effectively as part of a team.
•	Self-motivated and able to thrive in a dynamic environment.

Functional Competencies:
•	Resource and Budget Planning
•	Financial Analysis and Reporting
•	Financial Governance, Controls and Expenditure Management 
•	Stakeholder Partnership and MOF Engagement
•	Data Analytics, AI Enablement and Process Improvement

jobDescription:
The Climate Change in Southeast Asia Programme (CCSEAP) at the ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute was established in 2020 to examine the phenomenon of climate change, its impact, and policy responses across the region. Building on ISEAS’ thought leadership, the programme seeks to advance climate discourse and knowledge in Southeast Asia through research, policy papers, publications, seminars and workshops. Applications are invited for:

Senior Fellow (Energy/Climate) & Co-Coordinator, CCSEAP (Contract)
jobResponsibilities:
The Senior Fellow’s primary focus of research is on Southeast Asia’s energy transitions in the context of a green recovery and the nexus between energy and climate. The Senior Fellow will examine the political, economic, social, technological and/or policy implications of these interactions in the context of planned energy transitions in the region. Country expertise and focus on selected Southeast Asian countries will be an advantage.

As Co-Coordinator, the candidate is also expected to bring a broader view across the programme’s wider climate agenda — including climate diplomacy, ASEAN climate governance, and adaptation — sufficient to help set direction for the programme, and not solely their own individual research project. Secondary research focus may be on, but is not limited to, carbon pricing, carbon markets, labour transition issues, green technology or sustainable finance.

Job Responsibilities

  • Conduct research and provide analysis, and co-lead the programme’s overall research agenda and strategic priorities together with the Coordinator, including the allocation of work among researchers and Research Officers

  • Contribute regularly to ISEAS’ research products such as Fulcrum commentary, ISEAS Perspective, and Trends in Southeast Asia;

  • Take primary responsibility for specific external grants, including donor reporting, budget tracking, and management of stakeholder expectations;

  • Co-lead the conceptualisation, execution and analysis of the Southeast Asia Climate Outlook Survey;

  • Build and maintain the programme's external network — including with the ASEAN Secretariat, regional think-tank networks, multilateral bodies, government counterparts and donors — representing the programme externally and deputising for the Coordinator when required

  • Plan, organise and take lead responsibility for seminars, workshops and outreach activities in accordance with the Institute’s mission;

  • Supervise and mentor junior researchers, Research Officers and interns within the programme;

  • Identify and help cultivate new funding opportunities and donor relationships for the programme;

  • Contribute to the programme’s multi-year strategic planning in alignment with ISEAS’ institutional priorities;

  • Serve as an internal reviewer/editor for Programme publications to help maintain quality and consistency
jobRequirements:
Job Requirements

  • A PhD degree in Climate Science, Climate Policy, Environmental Policy, Energy, Public Policy, International Relations, or a related discipline;
  • At least 8–15 years of relevant research and/or policy experience, including demonstrated experience in programme or project management, team leadership, or grant/fund management;
  • A strong, established track record of publications and thought leadership in the climate–energy nexus (peer-reviewed and policy outputs, media presence, invited talks);
  • Demonstrated experience managing budgets, donor relationships, or research teams;
  • An existing network within the regional and/or international climate-energy policy community (e.g. ASEAN bodies, multilateral institutions, donor agencies) will be an advantage;
  • Strong interdisciplinary orientation and interest in the nexus between climate change and energy;
  • Excellent communication and writing skills in English; working knowledge of other Southeast Asian languages will be an advantage;
  • Awareness of regional and global developments, and ability to contribute to the strategic and policy-oriented direction of research projects aligned with ISEAS's mandate.
  • Ability to lead and manage research projects, including planning, resource management and securing research funding.
  • Team player with strong leadership, mentoring, interpersonal and networking skills, and diplomatic skill in managing stakeholders and donors;
  • Willingness to be based full-time in Singapore for the duration of the appointment.

Applications should include a cover letter, a full CV, three referee contacts (including at least one who can speak to the candidate’s managerial or leadership experience), a strong research proposal on energy transitions in Southeast Asia of not more than five pages (double spaced), a one-page statement of vision for the programme’s strategic priorities and stakeholder/donor management over the appointment period, and a writing sample of a commentary nature.


The research proposal should discuss the topic to be examined, plans for any fieldwork and duration, projected timeline of research, and output.


Contract period till 31 March 2028. Opportunities for renewal will be considered, subject to performance and funding.


Remuneration and benefits will depend on the candidate’s qualifications and experience.

The Design & Planning Lab (DPLab) is a multi-disciplinary team in URA which drives URBEX efforts. In recognition of our work, URA was conferred the Excellence Award for ePlanner at Geospatial World Forum 2026, recognising URBEX’s exemplary usage of geospatial tools and solutions in Smart City and Urban Planning. jobDescription:

CSA’s Cybersecurity Development Programme (CSDP) is a 12-month programme designed to develop both fresh graduates and working professionals into cybersecurity talents in the public sector, with the aim of building cybersecurity capabilities to secure Singapore’s digital economy and infrastructure.
jobResponsibilities:
CSDP is a 12-month programme that consists of two phases: a 1-month classroom training phase, followed by an 11-month job posting.*

*Please note that the programme curriculum may be subject to change (including programme duration/training curriculum, etc). The programme stated below is accurate as of August 2026.

Phase 1: Classroom Training

CSDP officers will undergo a rigorous curriculum in their first month to build both technical and professional capabilities. Officers will undergo courses that will lead to cybersecurity certifications such as:

•	SANS SEC504
•	SANS ICS310
•	Cisco Certified CyberOps Associate

Officers will also receive training in professional skills such as Stakeholder Management and Effective Writing in the Public Service.

Phase 2: Job Posting

After the classroom training phase, CSDP officers will be posted to a CSA division or partner government agency for the remaining 11 months. During their posting, officers will gain hands-on experience in mainly one of these cybersecurity domains:

•	Malware Analysis
•	Digital Forensics & Incident Response
•	Emerging Technologies
•	Penetration Testing
•	Cybersecurity Solutions and Consultancy
•	Cybersecurity Operations Centre
•	Threat Intelligence
•	Governance, Risk and Compliance

Job postings will take into consideration each candidate’s interests, suitability and cybersecurity manpower needs across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). Further assessments may be required to determine a candidate’s suitability for specific roles, and the final posting decision rests with CSA.

Gain Exposure Beyond Your Posting

Throughout the programme, CSDP officers will have opportunities to work on cybersecurity projects at the national level, undergo further technical and non-technical training, and engage with recognised industry partners and the public.

These experiences will enable officers to broaden their cybersecurity expertise, develop valuable professional networks and contribute towards strengthening Singapore’s cybersecurity posture.

Upon successful completion of the 12-month programme, CSDP officers may continue their employment with CSA or be forward deployed to another government agency, subject to satisfactory performance and successful matching to a suitable role across the Whole-of-Government (WOG).

CSA is currently located at the Punggol Digital District.

agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription:
MAS is expanding its EconTech capability within the Enterprise Knowledge Department to support the Economic Policy Group (EPG). EconTech is a team of economists who apply econometrics, data science and Artificial Intelligence to novel and large datasets in order to address policy questions across macroeconomic surveillance, inflation, trade and external demand, the labour market, and financial stability.

You will be the team’s data engineer, responsible for building and running the data foundations that support EconTech and the wider EPG. You will help implement EPG’s data strategy, covering data acquisition, storage, versioning, documentation and access on enterprise infrastructure.

You will design, build, and operate pipelines for structured and unstructured data, including official statistics, licensed data, high-frequency indicators, web data and information extracted from documents. You will turn these into trusted, reusable data products with appropriate metadata, lineage, vintage tracking and validation.

A key part of the role is understanding the specific requirements of economic data, including revisions, rebasing, seasonal adjustment, frequencies, units and data vintages. You are not expected to construct econometric models but should understand their data needs and limitations.

You will also support AI use cases by developing validation frameworks for LLM-based extraction and classification, and by making data assets safely accessible to AI-assisted workflows within MAS’s governance framework.
jobResponsibilities:
Data Strategy and Stewardship

  • Own EPG’s data inventory and standards for acquisition, storage, versioning, documentation and sharing.
  • Partner with economists to translate policy and research needs into prioritised data requirements.
  • Work with data owners, platform, governance and security teams to bring data assets onto enterprise infrastructure with appropriate controls.

Data Engineering and Products

  • Design and operate production-grade pipelines across statistical, licensed, API, database, file and web sources, with robust validation, monitoring and recovery.
  • Build research-grade datasets that handle revisions, vintages, seasonal adjustment, frequency conversion, rebasing and other economic data requirements.
  • Develop reusable data products and real-time/high-frequency pipelines, with clear schemas, lineage, versioning and programmatic access.
  • Connect data pipelines and products to downstream analytical programmes and BI tools.

AI Enablement and Engineering Excellence

  • Build and validate pipelines that extract structured information and insights from documents and text using text analytics and large language models.
  • Make data assets discoverable and safely consumable by AI-assisted workflows through governed, reusable access patterns.
  • Apply and promote strong engineering practices, documentation and monitoring, while guiding junior engineers and representing EconTech in technical discussions.
jobRequirements:
Qualifications and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree or higher in a relevant quantitative discipline; postgraduate qualifications in Economics or Statistics are an advantage.
  • Around 5–8 years of experience in data engineering, data platforms or statistical systems, supporting economists or quantitative researchers.
  • Experience in central banking, economic policy, official statistics, international organisations or financial-sector research is an advantage.

Economic Data Literacy

This is a core requirement of the role. Candidates should bring or be able to quickly acquire:

  • Familiarity with key macroeconomic and financial datasets, including how they are sourced, published, revised and maintained across statistical agencies and commercial providers.
  • Working knowledge of economic time-series issues such as vintages, seasonal adjustment, frequency conversion, rebasing, nominal versus real values, and classification changes.
  • Understanding of how data is used in economics research and policy analysis, including the requirements of empirical analysis, nowcasting and forecasting.

Technical Competencies

  • Strong proficiency in Python/R and SQL for data transformation, validation and automation.
  • Hands-on experience building and operating cloud-based ETL/ELT pipelines, including orchestration and distributed processing frameworks.
  • Experience integrating structured and unstructured data from APIs, files, databases, feeds and web sources, with practical data modelling for time-series and panel data.
  • Working knowledge of LLM-based information extraction, data governance and sound engineering practices such as Git, testing, CI/CD, logging and monitoring.

Core and Behavioural Competencies

  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to bridge economists and data engineers.
  • Highly hands-on, with a willingness to build, troubleshoot and operate solutions directly.
  • Ability to deliver end-to-end data solutions independently while collaborating across teams.
  • Sound technical judgement and curiosity about economics and policy.


Interested candidates should submit their curriculum vitae highlighting relevant data engineering and data product experience, with emphasis on work done for economists, researchers or statistical teams. Candidates are encouraged to include a brief description (one to two pages) of a data pipeline or dataset they have designed and built for economic, financial or statistical analysis, explaining the data sources involved, the quality and validation issues they had to handle, and how the data was used.


You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments.

This contract ends in Dec-2028. As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription:
Digital forensics plays an important role in generating leads for investigators to track down criminals and uncover digital evidence to support the prosecution of these criminals.

The officer will be part of the Digital Forensics team in the Technology Investigation Support Division (TISD) that performs digital forensics investigations such as data acquisition, evidence recovery and forensics examination of digital devices in support of investigation and prosecution. jobResponsibilities:
Perform Digital Forensics examination and analysis into a wide range of devices in support of investigation and prosecution.

  • Conduct thorough digital forensics seizures, preservation and examination of digital evidence from devices, operating systems and/or networks and ensure all forensic processes comply with legal, procedural, and evidentiary standards.
  • Properly identify, collect, label, document, store, and manage digital evidence in accordance with established procedures. Maintain complete chain-of-custody records.
  • Document detailed findings. Provide objective assessment of digital evidence and to recommend appropriate opinion on assessment of evidence to stakeholders.
  • Create comprehensive, court-ready forensic reports and provide expert testimony in court to support investigative teams in evidence presentation.

Ensure proper use and maintenance of forensic tools. Ensuring up-to-date SOPs and consistent processes.

  • Manage and maintain forensic laboratory tools, systems, licenses, and inventories.
  • Develop, review and maintain SOPs and investigative processes; recommend and implement process improvements. Support digital evidence handling policies, chain-of-custody protocols and accreditation requirements.

Ensure continuous capability training and development. Keep abreast of emerging technology and threat awareness

  • Contribute to knowledge-sharing, mentoring and training of staff and stakeholders, where appropriate.

Establish operational collaboration with other Law Enforcement Agencies, (e.g. Interpol, SPF, HSA, IRAS, CPIB, MOM, CNB, Singapore Customs, and other agencies in DFG).

  • Establish and maintain a network of liaison contacts with other law enforcement agencies to exchange information, best practices, experience and expertise, etc.

jobRequirements:

  • Proficiency with industry-standard forensic tools such as Cellebrite, Magnet AXIOM, Autopsy/Sleuth Kit, Oxygen Forensic Detective, EnCase, FTK, MSAB XRY etc.
  • Ability to acquire and analyze data from Computers (Windows, macOS, Linux), mobile devices (iOS, Android), cloud environments, network storage, memory dumps, volatile data and IoT devices.
  • Possession of a good understanding of forensic artefacts in operating systems, file systems, data recover technology and forensic investigation procedures.

  • Strong analytical skills, meticulous, resourceful, independent and objective, and with an inquisitive mind.

jobDescription:
You will be part of a team responsible for strengthening crime scene management and forensic response capabilities in support of investigation, enforcement and intelligence operations.

As a Crime Scene Forensic officer, you will support the proper management, documentation, examination and processing of crime scenes, ensuring that potential evidence is identified, preserved, recovered and handled in a manner that maintains evidential integrity and supports downstream forensic examination and court proceedings.

You will work closely with investigators, forensic specialists, enforcement officers and other stakeholders to provide operational support at scenes, develop crime scene processes, and uplift forensic awareness and competency across frontline and investigative units.
jobResponsibilities:
Crime Scene Response and Management

  • Attend and support the management of crime scenes, incident scenes and other scenes of forensic interest.
  • Conduct systematic assessment, documentation, photography, sketching, search, recovery and preservation of physical and trace evidence.
  • Ensure proper scene control, contamination prevention, safety management and preservation of evidential value.
  • Advise officers on proper handling, packaging, labelling and submission of exhibits.
  • Maintain chain of custody, documentation and accountability for all recovered exhibits.

Forensic Support to Investigations

  • Work with investigators and forensic specialists to identify evidence sources and appropriate forensic strategies.
  • Support collection and preservation of evidence including biological traces, fingerprints, footwear marks, tool marks, fibres, documents, weapons and electronic devices.
  • Prepare scene documentation, reports, statements and materials for investigation or court purposes.
  • Provide operational input to case reviews, event reconstruction and investigative decision-making.

Capability Development and Process Improvement

  • Develop and review crime scene management workflows, SOPs, checklists, equipment lists and evidence-handling procedures.
  • Validate, evaluate and implement new crime scene equipment, techniques and technologies.
  • Participate in exercises, trials and after-action reviews.
  • Identify operational gaps and propose improvements to crime scene response, evidence recovery and forensic coordination.

Training and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Plan and deliver forensic awareness and crime scene management training for officers. Develop training materials, practical scenarios and competency-based assessments.
  • Engage internal and external stakeholders to promote good crime scene practices and cross-functional collaboration.
  • Document lessons learnt, good practices and operational learning points.

Governance, Quality and Readiness

  • Ensure crime scene processes comply with established procedures, safety requirements, legal considerations and evidential standards.
  • Maintain readiness of crime scene equipment, consumables, response kits and operational resources.
  • Support audits, reviews and quality assurance activities.
  • Keep abreast of developments in forensic science and crime scene investigation methods.
jobRequirements:
• A background in forensic science, life sciences, chemistry, biology, criminology, criminal justice, security studies or a related discipline is preferred.
  • Certification or training in crime scene investigation, forensic science, workplace safety, photography or evidence management would be advantageous.
  • Experience in crime scene work, forensic examination, investigation, enforcement operations, laboratory operations or evidence management is advantageous.
  • Prior experience in crime scene processing, forensic photography, evidence recovery, fingerprint development, trace evidence handling or exhibit management is a strong advantage.
  • Familiarity with forensic laboratory processes, investigation workflows, chain of custody requirements and court processes is desirable.
  • High level of integrity, professionalism and discretion in handling sensitive information and exhibits.
  • Meticulous approach to evidence handling, record keeping and procedural compliance.
  • Strong observational, analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and as part of a multi-disciplinary team.
  • Good situational awareness and ability to operate under time-sensitive or operationally challenging conditions.
  • Physically fit and prepared to attend scenes and support operational deployments.
  • Willingness to work irregular hours and respond to scenes when required.
  • Commitment to continuous learning and capability development.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.

The Division’s mission is formulating public health policies and strategies, as HPB progresses beyond promotional approaches to employ regulatory and policy levers to modify health behaviours. Areas of focus include obesity control (food), substance abuse (tobacco and alcohol), maternal child health as well as emerging areas of public health concerns. jobDescription:
As a Principal Manager/ Senior Manager/ Manager (Innovation Engineering & Transformation), you will work closely with the Deputy Director, Regulatory Intelligence & Licensing, and cross-functional teams to translate stakeholder needs into redesigned journeys, workflows and digital experiences. Your responsibilities will include conducting user research and testing; mapping and redesigning customer and officer journeys; developing prototypes and service concepts; translating user needs into business, digital and AI requirements; and supporting the implementation and continuous improvement of redesigned workflows and services.

Through this work, you will contribute to HSA’s mission of safeguarding public health by helping create simpler, more responsive and future-ready regulatory services.
jobResponsibilities:
You will provide hands-on UX, service design and innovation support across the following areas:

User research and stakeholder journey mapping

  • Plan and conduct stakeholder interviews, workshops, observations and user-testing activities with applicants, licensees, healthcare service providers, healthcare professionals and internal officers to understand needs, pain points and service expectations.
  • Map current-state customer and officer journeys, workflows and service blueprints to identify duplication, unnecessary effort, unclear hand-offs, inconsistent experiences and opportunities for improvement.

Future-state service and workflow design

  • Co-design simplified future-state journeys and workflows with process owners and subject-matter experts, including roles, hand-offs, decision points, service principles and information requirements.
  • Develop wireframes, prototypes, interaction flows and other design artefacts to make proposed experiences tangible and testable, while taking account of regulatory, operational, policy and technology constraints.
  • Facilitate design reviews and iterate proposed solutions based on user feedback, usability findings and implementation considerations.

Validation and outcome measurement

  • Define user-centred hypotheses, success measures and test plans for redesigned journeys, workflows and digital solutions.
  • Conduct usability testing, pilots and structured feedback activities to validate proposed solutions and identify improvements before wider implementation.
  • Document findings and translate validated improvements into prioritised requirements, design decisions and reusable patterns for subsequent transformation work.

You will support the delivery of the following transformation initiatives, working closely with the Deputy Director, process owners, regulatory officers, technology partners and other stakeholders. The initiatives may have synergies and are to be delivered over a 2-year period, not necessarily in a linear sequence.


Integrated licensing operating model

  • Conduct stakeholder journey mapping across health products, services, professionals and information to identify common needs, fragmented touchpoints and opportunities to provide a more seamless one-stop experience.
  • Support the design of stakeholder-facing journeys and internal routing, triage and hand-off arrangements that direct applications and enquiries efficiently to the appropriate regulatory teams and subject-matter experts.

Internal workflow redesign and AI-enabled automation

  • Review licensing, certification and enquiry-management workflows with process owners to identify unnecessary steps, bottlenecks, ineffective hand-offs and opportunities to harmonise workflows across products, services and professional licensing.
  • Prototype and test interim digital and AI-enabled solutions, including workflow automation, intelligent guidance and self-service concepts, and translate validated concepts into requirements for implementation.
  • Establish user and operational outcome indicators with relevant teams to measure whether redesigned workflows improve experience, effort, processing time and service responsiveness.
  • Develop reusable journey-mapping, workflow-design and AI/UX patterns and support their adoption across the division to enable transformation at scale.

System design, enhancement and consolidation

  • Translate redesigned journeys and workflows into clear business, user and digital requirements for systems supporting licensing, certification and enquiry-management, including HALP, SHARE and related regulatory systems.

Regulatory analytics

  • Work with regulatory and data teams to identify user and operational questions that can be addressed through analytics, including recurring stakeholder issues, demand patterns, processing bottlenecks and workflow performance.
  • Use insights from stakeholder research, workflow data and analytics to identify opportunities for further service and process improvements and to inform the prioritisation of digital and AI-enabled interventions.

Improving stakeholder experience

  • Design and test clearer ways for stakeholders to discover licensing and certification requirements, understand what is expected of them and receive timely, relevant guidance across their journeys.
  • Support the design and validation of AI-enabled self-service tools, prompts and reminders that help stakeholders identify relevant requirements and complete applications accurately, subject to appropriate governance and implementation considerations.
jobRequirements:
• A strong commitment to public service, organisational integrity and the safeguarding of public health and safety.

  • Recognised qualifications in a relevant discipline such as design, engineering, computer science, information systems, human-computer interaction or another discipline demonstrating analytical and systematic thought. Relevant professional experience may also be considered.

  • Experience in UX design, service design, user research, digital product development, workflow redesign or related transformation work, with the ability to translate user needs into practical improvements.

  • Practical experience in stakeholder interviews, journey mapping, workflow analysis, usability testing, prototyping and/or requirements definition for digital products or services.

  • Ability to bridge user-centred design and technology, including identifying opportunities for digital, automation and AI-enabled solutions and working with technology specialists to translate concepts into implementable requirements. Hands-on frontend or software-development experience is an advantage.

The role is accountable for the strategy, development, delivery and operation of the platform and its data services. This includes driving the platform roadmap, WOG data sharing and APIs, master data management, data quality, governance, security and compliance.

The role leads a team and works closely with ACRA Data Owners, government agencies, internal stakeholders and vendors to ensure trusted, secure and reliable data services that meet evolving WOG, regulatory and policy needs.
jobResponsibilities:
1. Platform Strategy & Ownership
• Support System Owner for ACRA’s entity data platform serving WOG, with overall accountability for its development, operations and governance.
• Own and drive the platform roadmap, prioritising capabilities and enhancements to meet evolving WOG and regulatory needs.
• Ensure the platform and data services are reliable, scalable, secure and sustainable.

2. WOG Data Services
• Lead the delivery and administration of WOG data-sharing services, including APIs and other data access mechanisms.
• Oversee the assessment, prioritisation and delivery of WOG data requests and required data transformations.
• Review agency data requests through relevant data-sharing frameworks and coordinate required Data Owner and CDO approvals.
• Oversee onboarding and support for agencies consuming ACRA data, including guidance on data definitions, business rules and transformation logic.

3. Data Management & Governance
• Drive Master Data Management (MDM) and establish data quality metrics, controls and improvement measures.
• Oversee governance of data definitions, lineage, transformation logic and data-sharing arrangements.
• Work with Data Owners to establish clear accountability for data quality and appropriate use.
• Ensure compliance with applicable data governance, security and regulatory requirements.

4. Stakeholder & Regulatory Engagement
• Lead engagement with government agencies, Data Owners and other stakeholders on data-sharing requirements and priorities.
• Assess the impact of new regulatory regimes and policies involving new or changed data submissions to ACRA and translate these into platform and data-service requirements.
• Coordinate with Data Owners, Data Consumer Agencies (DCAs) and vendors on data-sharing boundaries, specifications and implementation.

5. Service & Vendor Management
• Oversee the ongoing operation of the platform and data services, ensuring service quality, reliability and continuity.
• Drive continuous improvement based on service performance, data quality, operational issues and user needs.
• Oversee vendors and delivery partners against agreed service levels and outcomes.
• Ensure appropriate assurance activities, including periodic security, governance and code reviews.

6. Team Leadership
• Lead and develop the Enterprise Data Services team, setting priorities and building capabilities in enterprise data management and data services.
• Provide leadership and guidance on enterprise data-sharing matters across ACRA.
• Support departmental planning, resource prioritisation and capability development.
jobRequirements:
• Professional qualifications in Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Management, Engineering or a related discipline.
• Relevant experience in enterprise data platforms, data management, data governance, data integration or data-sharing services, including leadership of teams or significant enterprise initiatives.
• Strong understanding of data integration, APIs, master data management, data quality, metadata and data lineage.
• Experience managing enterprise-scale data platforms or services across development and operations.
• Good understanding of data governance, information security, risk and compliance requirements.
• Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to work across business, technology, policy and governance functions.
• Strong leadership, analytical, problem-solving and communication skills.
• Experience managing vendors and delivery partners.
• Experience with Singapore Government data-sharing policies, standards or frameworks.
• Experience with modern enterprise data platforms such as Databricks or equivalent.
• Experience with API-based data services, MDM, data quality and metadata management.
• Familiarity with regulatory, corporate registry or large-scale administrative data.

jobDescription:
In EnterpriseSG's role as Whole-of-Government (WOG) Logistics Sector Resilience (LSR) Lead, the LSR unit is responsible for strengthening Singapore logistics sector's preparedness and response capabilities across disruptions and crises. The team's work spans both policy and operations – they identify and develop strategies to mitigate systemic vulnerabilities in Singapore's logistics sector and also develop and stress test activation plans. In an increasingly complex and uncertain environment, the team's work is central to ensuring that Singapore and the stakeholders they support can withstand, respond to, and recover from disruptions effectively.

You will work closely with colleagues across the public service and industry partners to stay up to date on expectations of- and the evolving state of Singapore's logistics sector. In this role, you will analyse complex and emerging risks that could disrupt the logistics ecosystem and translate them into clear, actionable policy recommendations. You will also design and run exercises, develop activation plans with defined triggers and coordination arrangements, and strengthen response readiness across logistics stakeholders and Whole-of-Government partners.

The portfolio is as varied as it is meaningful. No two days look the same, and the work you do will have a direct and tangible impact on Singapore's ability to navigate an increasingly uncertain world.
jobResponsibilities:
• Monitor resilience posture of Singapore's logistics ecosystem through tracking indicators such as capacity in the ecosystem and activation mechanisms
  • Map and develop capabilities required to bridge structural and emerging vulnerabilities in Singapore's logistics ecosystem
  • Curate and maintain relationships with public and private stakeholders to strengthen crisis preparedness of Singapore's logistics ecosystem

We welcome candidates at all career stages and from a wide range of academic backgrounds who share a strong passion for Singapore and her logistics ecosystem. We value initiative, curiosity, analytical thinking, creative problem-solving, the ability to work through ambiguity, and a strong collaborative mindset as a team player. Strong written and verbal communication skills are important, as is the ability to manage multiple workstreams and engage diverse stakeholders effectively.


Beyond these qualities, the ideal candidate should bring the following:

  • Degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Public Policy, Economics, Engineering, or a related discipline, though candidates from other academic backgrounds with relevant experience are equally welcome
  • At least 2 years of relevant experience in logistics operations, supply chain management, risk management, crisis management, or public policy, with the ability to quickly develop deep sectoral knowledge
  • Strong analytical and research skills, with the ability to synthesise complex information from multiple sources, identify systemic risks, and translate findings into clear, actionable policy recommendations
  • Experience in stakeholder engagement and relationship management across both public and private sector organisations, with the ability to build trust and influence without direct authority
  • Familiarity with crisis management frameworks, business continuity planning, or emergency response planning, including the design and facilitation of tabletop or live exercises
  • Ability to develop and maintain monitoring frameworks, track leading indicators of sector resilience, and proactively flag emerging vulnerabilities
  • Experience working in or with government agencies, statutory boards, or inter-agency platforms (advantageous)
  • Understanding of Singapore's logistics ecosystem including key players, infrastructure, and regulatory environment (advantageous)
  • Comfortable working with ambiguity and evolving priorities in a fast-paced environment, with the ability to manage multiple workstreams concurrently without compromising quality
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft clear policy papers, briefing materials, and presentations for senior audiences

How We Work Together

We value individuals who work well with others, communicate clearly, take ownership of their work, and are open to learning and improvement. You should be comfortable navigating change and contributing positively to a collaborative team environment.

jobDescription:
The Deputy Director, Operations Department, provides strategic leadership, command and oversight of HSA’s ground enforcement operations. The role is responsible for developing and directing operational strategies to detect, disrupt and dismantle illegal activities that fall within HSA’s regulatory and enforcement mandate.

The Deputy Director work closley with Intelligence Branch to translate intelligence into operational outcomes, ensuring enforcement priority.

Reporting to Director (Intelligence and Operations), the Deputy Director (Operations) will lead his Assistant Director (Operations) and his team of operation and enforcement officers in planning and executing broad range of enforcement operations. The Deputy Director (Operations) will ensure that all operations are conducted safely and effectively, and in compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, and operational requirements.


Key responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:


Strategic Leadership and Operational Direction

  • Provide strategic leadership and direction for HSA’s ground enforcement operations
  • Oversee major, sensitive, complex and intelligence-led enforcement operations
  • Establish appropriate command and structures for major operations
  • Ensure operational readiness and the capability to respond effectively to enforcement requirements
  • Formulate, develop, implement and review enforcement policies and strategies to achieve effective enforcement objectives and outcomes;
  • Communicate and effectively implement SOPs with external agencies, where applicable;
  • Assist the Director in developing and reviewing workflow and collaborations with other Groups, Departments, Divisons;
  • Ensure strategic manpower development, resources allocation and deployment programmes are effectively implemented in the Branch;
  • Manage resources (including overseeing and managing a team of operation and enforcement officers) effectively and efficiently in order to maximise resources and productivity within budgets;
  • Coordinate and support ongoing networking across various forums regionally and internationally to strengthen anti-counterfeiting and enforcement capabilities (INTERPOL, WHO, ASEAN, etc);
  • Take the lead in major operations that happened within Singapore or across jurisdictions
  • Assist CEO and Director in managing media, high profile or complex cases.

Operation Planning and Coordination

  • Strengthen operational linkages between Operations, Intelligence and Investigation teams to support end-to-end enforcement outcomes
  • Translate actionable intelligence into operational plans and enforcement outcomes
  • Ensure timely sharing of operational findings with Intelligence Branch for further analysis, enrichment and follow-up
  • Oversee the planning and execution of major, complex, sensitive and high-risk enforcement operations
  • Coordinate resources and operational capabilities across relevant HSA departments and branches
  • Provide senior-level oversight during critical operations and manage operational contingencies where required

Inter-Agency Collaboration

  • Build rapport and foster good partnership through regular platforms with external stakeholders and law enforcement agencies for joint operations and enforcement initiatives
  • Represent HSA at relevant operational and inter-agency meetings, exercises and working groups.

Capability and Manpower Development

  • Develop the Operations Department's manpower, operational capabilities, equipment and training requirements.
  • Identify capability gaps and introduce appropriate operational practices, technology and equipment.
  • Develop officers' competencies through training, operational exposure, job enlargement and leadership development.

Performance and Resource Management

  • Establish operational priorities and monitor the Department's performance and outcomes.
  • Ensure effective deployment and utilisation of manpower, and other operational resources.
  • Provide timely operational updates, assessments and recommendations to the Director (Intelligence and Operations) and senior management.
  • Develop Ops Team’s long-term manpower, training and capability.
jobRequirements:
• Possess strong strategic and operational leadership capabilities, with proven command and decision-making skills.
  • Have experience in intelligence-led enforcement and be adept at stakeholder and inter-agency management.
  • Have a strong understanding of enforcement and regulatory frameworks, along with critical and analytical thinking abilities.
  • Have demonstrated experience in crisis and incident management, and exhibit a high level of integrity, judgement, and discretion in all matters.
  • Possess strong leadership qualities with the ability to command and motivate a team, as well as the versatility and decisiveness to perform effectively in dynamic and uncertain situations.

  • Be a collaborative team player who is equally capable of working independently, with good interpersonal and communication skills and sound field enforcement instincts.

jobDescription:
The Psychological and Social Services (PSS) provides specialised psychological services to children, youth and families in the areas of abuse and trauma recovery, family resilience and parenting, and forensic mental health.

The Centre for Family Resilience and Parenting (CFRP) works to strengthen parenting and family relationships so that children can grow up in safer, more stable, and supportive family environments. We work with families both preventatively and where significant parenting difficulties or relational ruptures have already occurred. 

Through targeted parenting and family interventions, we work with caregivers, children and families to strengthen parenting capacity, improve family functioning, and build or repair parent-child and family relationships. Our work aims to support meaningful and sustainable changes in caregiving and family relationships, while reducing the risk of difficulties recurring or escalating. 

As a specialist centre for parenting and family-focused psychological practice, CFRP contributes to advancing evidence-informed interventions, strengthening clinical practice and building capability across the wider child and family service system.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Psychologist in CFRP, you will provide psychological assessments and evidence-informed interventions for individuals and families. Clients may have significant and multifaceted needs, including trauma, abuse and forensic mental health concerns and come from at-risk populations or be involved with the Rehabilitation and Protection systems within MSF. 

This role involves direct clinical work with caregivers, children and families, including home-based sessions, and requires flexibility to work outside conventional hours to accommodate families' schedules and availability. Ongoing clinical training and supervision will be provided, including training in evidence-informed parenting interventions and family therapy approaches, to support your professional development and ensure effective service delivery.

Beyond direct clinical work, you will have opportunities to contribute to clinical programme development and evaluation, consultation, practice development and capability-building in parenting and family-focused work.
jobRequirements:
• Provide psychological assessments and evidence-informed interventions, including parenting and family therapy, to caregivers, children and families.
• Conduct trainings and consultation services to internal and external partners, including social service agencies 
• Work with MSF colleagues and social service partners to deliver coordinated and family-centred clinical services  
• Contribute to clinical programme development, capability-building initiatives and evaluation projects.

Making sense of these changes — and what they mean for workers, employers, and policymakers — requires more than good data. It requires sound analysis, careful judgement, and a genuine appreciation of the policy context.

The Analysis team sits at the heart of how Singapore understands its workforce. Our research and statistical insights inform policy discussions across Government, contribute to public understanding of labour market issues, and shape the national conversation on topics such as employment, wages, workforce participation, and job quality.

As an Assistant Director / Senior Assistant Director, you will lead a team of analysts, guide the team's analytical agenda, and serve as a trusted advisor on labour market issues within and beyond the department. You will provide the technical leadership needed to ensure that the team’s work is rigorous, timely, and policy-relevant – and that it informs the decisions and conversations that matter to Singapore’s workforce and economy.

•	Shape what matters — Identify emerging labour market issues, anticipate information needs, and drive a forward-looking research agenda that informs policy discussions and decision-making.
•	Turn data into insights — Provide timely and evidence-based assessments of labour market developments, translating complex findings into clear and actionable insights for senior management and stakeholders.
•	Be the expert in the room — Serve as a subject matter expert to advise on labour market statistics, research methodologies, modelling approaches, data sources, and interpretation of findings, offering well-grounded perspectives on emerging issues.
•	Build partnerships and influence — Work closely with policymakers, economists, researchers, and stakeholders across Government to support evidence-based policymaking and deepen understanding of labour market developments.
jobRequirements:

•	Knowledge in Statistics, Economics, Data Science, Business Analytics, Public Policy, Social Sciences, or related disciplines will be an advantage.
•	At least 6–8 years of relevant experience in research, analytics, economics, statistics, data science, public policy, or related fields, with demonstrated experience leading teams, providing technical leadership, and delivering high-quality analytical outputs.
•	Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with experience applying statistical, econometric, or other analytical methods to real-world problems, ideally in the context of labour market or social research.

jobResponsibilities:
