jobDescription: SENIOR/ MANAGER, DATA PARTNERSHIPS — TRANSPORT AI PROGRAMME, LTA SINGAPORE
jobResponsibilities:
Singapore's land transport network moves millions of people every day. As AI reshapes what's possible in transport operations, the Land Transport Authority is investing in AI capabilities that will meaningfully improve how the network is sensed, managed, and optimised — for commuters, operators, and public officers alike.

AI systems are only as good as the data that powers them. We are looking for a Senior/ Manager to establish and lead our data acquisition and partnership function — the foundational capability that will enable our organisation to develop meaningful, operationally relevant data use cases and AI-enabled applications.

Beyond internal organisational data, operationally relevant datasets may be found across government agencies, industry partners, and contractors — each governed by their own access controls, sharing frameworks, and institutional considerations. You will be required to understand our concept of operations well enough to determine what data is needed, and pursue access to that data through establishing relationships, agreements and organisational infrastructure required to bring the right data in securely and sustainably.

What You Will Be Working On

You will lead a team to translate our concept of operations into a prioritised multi-modal data acquisition roadmap, identifying what data we need and sequencing efforts by operational value and feasibility. Your work also involves stakeholder engagement, negotiating access with government agencies, statutory boards, industries and research institutions.

As part of data acquisition, you will lead your team to define and enforce standards for how data is received — covering file formats, data schemas, metadata requirements, and update cadences. This ensures that datasets from disparate sources can be reliably ingested, integrated, and made ready for analytical and AI workloads. Where partners or contractors are unable to meet these standards natively, you will work with them to find practical solutions or manage the necessary transformation processes internally.

You will also be responsible for identifying and building the right platform for consolidating data from multiple sources, particularly where contractor or sensitive datasets introduce security and classification constraints that may rule out standard environments. You will work with technical, legal, and cybersecurity colleagues to arrive at an appropriate approach.

Underpinning all of this is sound data governance — ensuring that what we acquire is handled compliantly, with appropriate agreements and access controls in place. You will work closely with analytical, AI development and product teams to ensure that acquired data is properly onboarded and ready for use case development.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Computer Science, Infocomm Technology, Engineering, or a related field, with at least 8 years of relevant experience including 3 or more years in a leadership capacity. Experience in data governance, inter-agency coordination, or data strategy is strongly preferred.

  • Prior public service experience or experience working closely with government agencies, government data security and classification frameworks will be a significant advantage.

  • You should bring demonstrated experience in negotiating data access or managing data sharing arrangements in a government or operationally complex environment.

  • Experience building or leading a team of data scientists and engineers to deliver data pipeline, warehouse and data sharing capabilities.

  • Experience in working in cross-functional teams and collaborating with both technical and non-technical stakeholders to translate operational data needs into a prioritised data strategy.

jobResponsibilities:

Operating and Optimising the Core Central Contact Centre Tech Stack (C4TS)

• You will operationalise and manage the C4TS stack — encompassing Amazon Connect telephony and Salesforce/Service Connect CRM systems — across the satellite contact centres of the Resilience Community.
• You will work with the IT team and IT vendors to manage system configuration, access provisioning, and a common knowledge base that serves as the single source of truth for consistent citizen-facing answers across agencies, ensuring stable and reliable operations at all times.

Driving AI Adoption and Automation

• You will lead the charge on AI and automation in the contact centre space — piloting AI-agent solutions for the national crisis hotline and with Crisis Management Group (CMG) Lead Ministries such as MOH.
• You will run structured technology trials encompassing fit-gap analysis, piloting, and scale-up decisions, translating emerging technologies into tangible capacity and productivity gains that enhance the government's ability to serve citizens at scale during a crisis.

Ensuring Systems Integration and Interoperability

• You will lead annual systems-integration and interoperability checks across the satellite contact centres, coordinating trunk lines with GovTech and agencies to ensure seamless end-to-end case visibility.
• You will work to ensure that shared data and case tracking are robust enough that no citizen case is dropped or delayed.

Maintaining Crisis Playbooks and Business Continuity

• You will own and continuously refine the crisis operating playbooks, activation SOPs, and ServiceSG's business-continuity plan, ensuring they remain tested, current, and actionable.
• You will run the technology-readiness components of the annual exercise, stress-testing systems and processes against real-world crisis scenarios and closing gaps identified along the way.

Managing Technology Vendors and Delivery Partners

• You will manage relationships with technology vendors and coordinate deliverables and timelines with GovTech and the internal IT team, ensuring on-time and on-specification delivery of technology solutions.

Supporting Satellite Centre Operations and Stakeholder Alignment

• You will work closely with CMG Crisis Lead Ministries to develop IVR options and knowledge management frameworks for onboarded services, and support Resilience Community members in satellite-centre systems operations.

About EDB
The Singapore Economic Development Board (EDB), a government agency under the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI), is responsible for strategies that enhance Singapore’s position as a global centre for business, innovation, and talent. We undertake investment promotion and industry development, and work with international businesses, both foreign and local, by providing information, connection to partners and access to government incentives for their investments. Our mission is to create sustainable economic growth, with vibrant business and good job opportunities for Singapore.

For more information on EDB, please visit www.edb.gov.sg

About the EDB Associate Programme
The global economy is constantly changing. Technologies are reshaping industries, businesses are rethinking where and how they invest, and competition between economies continues to intensify. For Singapore to stay ahead, we need officers who are versatile, resilient and able to make sense of these shifts to identify opportunities and translate them into meaningful outcomes.

The EDB Associate Programme (AP) is a 10-month programme designed to build the foundations of a career at EDB. Through structured training, personalised mentorship and rotations across different areas of EDB’s work, you will gain first-hand exposure to how we work with companies, industries and partners to shape Singapore’s economic future.

Work alongside colleagues in a high-performing, collaborative environment and be part of a team that cares deeply about Singapore’s success and challenges one another to do better.
jobResponsibilities:
What the Programme Entails

Your Associate journey begins with a structured bootcamp that introduces you to EDB’s mission, work and ways of working, and equips you with foundational skills.

You will then be rotated across multiple divisions. Each rotation will give you opportunities to experience new challenges and work with different colleagues and stakeholders. Through these rotations, you will gain exposure to the core areas of EDB’s work:

1) Investment Promotion – Engage directly with companies to understand their business strategies and make the case for Singapore as an investment destination. This involves building relationships with senior business leaders, analysing industry trends, structuring project proposals, and negotiating with companies on the terms of their commitments to Singapore.

What you develop: Business acumen, relationship management and an understanding of global business dynamics

2) Industry Development – Beyond individual company relationships, EDB works to strengthen our economic sectors. We do so by mapping out an industry’s ecosystem, identifying gaps in capabilities or talent, and working with companies, trade associations, and other agencies to develop strategies that make Singapore a competitive hub.

What you develop: Systems thinking, strategy formulation, partnership building and the ability to translate insights into actionable programmes or initiatives.

3) Policy and Planning – EDB charts Singapore’s long-term economic trajectory – where the economy is headed, what structural shifts are underway globally, and what that means for Singapore’s positioning. You will work on frameworks, policies and incentives that shape how EDB attracts and retains investments.

What you develop: Analytical and research capabilities, skills in policy development and evaluation, and the ability to synthesise complex information

All Associates will also undergo foreign language training, giving you an early foundation to strengthen your ability to engage businesses and partners from around the world.

ECDA’s mission is to ensure that every child has access to affordable and quality early childhood care and education.

The Child Development (CD) division in ECDA spearheads a wide range of initiatives to support the development of young children with developmental needs and young children from low-income families, to ensure that they have a good start. You will  work closely with service providers and partners to ensure that services are accessible, delivered effectively and responsive to the needs of children and families.

You will  lead the management of service providers across the programme lifecycle, including operator appointment and re-appointment, funding agreements, performance monitoring, and exit and transition planning. You will engage operators regularly to address implementation issues and follow up on programme, funding and reporting requirements.

You will monitor programme and service performance and outcomes, and analyse programme and operational data to identify service gaps, implementation issues and opportunities to refine and improve programme delivery. You will be expected to independently assess issues, develop recommendations and translate these improvements into programme and service delivery.

You will lead service planning and improvement initiatives, including exploring different ways to organise and deliver services, managing cross-programme projects, and working with external vendors where services are procured. You will also identify and drive improvements in systems and processes that support programme administration and service delivery.

You will work with service providers, SG Enable and other government and sector partners to resolve service delivery and implementation issues, coordinate referrals and service transitions, and develop practical recommendations where existing policies or processes may not adequately address emerging or complex situations.

You may also lead new initiatives or workstreams where the operating model has yet to be established, including developing the approach, engaging relevant stakeholders and translating broad objectives into implementation.

People Leadership, Team Culture & Talent Growth

The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.
Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.[TV2.1]

You will be a part of HPB’s Healthy Ageing Programme Department, which strives to help older adults to improve and maintain their functional ability through healthy lifestyle practices and increase the quality and years of healthy life. You will develop and oversee integrated communications and engagement strategies across multiple programmes, translating behavioural and programme objectives into effective communication approaches that drive participation and sustained behaviour change.

You will provide strategic recommendations to senior management and ensure that communication initiatives are prioritised, delivered and evaluated effectively across the portfolio.

You will lead the development of communication and engagement strategies across media, digital and on-ground channels, determining communication objectives, target audiences, key messages and engagement approaches based on programme priorities, audience insights and behavioural evidence.

You will also lead the planning and implementation of ground activation strategies, working with outreach teams, community partners, agencies and vendors to secure stakeholder buy-in, resources and operational support, manage implementation risks and deliver initiatives within agreed timelines and budgets.

You will oversee communications planning and resource utilisation across the portfolio, while providing direction, coaching and oversight to officers supporting communications and engagement initiatives.

jobDescription:
The OSC is a new government agency set up to support the office of the Commissioner of Online Safety (“Commissioner”) established under the Online Safety (Relief and Accountability) Act 2025 (“OSRAA”).

The OSC comprises four teams, namely Case Resolution (“CR”), Investigations (“INV”), Operations Policy (“OP”), and Specialised matters, Appeals and Reconsideration (“SAR”), with CR and INV being the OSC’s two frontline operational units, focused on assisting victims who report online harms get these removed from the internet as well as ensuring compliance with the directions issued by the Commissioner.

Reporting to the Commissioner, the Deputy Commissioner (Operations) is the senior leader responsible for the end-to-end delivery of OSC’s victim complaints operations. This appointment will directly oversee CR and INV, ensuring that OSC’s processes are fair, robust, trauma-informed, evidence-driven and consistent with the OSRAA, while building a high-performing organisation capable of responding to fast-evolving online harms.

You will translate strategic intent into operational reality: designing and refining complaint handling frameworks, overseeing and developing strategies for investigations and case outcomes, setting service standards, and building strong inter-agency and industry operating relationships to achieve effective victim relief.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic leadership and organisational set-up

  • Co-develop OSC’s multi-year operational strategy and implementation roadmap with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team, including the OSC’s operating model, resourcing plan and performance measures.
  • Establish the OSC as a trusted authority for online safety victim complaints through transparent standards, consistent decision-making and measurable service quality.
  • Establish the OSC’s as a global thought leader for online harm victim relief.

Oversee the OSC’s case resolution and investigations (core accountability)

  • Lead and partner with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in owning the end-to-end lifecycle for the reporting of online harms, including intake, triage, evidence gathering, investigations, case assessment, outcomes issuance and post-outcome follow-up.
  • Set and enforce casework quality standards (e.g., timeliness, consistency, proportionality, victim-centred practice, record-keeping and audit trails).
  • Develop investigation protocols and escalation pathways for complex, high-risk or high-impact cases (e.g., coordinated or crossfire harassment, high virality online harmful activity, involving highly vulnerable victims).
  • Drive continuous improvement using case data and trend analysis to refine triage logic, prioritisation rules and operational playbooks.

Operational policy, frameworks and controls

  • Architect and maintain OSC’s operational frameworks and internal policies to implement OSRAA effectively (including guidance, decision frameworks, standard operating procedures and training standards).
  • Ensure strong governance, risk management and internal controls across case operations (including information handling, evidentiary integrity, oversight checks and process assurance).

Stakeholder engagement and ecosystem collaboration

  • Build and sustain effective working relationships with relevant government agencies, technology platforms, app stores, industry partners and community organisations to enable timely victim relief and reduce friction in cross-entity case handling.
  • Represent OSC in operational coordination fora, driving shared protocols and clear lines of accountability during incidents and surges.

People leadership, capability building and culture

  • Build, lead and develop multidisciplinary teams (e.g., case resolution officers, investigators, operations policy officers).
  • Establish a culture of professional rigour, empathy, learning and resilience, including strong supervision practices and quality coaching for case resolution officers.
  • Put in place workforce wellbeing measures, including structured debriefs, vicarious trauma support and safe operating norms for exposure to harmful content.

Corporate leadership and organisational management

  • Provide senior oversight of operational planning and resource allocation; partner corporate functions on workforce planning, budgeting, procurement, performance management and internal communications.
  • Support external communications on OSC’s operations (where appropriate), balancing public assurance with confidentiality and operational sensitivity.
jobRequirements:
Experience and domain expertise

  • At least 10 years’ supervisory experience leading operations, investigations, trust & safety, technology policy, regulatory operations, enforcement, or complex service delivery in public or private sectors.
  • Demonstrated experience in designing and running high-volume, high-stakes casework operations with clear service standards and quality controls.
  • Familiarity with how online platforms operate (including content moderation and enforcement processes, reporting tools, recommender systems at a conceptual level, and app ecosystem dynamics). Experience with online trust & safety, public policy, or online content regulation is advantageous.

Leadership and professional competencies

  • Strong judgment and ability to lead decision-making in ambiguous, sensitive and time-critical situations.
  • Excellent stakeholder management—able to build constructive partnerships while holding firm to statutory intent, public interest outcomes and operational integrity.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to craft operational policies, decision rationales, and executive-level briefings.
  • Proven people leader who can build capability, create psychological safety, and enforce high standards of professional conduct and confidentiality.

Resilience and wellbeing

  • You may be exposed to graphic content including (but not limited to) sexual material, minor safety, suicide and self-harm, violent extremism and bullying. Resilience, sound personal coping strategies and commitment to self-care are essential. OSC will support staff through structured wellbeing practices and supervisory safeguards.

Reporting line and working relationship

  • Reports to the Commissioner.
  • Works closely with the Commissioner and other members of the OSC’s leadership team to ensure coherent end-to-end delivery under OSRAA.
  • Supervises and works with Assistant Commissioner (Case Resolution & Investigation) in overseeing the work of CR and INV.

What success looks like (first 12–18 months)

  • A well-functioning complaints and investigations operation with clear triage, service standards and quality assurance.
  • Consistent, defensible case outcomes with strong victim experience and credible stakeholder confidence.
  • A capable team with established playbooks, training pathways, and wellbeing safeguards.
  • Effective operational relationships across government and industry that improve speed and quality of victim relief.

Position will be commensurate with experience.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

Republic Polytechnic's School of Engineering (SEG), in strategic partnership with industry leader SSW Group, is seeking an ambitious full-time Research Staff (12-month contract) to engineer an industrial-scale 1"m" ^3 self-sustained passive cold storage platform under a DGF-funded initiative.

Current biopharmaceutical distribution relies on massive active energy inputs and heavy daily coolant consumption. This project completely disrupts that model by building a zero-power-in-transit, high-performance thermal container (1"m"×1"m"×1"m" ) capable of locking in sub-zero temperatures (2–8°C) for over 72 continuous hours in harsh tropical environments.

Beyond standard transport, this passive design provides critical fail-safe protection against warehouse power outages and opens up new pathways for long-haul air and sea freight to distant international markets without relying on active electrical refrigeration networks.

You will lead the hands-on engineering across two breakthrough technological pillars:
- Active-Passive "Flash-Charging" Cryogenic System: A rapid-charging base station interface utilizing specialized heat exchangers and Liquid Nitrogen (LN_2) bursts to charge high-density Phase Change Material (PCM) cores and Vacuum Insulated Panels (VIP).
- Triple-Vector IoT Telemetry Engine: An ultra-low-power, cloud-connected sensor matrix tracking real-time Temperature, Relative Humidity, and Oxygen (O_2) levels to ensure absolute data transparency and regulatory compliance (HSA/FDA standards).

The successful candidate will contribute to prototype development, laboratory research, system integration, cold box temperature analysis, field validation at mimic cold storage environment, and technology commercialisation.
jobResponsibilities:
- Perform 3D CAD modelling, understand basic fluid dynamics, and heat exchanger design to eliminate thermal dead zones and maximize LN_2 thermodynamic efficiency across a 1"m" ^3 volume.
- Design, route, and balance high-pressure LN_2 cryogenic pipelines, vacuum-jacketed tubings, manifolds, and automated valve safety systems.
- Build IOT, test, and integrate low-power microcontrollers and sensor arrays (Temp,RH,O_2) with live, cloud-based telemetry dashboards.
- Perform laboratory experiments, cold storage environment trials, temperature and humidity monitoring, passive cold storage box testing, and data analysis.
- Develop, integrate, and evaluate prototype systems, sensors, and instrumentation.
- Collaborate with industry partners to support technology validation and deployment.
- Supervise final-year project students and interns involved in the project.
- Support intellectual property (IP) development, technology transfer, and commercialisation activities.
- Prepare technical reports, journal publications, presentations, and research grant proposals.
- Manage laboratory equipment & consumables, procurement, safety compliance, and research products.
jobRequirements:
- Qualification in Mechanical Engineering, Thermal/Fluid Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Systems Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline.
- Have basic foundational understanding of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer, or cold-chain storage technologies.
- Proficiency in 3D CAD modelling (Autodesk Fusion 360 or SolidWorks) and Design for Manufacturing (DFM) principles.
- Practical skills in embedded electronics, microcontroller programming (Arduino / ESP32), and IoT sensor integration.
- Experience or have interest in cryogenic fluids (LN_2), heat exchangers, or fluid pipeline design is a major advantage.
- A hands-on, proactive mindset with the drive to build physical prototypes and lead projects independently in a dynamic lab environment.

As a Security Consultant in our Cybersecurity Governance & Assurance team, you will play an important role in safeguarding the systems and information that millions of CPF members rely on for their retirement, healthcare and housing needs.

You will contribute to strengthening CPF Board’s cybersecurity governance, risk management and assurance capabilities, helping to ensure that cybersecurity risks are effectively identified, assessed and managed. Working with stakeholders across the organisation, you will provide cybersecurity advice, conduct security assessments and assurance activities, and support the continuous improvement of the Board’s cybersecurity posture and resilience.

In this role, you will:

• Conduct cybersecurity risk assessments and security assurance activities across systems, applications, infrastructure, cloud environments and technology initiatives to identify security risks, vulnerabilities and control gaps, assess the adequacy and effectiveness of cybersecurity controls and recommend appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.
• Provide cybersecurity risk and assurance advice to system owners, project teams and other stakeholders, translating findings into practical recommendations and supporting the implementation of appropriate security controls and mitigation measures.
• Assess cybersecurity risks arising from new and emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Generative AI (GenAI), as well as new solutions and changes to existing systems across application, infrastructure, network, cloud and security architecture, and contribute to the development of appropriate security, risk management and assurance measures to strengthen resilience and support secure adoption.

• Analyse and validate penetration testing findings, assess their exploitability and cybersecurity risk, perform or coordinate retesting and validation to ensure identified security vulnerabilities are adequately addressed.
• Leverage penetration testing results together with vulnerability assessments, threat intelligence, External Attack Surface Management (EASM), Adversarial Exposure Validation (AEV) and other technical security assessments to identify systemic security weaknesses and strengthen cybersecurity assurance.
• Explore the use of scripting, automation and data analytics, including Python where appropriate, to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of cybersecurity risk assessment, assurance, monitoring and reporting activities.
• Support and participate in internal and external cybersecurity audits, reviews and regulatory assessments, including the coordination, assessment and remediation of findings.
• Assess compliance with applicable cybersecurity policies, standards, regulatory requirements and industry frameworks, and recommend improvements where necessary.
• Develop, review and enhance cybersecurity policies, standards, procedures and governance frameworks to address evolving cybersecurity risks, regulatory requirements, emerging technologies and organisational needs.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement of cybersecurity governance, risk and assurance methodologies, processes, tools and capabilities, including the adoption of threat-informed and risk-based approaches.
jobRequirements:

Cybersecurity Governance & Assurance

• Relevant experience in cybersecurity, information security, technology risk, security assurance, cybersecurity governance or related areas.
• Experience in conducting cybersecurity risk assessments, security reviews, control assessments and/or other security assurance activities, and recommending appropriate risk treatment and remediation measures.

• Good analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to evaluate cybersecurity risks and controls in the context of business, technology and operational requirements, and communicate cybersecurity risks and recommendations effectively to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Penetration Testing & Security Assessment

• Experience or knowledge in penetration testing, vulnerability assessment or security testing, including the identification, validation and assessment of security vulnerabilities.
• Good understanding of common application, infrastructure, network and cloud security vulnerabilities, attack techniques and security controls, including familiarity with frameworks and references such as the OWASP Top 10, OWASP Web Security Testing Guide (WSTG), MITRE ATT&CK and CVSS.

The Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) administers the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) framework, which enables individuals to appoint trusted persons to make decisions on their behalf should they lose mental capacity. Over the years, OPG has progressively digitalised LPA services through online submissions and integrated digital platforms. However, the LPA process continues to involve multiple manual operational touchpoints and exception-handling scenarios involving a wide network of stakeholders — including donors, donees, certificate issuers, operational officers, service providers, and partner agencies.

As OPG continues its digital transformation journey, there is an opportunity to conduct a structured review of the end-to-end LPA journey to identify process inefficiencies, manual workarounds, duplication of effort, and opportunities for automation and AI-enablement.
jobResponsibilities:
The intern will lead a comprehensive process review of the LPA end-to-end journey and develop actionable recommendations for automation and digitalisation. Key project deliverables include:

- An as-is process map documenting the full LPA journey across all stakeholder touchpoints. 
- An automation opportunity register identifying specific pain points, manual workarounds, and recommended solutions (e.g. RPA, workflow automation, AI-assisted processing).
-  A recommendations report with prioritised proposals to reduce manual effort, improve turnaround time, reduce operational errors, enhance user experience, and improve data quality and reporting capabilities.
- A presentation of findings to OPG Divisional or Senior Management at the close of the project.

- The intern will gain hands-on experience in public sector digital transformation and process re-engineering. Specific learning outcomes include practical skills in process mapping and workflow analysis, exposure to automation tools and AI applications in a government service context, experience in stakeholder engagement and requirements gathering, and an understanding of how regulatory and operational considerations shape digitalisation decisions in the public sector.

Experiential Opportunities

Beyond desktop research, the intern will have the opportunity to engage directly with OPG operations officers, attend relevant team meetings and briefings, and observe frontline service processes to develop a grounded understanding of the LPA workflow. This exposure will inform the quality and practicality of the intern's recommendations.
jobRequirements:
Disciplines: Computer Science, Information Systems, Business Analytics, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Digital Transformation, Industrial & Systems Engineering

Preferred Skills: Process mapping, data analytics, user journey design, automation tools (e.g. Power Platform, RPA, workflow automation), basic understanding of AI and Generative AI applications, stakeholder engagement and requirements gathering

Singapore is a global hub port and a leading maritime centre. To ensure that ships calling at our port do so safely, they are required to comply with port entry requirements. [What will you be working on]

Reporting to the Marine Licensing and Permits Department, which is part of the Marine Services Division, you will part of a dynamic team that is issuing licenses/permits to ensure vessels operating in Singapore meet the necessary safety standards, certifications, ethical guidelines, and regulatory requirements.

You will also be involved in formulating policies to promote the harbour craft sector, creating a pipeline of seafarers to meet the industry needs and prepare for the decarbonisation milestones of the maritime industry.

Your key responsibilities include:

1. Licensing

  • Oversee the licensing of harbour craft and pleasure craft, ensuring that vessels meet safety, manning and regulatory requirements.

  • Shape forward-looking licensing policies to modernise the harbour craft fleet and support Singapore’s maritime decarbonisation journey.

  • Manage sea space allocation for mooring buoys and develop policies to support their safe and efficient use.

2. Port clearance processes

  • Drive projects to digitalise and simplify customer-facing processes, including licensing applications, enquiries and document submissions.

  • Oversee and support 24/7 port clearance operations to ensure efficient service delivery and timely support to port users.

  • Administer and enforce port clearance requirements to maintain safe, secure and well-regulated vessel movements.

3. Industry Development & Transformation

  • Administer and enforce manpower quota policies that support the sustainable development of the harbour craft sector.

  • Review and develop manpower policies and training initiatives to attract, upskill and retain seafarers.

  • Use harbour craft industry data to identify trends, risks and opportunities that can inform policy and operational improvements.

  • Engage industry stakeholders to understand operational challenges, build support for transformation efforts and encourage the adoption of new technologies.

More importantly, you should be proactive, adaptable and motivated to learn, lead change and deliver outcomes in a fast-paced operating environment.

You should have strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the confidence to engage diverse stakeholders both in writing and in person. The Land Policy team drives planning and policy development on industrial land and space to support Singapore’s manufacturing sector and long-term economic growth. The team also oversees policy and corporate matters relating to JTC Corporation as a 5th Schedule Statutory Board.

Working closely with economic agencies, planning agencies, and industry stakeholders, you will shape policies that keep Singapore’s industrial landscape competitive, sustainable and responsive to emerging opportunities.

Drawing on rigorous data analysis and extensive stakeholder engagement, you will oversee efforts to understand economic and industrial land market trends, sharpen policy levers, and ensure that industrial land resources are deployed effectively to support Singapore’s economic priorities.

•	Leading a fundamental review of Singapore's industrial land pricing framework in close collaboration with the Ministry of Finance and sector agencies, ensuring our pricing approach remains competitive, sustainable and aligned with broader economic objectives.
•	Ensuring that there is sufficient industrial land and space to support Singapore’s medium- and long-term economic needs, including through the creation and safeguarding of industrial land, reviewing land recycling and intensification strategies, and identifying opportunities to optimise land use.
•	Working with MTI’s economic agencies and industry partners to ensure that industrial land policies continue to support emerging growth sectors, facilitate business transformation, and anchor investments that create good jobs for Singaporeans.
•	Partnering JTC Corporation on the development of innovative industrial facilities and next-generation industrial districts to support evolving manufacturing trends, enhance enterprise competitiveness, and improve productivity.
•	Monitoring developments in the industrial property market and working with JTC to ensure that land supply, pricing and rental policies remain stable, sustainable and competitive.
•	Overseeing policy, governance and corporate matters relating to JTC Corporation and its subsidiaries, including organisational development, fiscal sustainability, strategic planning and Board-related matters.
•	Representing MTI on inter-agency platforms and engaging industry stakeholders to build consensus, address emerging issues and advance policy objectives.
•	Leading and developing a team of officers, fostering a high-performing and collaborative team culture, while ensuring officers are given opportunities for growth and development.

•	Excellent communication and stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to work effectively across Government agencies, statutory boards, industry stakeholders and senior management.
•	Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to guide teams through ambiguity and drive outcomes in a dynamic environment.

•	A strong interest in Singapore’s economic development and industrial transformation.
•	Comfort working with data, economic concepts and market trends to support policy analysis and decision-making.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

jobDescription:
The household sector balance sheet provides insights on the assets and liabilities held by households in Singapore as at end of period. The current compilation workflow involves manual data extraction from multiple different sources with varying input formats and data frequency, and tedious updating of charts and tables for reporting purposes. 

This project aims to overhaul the end-to-end workflow as follows:
i) standardising the ingestion of diverse data sources,
ii) migrating the compilation process from FAME and manual handling to a Python-based workstream, and 
iii) revamping the way compiled data is presented for submission and reporting, including exploring the integration of AI for data analysis and dashboard generation.
iv) introducing automated data validation checks at the point of ingestion, e.g. outlier detection, and completeness checks.
v) Building a centralised metadata repository, e.g. capturing data definitions, update frequencies, source contacts.
vi) Automating production of narrative reports or commentary templates
vii) Documenting new workflow and running structured handover sessions for all users 
viii) Preparing presentation deck on new workflow.
jobResponsibilities: Through this project, we will develop a standardised data ingestion framework, a Python-based compilation workflow to replace existing FAME-dependent processes, and an automated reporting output or dashboard for timely data reporting. In doing so, the selected intern will gain hands-on experience in statistical data processing and compilation, and develop practical skills in Python and AI applications.
jobRequirements:

agencyDescription: The Public Sector Science and Technology Policy and Plans Office (S&TPPO) is a department under the Prime Minister’s Office and serves as the functional leader for the Science, Technology and Engineering (STE) domain in public sector. jobDescription:
As the Functional Leader for Science, Technology and Engineering (STE) in the Public Service, S&TPPO shapes Whole-of-Government (WOG) strategies to build a strong and future-ready STE workforce.

This includes understanding how the STE workforce needs to evolve, strengthening critical and emerging capabilities, developing career pathways, and building a strong pipeline of technical and enterprise leaders across the Public Service. 

The Deputy Director supports the Director in shaping and implementing these strategies at the system level. The role combines strategic workforce planning and analytics, policy development, talent and leadership development, capability and career development, and cross-agency implementation.

Working closely with PSD, ministries and public agencies, the incumbent will identify systemic workforce challenges and opportunities, develop WOG-level strategies and interventions, and translate these into practical mechanisms that strengthen the STE workforce across the Public Service.
jobResponsibilities:
Strategic Workforce Planning & Intelligence
•	Lead WOG strategic workforce planning for the Public Service STE workforce, working with agencies to understand current workforce strengths and gaps and anticipate future manpower and capability needs.
•	Analyse workforce, labour-market and organisational data to identify emerging workforce trends, systemic risks and areas requiring intervention.
•	Develop workforce scenarios, segmentation and analytical approaches to understand the future size, skills and shape of the STE workforce and inform policy and workforce decisions.
•	Develop management insights and measures to provide S&TPPO and senior leadership with an ongoing view of workforce and leadership pipeline health.
•	Translate workforce evidence and insights into practical policy recommendations and interventions at the sectoral or WOG level.

STE Talent & Leadership Strategy
•	Shape WOG strategies to build a strong pipeline of STE technical leaders, including talent identification, succession planning, leadership development, mobility and career development.
•	Maintain system-level oversight of succession health and emerging talent for critical STE leadership positions, working with agencies to identify pipeline gaps and development needs early.
•	Work with PSD and agencies to strengthen how technical leadership and potential are identified, developed and recognised within the broader Public Service leadership system.
•	Design and implement development interventions that provide emerging STE leaders with the experiences, exposure and capabilities required for senior technical and enterprise leadership roles.
•	Strengthen connections between leadership development, succession planning, career pathways and deployment opportunities across agencies.

STE Capability & Career Development
•	Develop and steward WOG frameworks for STE capabilities and competencies, ensuring that these remain relevant to evolving technology, workforce and national needs.
•	Identify critical and emerging capabilities across the STE workforce and work with agencies to address capability gaps through coordinated WOG interventions where appropriate.
•	Shape career development frameworks and pathways that support the development of deep technical expertise while enabling mobility and a range of career and leadership pathways.
•	Work with relevant partners to strengthen professional development approaches, including programmes, professional networks, accreditation or other mechanisms where these can contribute to capability development.
•	Ensure that capability, competency and career-development initiatives form a coherent workforce architecture rather than a collection of standalone programmes.

Functional Leadership & Cross-Agency Implementation
•	Strengthen the mechanisms through which S&TPPO exercises its role as STE Functional Leader and works with agencies towards common WOG workforce outcomes.
•	Work across ministries and agencies to translate WOG workforce strategies into coordinated actions, while recognising differences in agencies' missions, workforce needs and operating contexts.
•	Review and strengthen cross-agency mechanisms for building shared capabilities, including Centres of Excellence, capability clusters, workforce groups and other appropriate governance arrangements.
•	Convene and work with HR leaders, STE leaders, central agencies and other stakeholders to develop common approaches and address workforce issues that cannot be effectively resolved by individual agencies acting alone.
•	Lead cross-functional and cross-agency teams to take strategic initiatives from problem definition and policy development through to implementation and review.

•	Understand how different workforce levers, including workforce planning, capability development, talent, careers, mobility and organisational mechanisms, interact as a system.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

The Corporate Digital Applications Department (CDD) manages CPF Board's digital systems for member engagement and corporate applications. 
We are looking for a motivated and detail-oriented intern to join our SB-FRS 117 project team. The project team comprises a Project Manager and Assistant Project Manager, and is supported by both an advisory vendor and an implementation vendor. • Coordinate testing activities across multiple stakeholder groups, including finance users, the actuarial team, scheme IT teams, and vendors, working closely with the project team throughout the process.
• Support the preparation of testing data, validate test data and results, review test cases, perform testing, and track defects and errors through to resolution.
• Facilitate communication and follow-ups between the various teams involved in the testing process to ensure timely and effective resolution of issues.
• Maintain clear and accurate project documentation, including meeting minutes, test plans, test cases, defect logs, and status reports.
• Leverage AI tools where appropriate to enhance productivity and the quality of work, such as drafting documentation, analysing data, generating test cases, or summarising meeting discussions.
• Assist with other ad hoc tasks to support the broader project team as needed.

• Keen to learn and adopt new technologies, with a willingness to pick up SAP systems such as SAP PAPM or SAP Datasphere on the job.

The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

By leveraging CDA training systems and the Emergency Responders’ Fitness and Conditioning Enhancement Lab (EXCEL) facility, the Senior Responder Research Data Officer strengthens CDA’s ability to optimise training design, resource allocation, and capability development through data‑driven decision‑making.

The role must deliver solutions that meet MAS technology standards and applicable Whole of Government compliance requirements.

The role sits in a four-person delivery team set up to establish a unified investment data architecture that enables generative AI use cases. You will design and drive implementation of three unified data layers — portfolio holdings, structured market and economic data, and unstructured research, news and sell-side content — together with the reconciliation and retrieval infrastructure that supports specific use cases across the investment value chain. You will join at the start of the build phase, designing against a product vision and user stories.

Data architecture and modelling

  • Design and develop the conceptual, logical and physical data models for investment data domains: security and reference data, positions and holdings, transactions, valuations and pricing, performance, benchmarks, risk, compliance, accounting and client reporting.

Unstructured data and retrieval architecture

jobDescription:
The Fiscal Policy Directorate in MOF is responsible for formulating and implementing fiscal strategies and frameworks to optimise the allocation of finite public resources, to maintain macroeconomic stability (e.g. through countercyclical fiscal policies), support economic growth, and promote social equity. This requires making difficult trade-offs across competing strategic priorities in the social, economic, security and infrastructure domains, while considering progressivity and inter-generational equity. Our work ensures that we can balance the budget and have sufficient resources to advance Singapore’s key priorities, for the benefit of Singaporean households and businesses. 

We ensure fiscal sustainability over the medium to long term by setting out plans for our revenue (e.g. taxes, returns on investment of reserves, Government fees), financing (e.g. use of bonds), expenditure, and public sector manpower priorities. This requires close collaboration with our colleagues across MOF, as well as other Government agencies.  

We are looking for a self-driven and highly motivated individual, with an interest in working with data, to join our dynamic and collaborative team. You will have the opportunity to gain a strategic overview of the government’s priorities, manage trade-offs among competing needs, and shape the public policy agenda. You will also have the opportunity to review and operationalise our budgetary policies (e.g. Block Budgets, Programme Budgets, Reinvestment Fund, Manpower Management Framework, debt management) to support our macro-allocation objectives. As a Fiscal Policy Associate, you will be required to consult widely at all levels, synthesise and analyse information effectively, generate robust policy options and exercise sound judgment over trade-offs.
jobResponsibilities:
Key areas of work could involve the following: 

Policymaking 
1.	Formulate, review and implement fiscal, budgeting, revenue, financing, debt management and public sector manpower policies to enable optimal allocation of resources across the Government and ensure fiscal sustainability 

Strategic Planning 
2.	Horizon scanning and research of future economic and social challenges/opportunities, and study the implications for Singapore 
3.	Formulate Singapore’s fiscal strategies and response to these key challenges and seed ideas for major public policy shifts 

Managing Stakeholders and Trade-offs 
4.	Work closely with stakeholders to shape the Government’s revenue and expenditure plans and ensure alignment and coherence with the Government’s strategic priorities 
5.	Analysis of fiscal impact of major policy changes and public spending programmes and manage the trade-offs across different sectors 

Data Analytics 
6.	Analyse fiscal and macroeconomic data to sense-make the impact of fiscal policies 
7.	Model and project our revenue and expenditure over the medium to long term
jobRequirements:

•	Strong critical thinking, writing and presentation skills, as well as good numeracy skills. 
•	A background in economics, social sciences, business or the quantitative disciplines.
•	Keen interest in public policy.

[A Trade Facilitator, A Trade Regulator and A Law Enforcer]
 
Singapore Customs advances Singapore’s economic development by protecting revenue and facilitating trade for a thriving Singapore economy. · Trade Facilitator: You facilitate customs connectivity across borders for a seamless and resilient end-to-end international supply chain, and work closely with local and international partners to advance Singapore’s economy. 
· Trade Regulator: You safeguard Singapore’s reputation as a global trade hub by upholding the rules of trade and tariffs, and keeping a close watch on strategic goods and technologies to maintain an effective and robust regulatory regime. 
· Law Enforcer: You protect Singapore’s revenue by adopting a whole-of-government approach, and working closely with other enforcement agencies to enforce against revenue-related and trade offences. 
 
No matter what your role is or how you spend your time, the impact of your contributions count. 
 
[Sign-on Bonus] Eligible officers who are newly appointed to the Public Service and Singapore Customs will receive a sign-on bonus of $8,000 paid in two tranches. 
 
[Retention Bonus] You will receive attractive retention pay-outs in your 4th, 7th, and 10th in Customs scheme of service. 

[Starting Salary] ·  $4,398-$5,196*

• Promote connectivity and interoperability with overseas markets through negotiating and implementing G2G agreements such as Free Trade Agreements, DEAs and GEAs

jobDescription:
The Economist Service is the premier service for economists in the Singapore public sector. By developing a core group of professional economists, the objective of the Economist Service is to sharpen economic analysis in the public sector in order to improve public policies.

Economists in the Economist Service undertake economic research and analysis in many Ministries and agencies across the public sector. These include the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Manpower, Ministry of Social and Family Development, Ministry of Health, and Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment. Through postings to diverse Ministries and agencies, the economists contribute their expertise to inform a wide range of public policies, from economic policies to fiscal, socio-economic, health, security and infrastructural policies.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of a team of economists whose primary focus is to develop a comprehensive evidence base to support policy formulation in Singapore. Together with your team, you will strive to keep abreast of the latest economic/socio-economic issues in our public discourse, be at the forefront of the latest economic ideas and thinking, and be thought leaders on economic issues within the Singapore public sector. This will be achieved through:

(i) Identifying pertinent “hot-button”, emerging and/or longer-term economic/socio-economic issues in Singapore by conducting pre-emptive sensemaking;

(ii) Synthesising what is currently known about these issues by drawing on existing research studies and the experience of other economies to form an evidence base; and

(iii) Leading research and policy projects to provide insights on these issues within the Singapore context if there are gaps in the existing literature.
jobRequirements:
* Degree / Master’s / PhD in Economics. While a postgraduate degree will be advantageous, strong candidates with an undergraduate degree will also be considered.

* Strong quantitative skills (e.g., econometrics) for policy modelling and simulations, as well as impact evaluation studies.

* Strong passion for empirical research and extensive experience in solving complex problems using quantitative approaches.

* Proficiency with statistical/programming software (e.g., STATA, R, Python).

* Ability to distil, synthesise and explain the key insights from existing research studies and economic theory.

* Strong interest and a willingness to develop expertise in a diverse range of issues, including economic structure and growth, sustainability and resilience, labour market, internationalisation and investments, as well as productivity and innovation.

* Excellent communication skills, including an ability to express complex ideas simply and clearly.

Interested candidates should submit a copy of the latest educational certificate and transcripts from 'A' Levels or Diploma onwards, including unofficial transcripts (if any), to facilitate the processing of your application. If there are any coursework projects or thesis in Economics, please submit a copy for reference too.

agencyDescription: The Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) is the national authority that registers and is responsible for the administration of IP rights in Singapore. jobDescription:
Great ideas do not discriminate — anyone can have them. With the right protection and support, a great idea can become a trusted brand, a transformative technology, an innovative process or design, or even a song or story that inspires one’s soul.

Housing Singapore’s largest community of intellectual property (IP) experts, IPOS understands better than anyone how important it is to protect ideas and creations for now and the future. We leverage on our deep technical, legal and business expertise to help innovative enterprises grow, through their intangible assets, including IP, from Singapore, through Singapore. We catalyse the ideas today, into assets tomorrow.
 
A trade mark can be any word, name, letter, numeral, device, shape, colour, aspect of packaging, or a combination of such elements. In some cases, even sounds or holograms may qualify. From the Singapore Airlines bird logo to the DBS quatrefoil, trade marks help businesses build distinctive brands and protect their reputation. 

We are currently seeking Associate Trade Mark Examiners to join the Registry of Trade Marks. In this role, you will work closely with fellow examiners to assess trade mark applications and ensure they comply with the legal requirements for registration. You may also contribute to the formulation and implementation of national trade mark policies, supporting Singapore’s position as a global hub for intellectual property and intangible assets.

The role includes an initial structured training period of approximately 18 months, during which successful candidates will progressively develop the legal, analytical and professional judgment required for independent trade mark examination. This training combines on the job learning, with mentoring and formal instruction provided, and requires sustained commitment and dedication from the job holder.
jobResponsibilities:
Examining a trade mark application requires a combination of sound thinking, good judgment, strong analytical skills, and some understanding of, or an interest in how businesses brand, market and identify themselves.

As a Trade Mark Examiner, you will:

1.	Assess distinctiveness
Determine whether a proposed trade mark is capable of distinguishing the trade origin of the relevant goods or services.

2.	Conduct searches for conflicting marks
Identify earlier trade marks on the Singapore trade mark register that may conflict with the application.

3.	Review specifications of goods and services
Examine the description of goods and services applied for, with reference to international classification standards.

4.	Communicate examination outcomes and provide guidance

Correspond with applicants or their legal representatives on examination outcomes, including raising objections where necessary, and assessing responses received. Provide guidance and assistance to members of the public who have queries on trade mark related matters.

Beyond examination work, Trade Mark Examiners may take on administrative and project based responsibilities that support the effective functioning of the Registry and the broader objectives of IPOS.

As you gain experience and seniority, your role will broaden to include mentoring, training and supervisory responsibilities, contributing to the professional development of junior colleagues.

jobResponsibilities:
This portfolio plays a key part in delivering Enterprise Singapore's financing programmes, ensuring that enterprises and Participating Financial Institutions (PFIs) are supported with accurate, timely, and well-administered financing operations.


PFI Reporting Management

  • Verify the accuracy of monthly reports, loan data and premiums payable submitted by PFIs, ensuring figures are reconciled and discrepancies are promptly resolved.
  • Proactively follow up with PFIs to ensure timely and accurate submissions, addressing outstanding items to maintain operational integrity.

Claims Processing and Management

  • Address stakeholder enquiries relating to claims processes and guidelines, delivering clear and timely responses to facilitate smooth claims operations.

Digital Transformation and Process Improvement

  • Contribute actively to digitalisation projects aimed at improving operational efficiency and financing operations workflows.
  • Perform User Acceptance Testing (UAT) for new systems, documenting findings and providing structured feedback to ensure systems meet operational requirements.
jobRequirements:
What You'll Be Using and Applying

  • Ability to verify and reconcile financial data, identify discrepancies, and ensure the integrity of reports and claims submitted by external parties.
  • Familiarity with process transformation or system implementation, including the ability to contribute meaningfully to UAT and operational workflow improvements.
  • Proficiency in managing documentation and compliance requirements across multiple cases simultaneously, with strong attention to detail.

How We Work Together

We value individuals who demonstrate our CoRE values – collaborating effectively across teams, engaging others with respect, acting with courage to speak up and make decisions, and being enterprising in taking ownership, learning continuously, and driving outcomes in a dynamic environment.

agencyDescription:
The Civil Service College (CSC) is a statutory board under the Public Service Division, Prime Minister’s Office. We are the central learning institution for the Singapore Public Service and we partner government ministries and agencies to develop people for a first-class public service.

CSC brings together public officers from diverse backgrounds and provides them with opportunities for learning and skills upgrading. Our service-wide networks enable public officers to build capabilities, develop shared ethos and gain deeper perspectives, creating a collaborative environment for dialogue and knowledge sharing.

Through our programmes and services, CSC aims to strengthen strategic capacity in governance, leadership, public administration and management for the Singapore Public Service.
jobDescription:
About the Institute:
At the Civil Service College (CSC), the Institute of Governance and Policy (IGP) brings together learning and development (L&D) specialists and researchers to build Public Service capabilities in governance, social-economic policy, international relations, public communications and engagement, and policy tools such as evaluation behavioural insights.

What the Role Is:
As a Researcher (Economics) in IGP, you will work with senior officers to examine how the Singapore Public Service can respond to emerging challenges, strengthen institutions, and govern effectively in an increasingly complex environment. You will contribute to research on cross-cutting public policy issues and translate the resulting insights into learning experiences, programmes and resources for public officers. The role involves engagement with public sector leaders, domain experts, stakeholders, and learning professionals to shape thinking and practice across the Public Service.
jobResponsibilities:
Your role will involve:
• Conducting research on public policy and economic issues  that brings fresh perspectives, thought leadership and produces actionable insights for policy and planning officers.
• Designing and delivering learning interventions that build public sector capabilities.  Work with learning designers to translate economic research insights into learning experiences that strengthen officers' knowledge, skills and judgement. This includes developing learning resources, digital content, as well as co-designing and running learning sessions and activities.
• Collaborating with domain experts and stakeholders, including public sector leaders, agencies, external specialists, learning and development professionals and other stakeholders to sense make learning needs and gaps in Singapore's governance and policy capabilities, so that our learning interventions are developed in a relevant and timely manner.
jobRequirements:
What We Are Looking For:
• At least 3 years of experience in a policy role in Public Service. Experience in economic policy roles would be especially advantageous.
• A degree in Economics would be necessary; familiarity with quantitative research and methods would be beneficial.
• Strong interest in public policy, governance, and issues affecting the Public Service.
• Curiosity and learning agility, with the ability to translate research into effective learning content, programmes, or resources.

[Core Competencies]
• Thinking Clearly and Making Sound Judgements - Collect and analyse relevant information, evaluate options, and recommend an appropriate course of action.
• Working as One Public Service - Understand how the work contributes to whole-of-government outcomes; work across organisational boundaries; reconcile differing views; and build networks that support shared goals.
• Working Effectively with Citizens and Stakeholders - Seek feedback actively, identify unmet needs, co-create solutions that advance the common good, and communicate policy intent and processes with care and clarity.

[What you can expect]

• Growth Opportunities: We champion continuous learning - not just for the public service, but for our officers as well. We actively support our officers’ career growth through:
• Scholarship and sponsorship opportunities for higher education.
• Diverse development opportunities for officers at every career stage.
• Attachment programmes, cross-functional job rotations and gig projects.
• Coaching programmes and leadership development initiatives.
• Work Environment: We provide meaningful work, practise mutual respect and encourage innovation.
• Hybrid & Flexible Work Arrangements: We provide hybrid and flexible work arrangements to support our officers’ work-life needs. We trust that our people will deliver their best, and we strive to provide the support and flexibility they need.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. The appointment grade and actual job title will be commensurate with the candidate’s work experience.

•	The ability to manage multiple priorities and respond effectively in a fast-changing environment.
•	Strong people leadership skills with a demonstrated ability to develop teams and deliver results through others.

agencyDescription:
The Health Sciences Authority (HSA) applies medical, pharmaceutical and scientific expertise through its three professional groups, Health Products Regulation, Blood Services and Applied Sciences, to protect and advance national health and safety. For more updates on public health and safety matters, follow us on Twitter at www.twitter.com/HSAsg and LinkedIn at https://sg.linkedin.com/company/health-sciences-authority.
jobDescription:
As Deputy Director, Regulatory Intelligence & Licensing, you will lead a team of operations and policy experts to maintain operational excellence while transforming HSA into an integrated, efficient and future-ready regulator—one that anticipates risks, predicts stakeholder needs and enables innovation through intelligence-led and AI-powered regulation. Your responsibilities will include redesigning HSA’s technology systems, stakeholder journeys, internal workflows and officer roles; establishing robust policies and processes; driving continuous improvement; and maintaining high standards of service.

Through this work, you will contribute to HSA’s mission of safeguarding public health by upholding standards of quality, safety and efficacy.
jobResponsibilities:
You will oversee the following business operations:

A. Licensing and certification applications


  • Oversee the end-to-end administration of licences and certificates under the Healthcare Services Act and Health Products Act. This includes licensing public and private healthcare services and regulating health-product dealers—including manufacturers, importers and wholesalers—across all regulated product categories. Ensure the effective management of new applications, renewals and amendments, as well as cessations, revocations, rejections and cancellations, from initial screening and fee collection through processing and final approval.

  • Oversee regulatory powers relating to the refusal, suspension or revocation of licences, financial penalties and the removal of Key Appointment Holders, where applicable requirements under the HCSA, HPA or other legislation administered by HSA have not been met.

B. Enquiries, complaints and feedback processes


  • Establish and oversee a structured and transparent framework for the timely management, escalation, resolution, tracking and closure of licensing and certification enquiries, complaints and feedback from licensees, industry stakeholders and members of the public. Ensure clear accountability, high service standards and continuous improvement.

  • Work closely with Corporate Communications & Service Quality and relevant HSA departments to ensure that licensing and certification enquiries are assigned appropriately and addressed accurately, consistently and promptly.

  • Oversee the review and resolution of appeals arising from licensing and certification decisions. Engage applicants and licensees to clarify HSA’s decisions, address areas of disagreement and facilitate resolution, while ensuring that all appeals are handled fairly, consistently and in accordance with established regulatory processes.

C. Policy and regulatory framework

  • Oversee the periodic review of licensing and certification guidelines, guidance documents, circulars and codes of practice to ensure that they remain current, coherent and aligned with the HCSA, HPA and other legislation administered by HSA.

  • Ensure that licensing and certification policies, screening criteria and operating procedures are translated into clear, consistent and practical guidance for officers, applicants and licensees.

  • Work with relevant policy, legal and regulatory teams to identify gaps or ambiguities in existing requirements and recommend appropriate policy, legislative or operational changes.

2. You will prioritise and lead the sequencing of the following transformation initiatives, which may have synergies. The transformation is to take place over a 2-year period, not necessarily in a linear sequence.


A. Integrated licensing operating model


  • Design and implement an integrated operating model for licensing and certification across health products, services, professionals and information, providing stakeholders with a single point of access to HSA.

  • Redesign internal triage, routing and hand-off arrangements to direct applications and enquiries efficiently to the appropriate regulatory teams and subject-matter experts.

B. Internal workflow redesign and AI-enabled automation

  • Review and redesign licensing, certification and enquiry-management workflows to eliminate unnecessary steps, bottlenecks and ineffective hand-offs – also with a view towards harmonising workflows across products, services and professional licensing.
  • Implement interim standalone AI-tools to introduce automation, while working with the Chief Information Officer to translate redesigned workflows into a prioritised pipeline of system enhancements with agentic AI capabilities.

  • Establish appropriate outcome-based performance indicators to measure the effectiveness of redesigned workflows.

  • Scale this capability across the division without increasing headcount.


C. System design, enhancement and consolidation


  • Lead the design, implementation, continuous improvement, and governance of existing IT systems (e.g. Healthcare Application and Licensing Portal, Pharmaceutical Regulatory Information System (PRISM), Singapore Health Product Access and Regulatory E-System (SHARE), Healthcare Application and Licensing Portal (HALP) and Professional Registry System (PRS)). Consolidation may be necessary.

D. Regulatory analytics


  • Develop and deploy data- and AI-enabled regulatory-intelligence capabilities to support risk stratification, early warning, horizon scanning and the identification of emerging industry trends, technological developments and public-health threats.

  • Apply analytics to licensing, certification and enquiry-management operations to support risk-based triage, demand and workload forecasting, bottleneck detection, processing-time analysis and the identification of recurring stakeholder issues.

E. Improving stakeholder experience


  • Shift from predominantly reactive responses towards proactive regulatory guidance, including timely prompts, reminders and information tailored to stakeholders’ circumstances and regulatory obligations.

  • Simplify the discovery of licensing and certification requirements and implement AI-enabled self-service tools that help stakeholders identify relevant requirements and complete applications accurately.
jobRequirements:
• A strong commitment to public service, organisational integrity and the safeguarding of public health and safety.

  • A recognised qualification in any discipline that demonstrates analytical training and systematic thought. It is more important to demonstrate strong analytical and systems-thinking capabilities, including the ability to understand complex issues, evaluate evidence, identify risks and develop practical solutions.

  • Experience in strategic planning, policy development and/or operational management roles. These roles develop the abilities of translating broad organisational objectives into implementable plans, processes and outcomes; and balancing operational efficiency, stakeholder needs, regulatory requirements and public-interest considerations.

  • A minimum of 5 years of supervisory experience.

  • Ability to lead digital and AI-enabled transformation from a business perspective, including identifying appropriate use cases, defining operational requirements and working with technology specialists. Coding or technical-development experience is not required.

  • Strong stakeholder-management skills, with experience working directly with senior leaders, government agencies, operational teams and external stakeholders to build alignment and deliver shared outcomes.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex matters clearly, influence senior stakeholders and manage differing perspectives.

The successful candidate will be offered a 1-year contract (with option for automatic renewal for a further one year) in the first instance.


Shortlisted candidates would be contacted within 30 days from the closing date of the advertisement. We regret that only shortlisted candidates would be notified.
