agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Physical Activity Department, within the Physical Activity and Healthy Ageing Division, dedicated to making active living a cornerstone of daily life. The department works across government, healthcare, community and industry to connect residents to the right physical activity opportunities and support them in building sustainable habits. Through shared journeys, coordinated programming and trusted partnerships, it seeks to make the physical activity ecosystem simpler to navigate, more inclusive and better aligned to residents’ needs. Evidence, data insights and technology are used to guide decisions, personalise support, strengthen delivery and improve outcomes across partners.
jobResponsibilities:
As Assistant Director, Operations Excellence & Programmes (Physical Activity), you will report to the Head of Department and lead, organise and develop the team to deliver its full range of workstreams and outcomes. Your success will depend on building a capable, accountable and well-coordinated team, setting clear direction and ensuring effective execution across two equally important complementary portfolios: strengthening operational excellence across the physical activity programme landscape, and overseeing the delivery and governance of department-led physical activity programmes. Through the team, you will turn strategic direction and partnership approaches into coordinated workplans, deploy resources and ensure programmes are of high quality and delivered safely, consistently and effectively for residents.


Across both portfolios, lead the team to deliver. Set direction, organise the team around its workstreams and translate priorities into an integrated workplan. Deploy resources, assign accountable workstream leads, coach officers, review performance and manage dependencies, risks and escalation so the team delivers its collective outcomes.


Operations Excellence portfolio

Set operational governance and assurance. Establish practical standards, processes, controls and reporting across the physical activity programme landscape. Oversee quality assurance, audits, operational risks and incidents, and ensure corrective actions are completed and lessons applied.


Provide visibility of operational performance. Develop indicators, dashboards and assurance reviews that give management clear sight of operational health, service quality, control effectiveness and emerging risks, and drive timely follow-up.


Drive continuous improvement and productivity. Simplify workflows, strengthen controls and improve productivity using data, feedback and root-cause analysis. Assess suitable automation, AI and digital tools, and support teams across the organisation to adopt better ways of working.


Programmes portfolio

Oversee portfolio planning and programme delivery. Work with the department’s Strategy and R&D team to translate agreed direction into viable plans. Guide programme managers on capacity, deployment, budgets, timelines, dependencies and risk controls, and keep delivery aligned with intended outcomes and resident needs.


Maintain programme performance and governance. Oversee outcomes, participation, service quality, safety, access, budgets and vendor performance. Direct recovery actions where needed, resolve material trade-offs and hold programme managers accountable for follow-through.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for a leader who has successfully run a team to deliver multiple, interdependent workstreams. You should be able to set direction, create the conditions for strong team performance and drive outcomes through others, while connecting strategy with delivery and strengthening operations. You should bring:


  • Qualifications: A degree in Business or Operations Management, Engineering, Quality Management, Data Analytics, Economics, Public Health, Health Services Management, Exercise and Sport Science, or a related discipline. Relevant professional certification is an advantage.
  • Experience: At least 7–10 years in operations excellence and programme management, including substantial experience leading a team to deliver multiple workstreams and holding workstream leads accountable in a multi-stakeholder environment.
  • Leadership: A strong track record of building and running successful teams—setting direction, designing clear roles and accountabilities, balancing resources, developing officers and driving coordinated delivery through empowered workstream leads.
  • Capabilities: Strong skills in operational governance, process improvement, programme and vendor management, performance reporting, risk, audit and quality assurance. Able to turn data into practical decisions and improvements.
  • Attributes: A collaborative, adaptable and solutions-focused leader with strong stakeholder, facilitation, written and presentation skills. Familiarity with automation, AI or digital productivity tools is advantageous.

Successful candidates will be offered a 2-year contract.

User Experience & Product Design and Improvement

The Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA) was established in 2025 as a statutory board under Singapore's Ministry of Health (MOH) to serve as the central authority for public health policymaking to manage and control the threat of communicable diseases. This is aimed at strengthening Singapore's public health capabilities built during the COVID-19 response to ensure a unified command and coordinated approach across all situations, from routine disease control to future outbreaks.

CDA safeguards the nation from communicable diseases through disease surveillance, outbreak investigations, vaccination programs, public education, and global health collaboration. Beyond domestic activities, the CDA aims to expand Singapore’s global outreach and foster collaboration with international partners.
jobDescription:
• Senior Public Health Officer/Public Health Officer in the Clinical Advisor Office plays a pivotal role in conducting horizon scans, literature reviews, convening and supporting technical advisory committees and expert workgroups, reviewing, developing and updating or renewing of clinical guidance related to communicable diseases; assisting the Clinical Advisor Office in reviewing and providing inputs for requests relating to infectious diseases matters of national importance, in consultation with the Clinical Advisor and the Infectious Diseases Clinical Advisory Committee; assisting in developing an overarching strategy on therapeutics for infectious diseases (including novel therapeutics for pandemics); and coordinating and working with divisions in the Communicable Diseases Agency, whole-of-government ministries and agencies, and other professional bodies and societies.

• This position involves proactive needs assessment, committee facilitation, strategy development, stakeholder coordination and ensuring the currency and alignment of clinical guidance with international best practices and local healthcare priorities.

• The Senior Public Health Officer/Public Health Officer will be working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time.
jobResponsibilities:
(i) Horizon Scanning and Needs Assessment

  • Conduct proactive horizon scanning to identify emerging needs and trends in the field of communicable diseases, aligning with international best practices and local healthcare priorities.
  • Determine the requirements for new or updated clinical guidance based on the identified needs and trends, ensuring responsiveness to evolving public health challenges.
  • Conduct literature reviews to support the review and provision of inputs for requests relating to infectious diseases matters of national importance.

(ii) Committee Organisation and Facilitation


  • Convene advisory committees and expert workgroups to provide inputs on infectious diseases matters and for reviewing and developing of clinical guidance
  • Support and facilitate expert committees and workgroups for the drafting and review of clinical guidance, ensuring the inclusion of multidisciplinary expertise and stakeholder input in the clinical guidance development process.
  • Coordinate committee activities, including scheduling meetings, managing documentation, and fostering collaboration among committee members.

(iii) Clinical Guidance Development and Maintenance


  • Review, develop, and/or update clinical guidance, ensuring that they remain current, evidence-based, and aligned with international standards.

  • Coordinate the periodic review and refreshment of existing clinical guidance to reflect the latest evidence and best practices, working closely with subject matter experts and stakeholders.

(iv) Strategy Development


  • Assist to review and develop an overarching strategy on therapeutics for infectious diseases and coordinating and working with whole-of-government ministries and agencies, and other professional bodies and societies

(v) Stakeholder Engagement


  • Engage with internal and external stakeholders, including healthcare professionals, researchers, policy makers and public health experts, to gather input and insights for the development and maintenance of clinical guidance.

(vi) Documentation and Reporting


  • Maintain comprehensive documentation of clinical guidance development processes, committee activities, and guidance updates, ensuring transparency and accountability in the guidance development and maintenance process.
jobRequirements:
Qualifications and Skills

  • A degree in medicine, pharmacy, public health, biological sciences, healthcare, or a related field.
  • Relevant experience in a related field would be an advantage.

Key Competencies Required

  • Strong organisational and project management skills, with the ability to coordinate committee activities and manage guidance development processes.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and collaborate with diverse stakeholders and subject matter experts.

  • Familiarity with evidence-based medicine, clinical guidance development methodologies, and public health principles

  • Proactive and detail-oriented, with the ability to conduct thorough needs assessments and horizon scanning activities to inform clinical guidance development.

Additional Information

  • This position reports to the Assistant Director and requires a commitment to upholding the mission and values of the organisation, with a focus on advancing public health through the development and maintenance of high-quality clinical guidance related to communicable diseases.

  • As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

jobDescription:
Family Life Group (FLG), under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) strengthens and supports families through their different life stages. Our work spans policies, programmes, and public education efforts, all in service of making Singapore the best place for family life.

The Inter-Generational Support Division (IGS) sits within FLG and focuses on three areas: encouraging pre-planning through the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA); protecting the dignity and interests of vulnerable persons who lack mental capacity under the Mental Capacity Act; and supporting the resolution of maintenance disputes between parents and their children through the Tribunal for the Maintenance of Parents (TMP).
jobResponsibilities:
As an Investigation Officer in the IGS Investigation and Litigation Unit, you will play a critical role in safeguarding vulnerable persons who may lack mental capacity. You will investigate allegations of abuse, neglect, financial exploitation, and misuse of authority involving LPA Donees and court-appointed Deputies under the Mental Capacity Act (MCA). Your investigations will support enforcement and legal decisions that protect vulnerable persons and maintain public confidence in Singapore's mental capacity framework. You will:
• Conduct end-to-end investigations into alleged abuse and misconduct by LPA Donees and court-appointed Deputies, from case assessment and evidence gathering to the preparation of investigation findings and recommendations.
• Interview whistleblowers, vulnerable persons (where appropriate), witnesses, and subjects of investigation, exercising professionalism, empathy, and sound judgement.
• Gather, review, analyse, and document financial, social, medical, and other evidential materials while maintaining proper evidence management and investigative standards.
• Identify investigation risks, assess safeguarding concerns, and recommend appropriate intervention, enforcement, or legal actions
• Work closely with the IGS Litigation team in cases involving court applications, including the revocation of LPAs and deputyship orders.
• Partner with MSF's Investigation Branch and other government agencies on investigations and enforcement actions relating to offences under the MCA.
• Contribute to the enhancement of investigation methodologies, SOPs, case management systems, and risk assessment frameworks, including the adoption of digital and data-driven solutions
• Analyse investigation trends and emerging risks to strengthen operational policies, controls, and preventive measures.
jobRequirements:
• Relevant education in any discipline
• Experience in investigations, audit, compliance, enforcement, regulatory work, financial crime, fraud risk management, casework, social service, or related fields will be an advantage.
• Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to assess complex information, evaluate evidence objectively, and exercise sound judgement in reaching investigation findings and recommendations.
• Ability to plan and conduct investigations, including gathering, assessing, and documenting evidence from multiple sources in accordance with established procedures and legal requirements.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to conduct interviews, engage case parties professionally, and prepare clear, concise, and well-reasoned investigation reports
• Ability to analyse records and documents, identify inconsistencies, gaps and risks, and apply relevant legislation, policies, and procedures to investigative work.
• Ability to manage sensitive interactions with diverse stakeholders, including uncooperative or difficult parties, while maintaining professionalism, empathy, and impartiality.
• Ability to work independently, prioritise competing demands, and deliver quality outcomes within timelines.
• Strong interpersonal and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships with internal and external partners.
• Proficient in leveraging digital, data and AI tools to enhance productivity, strengthen analysis, enhance case management, and drive continuous improvement.
• Commitment to continuous learning and professional development, including keeping abreast of developments in investigation practices, legislation, technology, and AIenabled tools.

The work location is in Bishan. You will be notified whether you have been shortlisted within 4 weeks from the closing date of this job posting.

agencyDescription:
The Internal Security Department (ISD) confronts and addresses threats to Singapore’s internal security and stability. For over 75 years, ISD and its predecessor organisations have played a central role in countering threats such as those posed by foreign subversive elements, spies, racial and religious extremists, and terrorists.

At the heart of our work are the collection of intelligence that enables us to size up the threats to Singapore’s internal security, and taking the executive actions necessary to overcome those threats. Every day, we collect and analyse intelligence, make impartial assessments, and take decisive action to counter the threats to Singapore’s internal security and stability, and sovereignty.
jobDescription:
The Internal Security Department (ISD) confronts and addresses threats to Singapore’s internal security and stability. For over 75 years, ISD and its predecessor organisations have played a central role in countering threats such as those posed by foreign subversive elements, spies, racial and religious extremists, and terrorists. A fulfilling and rewarding career awaits those who want to join in ISD’s critical mission of keeping Singapore safe, secure and sovereign for all Singaporeans. 

Data is integral to ISD’s operations. As the use of data and analytics grows, having a vigorous data security and management regime becomes even more essential to enable secure data operations. You will join the Data and AI Governance unit that reports to the Chief Data Officer (CDO), where you will work together with like-minded data governance professionals and data security experts. Depending on your interests and aptitude, you will have the opportunity to learn and gain valuable experience in a broad spectrum of data-related roles, ranging from Data and AI policy formulation, security risk consultancy, data asset management and data strategy development. You will also work with cross-functional teams to offer guidance on data security, compliance and risks as we continue to leverage data, analytics and AI to bolster our operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Data Security Specialist, you will be working on one or more of the following functional roles: 
•	Conduct regular data security risk assessments across diverse business scenarios to safeguard data integrity and ensure strict confidentiality of corporate data.
•	Design and implement data security controls in systems and processes to protect sensitive information against unauthorized access or breaches.
•	Oversee user access management processes to ensure permissions for sensitive data are strictly controlled and appropriately granted.
•	Monitor ongoing data usage and activities to maintain data confidentiality and ensure alignment with established business requirements.
•	Advise cross-functional teams on IM8 and industry data security best practices and compliance standards.
•	Lead investigations and responses to data security breaches and incidents to mitigate risk and minimize operational impact.
•	Maintain and update security documentation and operating procedures to ensure continuous compliance with evolving regulations and support organizational knowledge management.
•	Monitor and evaluate emerging data security technologies for potential implementation to help optimise internal data security operation. 
•	Work across multiple functions to influence senior stakeholders, and communicate complex data security topics clearly to both technical and business audiences.
•	Support Data Governance team for the implementation of the data awareness programme (e.g. training, edm etc) to ensure ISD officers are equipped with the knowledge on proper handling of data in their daily work.
jobRequirements:
•	Degree in Information Systems, Computer Science, Data Engineering and other related disciplines, or equivalent competencies 
•	Certifications such as Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP), Certified Information Security Manager (CISM), Certified Risk and Information Security Control (CRISC), ISO 27001 etc are preferred but not mandatory.
•	A minimum of 5 years’ experience in data security, cybersecurity, data architecture, Data Governance, IT governance, IT auditor, enterprise risk management or related fields is preferred. 
•	Demonstrated experience in implementing or operationalizing data security or security tools within an organization.
•	Familiar with IM8 on data management, cybersecurity principles and processes would be an advantage. 
•	Proficient in writing and leveraging data audit and analytical tools to inform insights. 
•	Able to work across multiple functions, influencing senior stakeholders, and communicating complex data security topics clearly to both technical and business audiences.
•	Skilled in engaging, influencing, and presenting confidently to senior leaders and stakeholders to drive alignment, decisions, and sustained adoption. 
•	Applicants who are keen to build a career in data security but with no experience are welcome to apply.
•	Only Singaporeans need apply.

agencyDescription:

By working closely with our tripartite partners, industry and community stakeholders, we strive to create workforce and workplace policies that foster resilience, adaptability, and a bright future for a thriving Singapore.

Here at MOM, we are committed to creating an inclusive experience not just for our national workforce, but also for our officers who work tirelessly to champion human potential for a thriving Singapore.
jobDescription:
The Income Security Policy Division (ISPD) leads MOM’s efforts in empowering Singaporeans to plan and save for a secure retirement. Within ISPD, the Financial Planning Programme Department (FPPD) spearheads strategic communications, research, policy development, and international advocacy efforts to improve Singaporeans' financial wellbeing and retirement adequacy. FPPD also co-leads MoneySense, Singapore's national financial education programme, with the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), helping Singaporeans manage their money well and make informed financial decisions on their own.

You will drive the research agenda on financial literacy and policy reviews on retirement adequacy, lead the development of behavioural nudges to encourage positive financial planning behaviour and support international advocacy work. This includes leading the design and implementation of key surveys, analysing survey findings, undertaking deep dives to identify areas for improvement, and conducting cross-country research, landscape scans and responses to international information requests. You will also conduct research studies, including behavioural insights studies, using appropriate qualitative and quantitative methods to generate actionable insights for financial literacy initiatives, communications and partnerships and CPF policy reviews. 

You will work closely with agencies such as CPF Board and the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) to leverage synergies across research plans for financial literacy and retirement planning, including on policy communications and enhancements to their digital services. You will also facilitate collaborative data sharing with MoneySense partners and academia, as well as collaborate closely with other relevant agencies.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Lead the development of the engagement and partnership strategy with (i) government agencies to infuse financial literacy messaging at government touchpoints and digital services; and (ii) non-government entities to create awareness and encourage positive financial actions at life stages 
•	Lead the conduct of quantitative and qualitative research studies/projects of ISPD, which would include managing third-party vendors and other key stakeholders (e.g. academia)
•	Support international advocacy efforts through research and coordination of responses to international information requests on financial literacy and retirement adequacy
•	Provide data cuts and further analysis for survey findings as requested by the team or other MoneySense stakeholders
•	Prepare and present key survey findings and analysis at relevant platforms
jobRequirements:
•	Qualification in a relevant field such as Business, Data Science, Economics, Psychology, Social Science, Statistics or Public Policy
•	At least 5 years of working experience, preferably in policy research
•	Experience with quantitative, qualitative and behavioural insights research methods and analysis (e.g. surveys, focus groups)
•	Competent in analysing data, with experience in statistical analysis, data visualisation using R, Python other analytical software
•	Strong communication skills and interpersonal skills, comfortable in managing and engaging stakeholders
•	Self-driven, able to work independently and in a team
•	Advantageous to have data manipulation and visualization skills using Tableau or Power BI

Purposeful Work – Beyond being a pension fund, we are unique in being a national social security organisation, and we serve CPF members knowing that our work we make a difference.

Professional Growth – At CPF Board, you will have the opportunity to learn on the job, acquire new skills, and broaden your knowledge. Although you are joining one organisation, you will have access to many career paths in the years ahead.

jobDescription:
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) is Singapore's central bank and integrated financial regulator. MEPS+ (Central Banking & Devt Platforms Division) is responsible for the MAS Electronic Payment System — a mission-critical system supporting interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructure. MEPS+ serves the entire Singapore financial sector and requires 24/7 operational reliability, strict compliance with government regulatory frameworks, and close coordination with financial institutions and government agencies.

As System Manager, you are the operational and delivery owner for MEPS+ and related systems. You own the outcomes, and coordinate across software engineers, product owners, compliance teams, and external vendors to ensure system reliability, regulatory compliance, and successful delivery of enhancements and patches.
jobResponsibilities:
Operational Delivery & Application Portfolio Management

  • Own operational delivery outcomes for the MEPS+ application portfolio across interbank payments, government securities management, and domestic market infrastructures. Make and recommend strategic decisions on application rationalisation, consolidation, or decommissioning to optimise portfolio efficiency.
  • Coordinate release management and delivery cycles with product owners, ensuring timely and quality deployment of enhancements, patches, and security updates across major (semi-annual) and monthly patch cycles.
  • Own Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for applications under management. Review SLI and SLO performance reports produced by the SRE team, identify trends and deviations, and escalate or drive remediation as appropriate. Set requirements for monitoring coverage and alert quality; hold the SRE team accountable for outcomes.
  • Coordinate verification of monthly and quarterly system patching with the SRE team. Ensure patch outcomes are documented and meet compliance requirements.

Tech Delivery Manager Responsibilities (During Release Cycles)

  • Lead release planning and delivery activities during major enhancement releases (semi-annual). Coordinate with product owners, development teams, testing teams, and vendors to establish release scope, timelines, and deployment readiness criteria.
  • Manage release communication to all stakeholders. Provide status updates, escalate blockers, and maintain stakeholder alignment on release objectives and timelines throughout the cycle.
  • Own release governance and quality standards for MEPS+. Define the release readiness criteria and test governance framework that the Software Engineer executes against. Review and sign off on test outcomes, patch verification results, and release readiness reports before production deployment.

Incident Management

  • Own the incident management framework for MEPS+. Define and maintain incident escalation paths, SLO targets (P1, P2, P3), and communication protocols. During major incidents, lead stakeholder communication and coordinate the response — software engineers provide technical investigation and resolution support.
  • Drive root cause analysis and post-mortems following significant incidents. Own the documentation of lessons learned and track implementation of preventive measures to reduce recurrence.

Vendor Coordination & Procurement

  • Own vendor governance for outsourced components and services. Chair vendor performance reviews, monitor SLA compliance, and make escalation decisions when vendor performance falls short. Coordinate with software engineers for detailed technical review of vendor-delivered code and fixes.
  • Lead MAS's participation in procurement activities for outsourced services, including defining tender specifications, evaluating vendor proposals, and contributing to contract negotiations.

Compliance, Governance & Risk Management

  • Coordinate RFI responses across the team, ensuring accurate and timely submission of supporting documentation.
  • Plan and lead resiliency exercises including Disaster Recovery drills, manual contingency procedures, and CyberEx participation. Validate system failover and recovery capabilities. Maintain compliance with ICT Governance policies and standards specific to government financial infrastructure.
jobRequirements:
Essential Criteria

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in managing, operating, or delivering complex mission-critical systems. Minimum 3–4 years in a delivery management, operations management, or technical programme management role with clear accountability for system reliability or release outcomes. Experience with payment systems, securities settlement, or financial infrastructure is advantageous but not required.

jobTitle: Senior Researcher / Researcher (Botanical Research – Herbarium) - SBG
agencyDescription: At the National Parks Board (NParks), we take pride in conserving our natural heritage and enhancing green spaces for all to enjoy in our City in Nature. We have a multi-talented and highly passionate team that is driven by the goal to create a unique world-class living environment through excellence in biodiversity conservation, greenery and recreation, and veterinary care in partnership with the community. If you share our love for nature and animals, and our zest for innovation and continuous learning, we have the perfect working environment for you.
jobDescription:
The Singapore Botanic Gardens (SBG) is one of the world's oldest tropical botanical gardens and one of only three botanic gardens globally recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The institution undertakes a range of research including taxonomy and systematics (including phylogenomics), conservation, forest and tree ecology, as well as other programmes in horticulture and urban ecology.

The Botanical Research Branch conducts taxonomy and systematics research on Malesian flora across the Herbarium, Molecular and Micropropagation Laboratories, and Seed Bank, with particular focus on Singapore's native species and regional plant diversity alongside conservation work on key groups including Orchidaceae and Zingiberaceae. The Singapore Herbarium (SING) holds approximately 800,000 collections from Singapore and the region, with extensive holdings from Peninsular Malaysia, Borneo, and New Guinea, and is currently undergoing digitalisation. The Gardens publishes the peer-reviewed journal Gardens' Bulletin Singapore and is overseeing the writing and publication of the Flora of Singapore in parallel with a genomic flora of Singapore's native species.

This role will be primarily based in SING and undertaking research into the plant diversity of Singapore and Malesia.
jobResponsibilities:
You will be a member of the team working on research on the plant (angiosperm) diversity of Singapore and surrounding regions. We are seeking candidates with demonstrated experience and research expertise of collections-based research on plant taxonomy and systematics. The candidate’s research background should include applications of systematic theory and techniques, biogeography, understanding of morphological descriptive taxonomy and have working experience of employing modern tools for collections-based research including machine learning and/or biogeographic analysis. The candidate will be expected to develop a research programme on angiosperm groups for which Singapore Botanic Gardens has considerable holdings (e.g., Gentianales, Poales, Arecaceae), but candidates with research in other plant groups with high diversity in Southeast Asia will be considered. Opportunities for collaboration with regional partners and fieldwork will be possible and encouraged where they complement SBG's research aims. In addition, the job holder is expected to leverage modern computational tools to develop research questions and publish research outcomes from the digital dataset generated as part of the SING digitalisation programme.

Specifically, you will:

- Initiate and drive exciting research projects to understand the diversity, evolution, biogeography and classification of important tropical groups found in Singapore and surrounding regions.

- Curate and enhance the holdings in SING through fieldwork and the acquisition of specimens, as well as critical identifications following new findings.

- Make use of rich image datasets and develop innovative research questions and projects with both internal and external stakeholders and collaborators employing new computational methods.

- Analyse data, publish findings in reputable peer-reviewed journals and share findings at scientific conferences.

- Communicate and share knowledge on plant diversity, herbarium research and conservation with students and non-scientist stakeholders, through giving talks and lectures, mentoring students, publishing popular scientific articles, media interviews etc.

- Support science across Singapore Botanic Gardens and within the National Parks Board, including involvement in projects on other research programmes, involvement in workshops and working groups, etc.
jobRequirements:
- PhD in botany or related discipline with a taxonomic focus on angiosperms.

- Experience with herbarium-based research, proficiency in the statistical programming language R, Python and other statistical programming languages, evidence of working knowledge of innovative technologies to leverage data generated from specimens (e.g., ML from digital images, occurrence data etc.).

- Keen interest in the plant diversity of tropical Asia, integrative taxonomy, and a knowledge of contemporary APG classification (preferably with experience in species-rich tropical groups in Singapore and Malesia).

- Ability to formulate independent research projects with experience in scientific publishing in reputable scientific journals and drafting research proposals.

- Able to conduct field work for plant collections, including overseas travel.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong interpersonal abilities and capacity to work both independently and collaboratively in a team environment under time pressure.

- Self-motivated, organised, and open-minded, with willingness to take on roles and responsibilities to support the organisation’s functions and mission.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

Our people set us apart as we champion the development of a future-ready built environment for Singapore. Our people’s commitment to regulating building safety, leading and transforming the built environment and the industry, helps us to build a safe, high quality, sustainable and friendly built environment. 

Join us in our journey to transform the way we shape Singapore’s landscape.

Impactful: Champion an inclusive and sustainable built environment for people of all ages, abilities and needs.

Transformational: Lead the transformation of the built environment sector to deliver a safe, high quality, sustainable and friendly built environment.

Forward-Looking: Shape the landscape to prepare for the future of Singapore, rally the built environment sector to achieve far-reaching goals that reach beyond today and improve the living environment for Singaporeans from all walks of life.
jobDescription: The Building and Construction Authority (BCA) champions the development of a future ready built environment for Singapore. Besides regulating building safety, we lead and transform the built environment sector in delivering a safe, high quality, sustainable and friendly built environment. We are looking for resourceful, energetic and self-motivated individuals who are inspired to play an active role to make a difference to Singapore’s built environment.
jobResponsibilities:
• You will be part of the team that processes and approves the structural plans and calculations of the buildings submitted by Professional Engineers and Accredited Checkers.

  • You are required to perform audit checks on selected structures, conduct construction site checks and take proactive actions to prevent damages to adjacent properties.

  • You are also expected to investigate into complaints on buildings that are dangerous and assess their structural integrity and safety.

• A degree in civil and structural engineering.

jobDescription:
The Standards Division serves as Singapore's national standards body, administering the Singapore Standardisation Programme and working with over 2,600 industry experts to develop Singapore Standards that support national plans and emerging areas. The division collaborates with international bodies like ISO and IEC to ensure Singapore's standards align with global best practices.

This traineeship offers an opportunity to drive digital transformation within the Standards Division, focusing on business process redesign and system implementation. You will develop competencies in digital product management, business process analysis, change management, and user experience design. Through this role, you will gain valuable experience in translating business requirements into technical solutions and supporting organisational change initiatives in a government setting.
jobResponsibilities:
• Business Process Redesign: Lead the digitalisation of the Standards Division's processes, conducting comprehensive business process re-design to streamline standardisation programmes and document these processes for implementation.

• User Story Development: Draft detailed user stories to support ongoing digital transformation projects, ensuring that technical solutions align with business needs and user requirements.

• Change Management and Training: Prepare change management communication packages to facilitate smooth transitions and conduct user training sessions to support system onboarding across the division.
jobRequirements:
• Technical Background: Background in IT product management with demonstrated experience in user story development and agile methodologies.

• Analytical Skills: Strong analytical abilities to understand complex business processes and translate requirements into clear, actionable user stories.

• Communication and Training: Experience with change management principles and training delivery would be advantageous, along with excellent communication skills for stakeholder engagement.

jobRequirements:

The YCS Internship Programme is open to Singaporean students studying Business, Humanities, Social Sciences, Communications & New Media, Events Management or other relevant disciplines in polytechnics and recognised universities.

You may refer to the list of available internship roles at https://go.gov.sg/nycinternshipprogramme 
Please submit your application at https://go.gov.sg/nycinternship-interestform

• Knowledge in Engineering.

• Proficient in MS Office (i.e., Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, Word). Proficiency in data visualisation/ analytics tool, or robotic process automation will be an advantage.

jobTitle: Platform & SRE Engineer (Database and Search Platform)
agencyDescription:
The Centre for Strategic Infocomm Technologies is the lead digital technology agency in the Ministry of Defence, and a member of the Defence Technology Community. Our technical focus areas include Cybersecurity, Data Analytics, Software Engineering, and Cloud Infrastructure and Services. We conduct applied research and develop customised digital solutions to support national missions such as cyber defence and counter-terrorism.

jobDescription:
We are seeking experienced Platform & SRE engineer to design, develop, and maintain our large-scale database and search infrastructure. The ideal candidate will have a strong background in date base systems, search technologies and software engineering.

The Engineer will be responsible for ensuring the scalability, performance, and reliability of our database and search systems, developing new features and evaluations of new technologies to support our growing user base.
jobResponsibilities:
• Build and maintain high-available, scalable large-scale databases and search platforms using techonologies like PostgreSQL and Elasticsearch
• Design and implement data integration and migration pipelines to ingest data from various data integration points including APIs, files, and/or other databases
• Improve platform availability and performance through use of SRE practices
• Conduct incident managment, including troubleshooting, resolution and post-mortem of the database and search platforms
• Provide technical guidance and mentorship to fellow engineers as a subject matter expert in database and search platform engineering
• Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including projects, engineering, and operations to ensure platform and product usability and alignment to organisation goals
jobRequirements:
• A degree or professional qualification in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or related fields
• 3+ years of experience with database systems, including relational databases (e.g. PostgreSQL, Oracle) and/or NoSQL databases (e.g. MongoDB, Elasticsearch)
• Proficiency in programming languages, including Bash, Go, Java, Python
• Experience in cloud-native technologies for container orchestrations, CI/CD, infrastructure automations and observability
• Experience with data modelling, schema design, performance tuning and data migration

Nice to Have
• Experience in managing physical and virtual infrastructures
• Experience in managing cloud database and search services using AWS RDS, Google Cloud SQL, or Azure Database Services
• Passion for open-source technologies

Why join us?
• The work is purposeful and meaningful 
• You will work with the best engineers 
• We work with modern technologies and tech stacks 
• We have excellent engineering culture and work-life balance 
• We aspire to engineering and operational excellence 
• We empower to innovate 
• We grow together as a family

agencyDescription: MAS is the central bank of Singapore. Our mission is to promote sustained non-inflationary economic growth, and a sound and progressive financial centre.
jobDescription:
MAS’ Data Analytics & Engineering Division (DAE) is a specialised team within the Data Technology and Architecture (DTA) Department within the Technology Group (TG) in MAS.

DAE’s primary purpose is to partner internal MAS functions to generate business value through the enablement of effective and efficient use of data driven insights for business value creation. This is achieved through effective strategies, strong in-house development capability, standardization of processes, tooling enablement, establishing a product development mindset, promoting knowledge sharing within MAS and complementary external collaborations.
jobResponsibilities:
As a DAE Product Manager, you will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and needs of stakeholders, as well as the agility to respond to changes and developments.

  • Day 2 Operations & Support

    • Hands-on operational management of production systems, log analysis, and incident response while maintaining deep technical understanding of system components

    • Oversee RCA for incidents and service degradations, identifying systemic issues and proposing cross-functional improvements beyond immediate scope

    • Proactive system optimisation through continuous monitoring, identifying performance bottlenecks, and recommending architectural or process enhancements to prevent future issues

    • Manage and troubleshoot technical components with sound judgment, escalating complex problems while suggesting preventive measures and long-term solutions

    • Establish, maintain, and continuously improve SOPs, incorporating lessons learnt and industry best practices to enhance operational efficiency

    • Manage SLA/SLO compliance, performing regular logs/accounts reviews, and implementing corrective actions when thresholds are breached

    • Identify operational gaps and collaborate with development teams, infrastructure teams, and business stakeholders to remediate systemic inefficiencies

    • Lead post-incident reviews and translate findings into actionable improvement initiatives across technology and process domains

  • Product Lifecycle & Development Management

    • Lead end-to-end product lifecycle management, from conceptualisation to launch and ongoing operational excellence, ensuring product relevance and value throughout its lifetime

    • Manage product development using Agile methodologies, facilitating ceremonies, and analysing project metrics to ensure successful delivery

    • Oversee project management activities, including risk assessment, resource allocation, and adherence to quality and security standards

    • Balance feature development with operational stability, making informed trade-off decisions between new capabilities and system reliability

    • Oversee ICT Governance audits and reviews to maintain adherence to best practices
jobRequirements:
• Essential Day 2 Operations & Support Experience:

    • Minimum 8-10 years of hands-on Day 2 operations experience managing Data Science platforms, analytics infrastructure, or similar technology systems in production environments

    • Proven track record of conducting RCA and implementing both immediate fixes and strategic improvements that extend beyond assigned scope

    • Demonstrated ability to identify systemic issues during routine operations and proactively propose cross-functional solutions involving multiple teams or departments

    • Experience in creating, executing, and evolving SOPs based on operational learnings, not just maintaining static procedures

    • Strong technical troubleshooting skills with the ability to dive deep into logs, metrics, and system behaviours to diagnose complex issues

    • Experience managing SLA/SLO compliance, incident management, and translating operational metrics into improvement initiatives

    • Proven ability to balance tactical operational execution with strategic thinking, suggesting improvements to architecture, processes, and tooling

    • Experience with observability tools, monitoring platforms, and automation frameworks

  • Product Management & Technical Skills:

    • Experience in product management with understanding of full product lifecycle, particularly post-launch operational phases

    • Strong understanding of Agile methodologies and project management principles, with emphasis on DevOps and SRE practices

    • Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex business requirements into actionable product features and operational requirements

    • Strong understanding of ICT governance frameworks and best practices within financial services environment

  • Collaboration & Communication:

    • Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills, with ability to advocate for operational improvements and influence decisions across various levels of the organisation

    • Demonstrated experience collaborating with development, infrastructure, security, and business teams to implement holistic improvements

    • Experience in creating and maintaining technical documentation, runbooks, and knowledge bases that evolve with system changes

    • Ability to work collaboratively in a team environment, mentor junior operations staff, and manage multiple priorities

  • Preferred Qualifications:

    • ITIL Expert/Master certification

    • PMP and CSM/CSPO certification

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, you may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo further assessment.

This is a 2-year contract. All applicants will be notified on whether they are shortlisted or not within 4 weeks of the closing date of this job posting.

At MND, we aspire to create a quality, vibrant and sustainable living environment for our people. We also strive to shape Singapore into a world-class city of knowledge, culture and excellence – one which keeps pace with global challenges and the rising aspirations of Singaporeans.

Our Vision:

An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City
MND's vision reflects our growing emphasis not just on physical infrastructure, but also on the softer aspects of creating emotional attachment in our people, the global talents and corporations whom we attract here. At the same time, it articulates MND's goal of building upon Singapore’s unique distinguishing characteristics to develop Singapore as a global city of knowledge, culture and excellence.


Our Mission:

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
MND will provide quality physical infrastructure for the nation by working with our partners in the public and private sectors.

Create a Vibrant, Resilient and Sustainable Living Environment
MND will strive to make Singapore a livelier and more exciting city, and ensure our nation is well-prepared to face the growing uncertainties and complexities. MND will also maintain the quality and resilience of our built and natural environment to ensure high standards of living, and carry out development that meets the needs of the present without compromising that of future generations.

Provide Affordable and Accessible Public Housing
MND will commit to support Singaporeans' homeownership aspirations and ensure public housing remains affordable and accessible.

Build Rooted and Cohesive Communities
MND will strive to foster our citizens' attachment and love for our homeland and maintain social cohesiveness in our communities, even as Singapore continues to be an open and globalised society.

agencyDescription:
The Ministry of Health’s (MOH) vision is to champion a healthy nation with our people – to live well, live long and with peace of mind. As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobResponsibilities:
You will:

1.	Review Care Transformation (CT) priorities and care model innovation to inform Singapore’s healthcare transformation strategy. This includes reviewing major care model innovations and pilots across MOH, Clusters, community care providers and MOH Office for Healthcare Transformation (MOHT). 

2.	Assess and support mainstreaming of successful pilots to encourage sector-wide adoption. This includes working through financing, regulatory and IT enablers with relevant stakeholders in support of national-level CT efforts.

3.	Drive and oversee Clusters’ efforts and commitment towards meeting national CT targets. Work with Clusters to implement the CT agenda required to close remaining gaps.

4.	Drive and oversee capacity planning for the public healthcare system, over both medium- and long-term horizons, factoring in the impact of CT, care integration and inter-dependencies across settings when assessing healthcare demand at the national and regional level.

5.	Review and refine our capacity monitoring capabilities and frameworks at the public healthcare system level, beyond individual settings, to identify system-level bottlenecks and develop relevant solutions to address system-wide challenges.
jobRequirements:
• A degree in healthcare management, public health, health analytics, or a related field.
• Experience in strategic planning, service capacity analysis, or related areas is preferred.
• Proficiency in analysing and interpreting datasets to identify trends and develop actionable insights.
• Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills to collaborate effectively with diverse teams.
• Ability to manage projects and coordinate efforts across multiple internal and external stakeholders.

Key Competencies Required:
• Thinking Clearly & Making Sound Judgements – Strong analytical and critical thinking abilities to support the crafting of
sound policy recommendations; ability to grasp timelines, operating context and ground realities.
• Learning & Putting Skills into Action – Possesses the drive and curiosity to learn and apply new skills, knowledge and
new ways of working.
• Improving & Innovating – Ability to seek continual improvements, and to innovate and experiment while managing the
risks involved.
• Working Effectively with Stakeholders – Ability to mobilise and rally partners and stakeholders towards a collective
purpose.

As part of the shortlisting process for this role, candidates may be required to complete a medical declaration and/or undergo
further assessment.

We collect, compile, analyse and disseminate a wide range of economic, business, household and population data, as well as analyse and monitor trends in the economy and population.

jobTitle: Senior/Assistant Director, Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division
agency: Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry
agencyDescription:
Working at METI places you at the heart of Singapore’s economic policy-making. We drive productivity-led growth, safeguard and expand our economic space, and build a future-ready economy where firms can thrive. Together, we create a Singapore which is a city of possibilities, a home to great firms, and a place where the world connects — with people at its heart.

When you join METI, you contribute to our mission of creating good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans, enabling them to improve their lives and secure a better future.
jobDescription:
With the shifts in the global order and deepening geopolitical tensions, we live in a world which is less predictable and secure. In recent years, global supply chains are increasingly being scrutinised for their ability to withstand shocks. Countries are reconfiguring trade networks and supply chains in the name of resilience and security. As a small and open economy with limited natural resources, Singapore needs to be prepared and reacts nimbly in the face of such changes . 

The Supply Chain and Economic Resilience Division (SCERD) is responsible for ensuring economic resilience and the resilience of Singapore’s critical supply chains. SCERD also oversees building and institutionalising resilience, operational preparedness and crisis management capabilities in the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

jobDescription:
Rehabilitation & Social Mobility (RSM) Policy Directorate develops policies and programmes which:
a)	Deliver stability, self-reliance and social mobility for lower income families
b)	Protect individuals and families from abuse and neglect or problem gambling
c)	Rehabilitate individuals from social dysfunction.

Family Intervention Division develop and review policies which enhance intervention, stability and resilience of youth-at-risk and vulnerable families (including those with problem gamblers).
jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of a team of officers who will be working with other Ministries and Divisions within MSF and our stakeholders to formulate and conceptualise comprehensive family service policies and programmes. In particular, your work on family services targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families and individuals will focus on designing systems and policies that intervene upstream and downstream to influence family functioning, reduce risk and strengthen protective factors. 

Your responsibilities as a Assistant Director (Family Intervention) will include:
•	Collaborate with external stakeholders and partners across Ministries and Divisions to formulate, implement and evaluate family service policies targeting moderate-to-high-risk vulnerable families.
•	Work closely with policy, operations and practice divisions within MSF to ensure seamless integration between policy development, service delivery and frontline practice, facilitating regular coordination and alignment across different functional areas.
•	Conceptualise and design upstream and downstream intervention systems that influence family functioning, reduce risk factors and strengthen protective factors.
•	Conduct policy research and analysis to inform evidence-based approaches to family service delivery and intervention strategies.
•	Plan and carry out stakeholder engagement activities with partners, service providers and other stakeholders/beneficiary groups to ensure responsive policy development.
•	Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of family service policies and programmes, using data analysis to inform continuous improvement and refinement.
•	[If given supervisory responsibilities] Lead a team of officers to carry out the above responsibilities.
jobRequirements:
Competencies required:
•	[Policy Development & Analysis] Formulate comprehensive policies by analysing complex social issues, evaluating evidence, and developing frameworks that address the needs of vulnerable families while considering implementation feasibility.
•	[Cross-Agency Collaboration] Build and maintain effective partnerships across government divisions, external agencies and community stakeholders to ensure coordinated policy development and service delivery.
•	[Programme Design & Implementation] Conceptualise and design family service programmes from inception to implementation, ensuring alignment between policy objectives and operational delivery mechanisms.
•	[Stakeholder Engagement] Develop and execute engagement strategies with families, service providers, and community partners to inform policy development and ensure responsive service design.

To be successful in this role, you must have/be:

•	Strong collaborative skills and teams ethos to work effectively across multiple divisions

jobDescription:
READY TO DIG DEEPER THAN HEADLINES?

Love connecting dots that others miss? Fascinated by issues and developments that affect Singapore? At Security and Intelligence Division (SID), we’re on a mission to protect Singapore in an increasingly unpredictable world. 

As a Target Analyst, you will conduct deep investigations into entities and networks to identify emerging threats and operational opportunities on issues and developments that shape national interests. You will use multi-source intelligence and data analytics to synthesise information into actionable insights that drive high-stakes decisions. Translation? You won't just be reading news tickers. You'll be uncovering the stories hidden beneath the surface. It's part detective work, part strategy play, and 100% real-world impact. In this role, your analysis protects Singaporeans and safeguards our national interests.

Whether you're a fresh graduate hungry to master specialised analytical tradecraft or a mid-career professional looking to pivot for a greater purpose, this is your chance to contribute to Singapore’s national interests.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Integrate Fragmented Data: Combine data from diverse sources— OSINT, technical metadata, and specialised feeds
•	Separate Signal from Noise: Filter through large volumes of messy, conflicting information by asking the right questions, and discerning the relevant picture from unrelated noise
•	Map Networks: Map out complex networks of entities and operational infrastructures, and create clear pictures from a large web of disparate clues
•	Tell the Story Behind the Data: Translate complex technical data and convoluted investigative trails into clear and concise executive briefs to provide early warning and strategic support for Singapore's policymakers
•	Build & Innovate: Develop new investigative tools, and refine analytical workflows to keep our team ahead of emerging risks

What you will gain
•	Unmatched Purpose: Contribute directly to the safety, stability, and sovereignty of Singapore
•	Culture of Continuous Learning: We invest heavily in professional training, including advanced OSINT, data analytics, foreign languages, and cutting-edge investigative methods
•	High-Calibre Teams: Work alongside passionate, like-minded analysts, data experts, and domain experts who love what they do
jobRequirements:
•	Singapore Citizens only

We are looking for individuals with an investigative mindset who are able to find clarity in ambiguity and turn fragmented data into clear answers. You would possess the creativity to:
•	Hunt for missing pieces: Develop mastery of the information landscape and know where to find additional data sources when the current picture is incomplete
•	Slice and dice data: Approach data with clear questions to ensure your analysis is relevant, looking for patterns that others miss
•	Connect the dots: Turn disjointed or weak signals into a coherent narrative of “how things fit together”

We will provide the tradecraft training; you bring the curiosity. Your job isn’t to know all the answers today, but to have the drive to uncover them. Desired qualities and attributes include:
•	Keen interest in geopolitical, threat or security-related developments
•	Strong investigative, analytical, and problem-solving skills
•	Willingness to apply new tools and technologies to derive insights from information
•	Interest in mastering a foreign language and culture
•	Both detail-oriented and able to zoom out to see the big picture
•	Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
•	Strong communication skills
•	Motivated team player and an independent self-starter

We actively welcome candidates from adjacent backgrounds such as (but not limited to):
•	Geopolitical Risk Researchers: Analysts skilled in open-source research (OSINT), digital forensics, or regional threat monitoring
•	Trust & Safety / Risk Operations: Investigators who identify bad actors, coordinated abuse, or platform manipulation at scale
•	Cyber Threat Intelligence (CTI): Analysts who track threat actors, malware campaigns, or digital indicators
•	Financial Crime & Fraud Investigations: Specialists who follow paper trails, map suspicious transactions, and uncover hidden entity relationships

Beyond these professions, candidates with the following foundational skills will hit the ground running:
•	Investigative & OSINT Methodologies: Advanced search techniques, digital footprinting, domain/IP pivoting, social network analysis, and online investigation frameworks
•	Link Analysis & Visualisation: Practical experience with network visualization platforms (e.g., graph analysis tools)
•	Domain Expertise: Familiarity with regional or international geopolitical, threat or security issues
•	Language Expertise: Mastery of a foreign language

We hire at various levels. Junior analysts focus on execution and tradecraft mastery, while experienced hires will lead complex investigations and mentor teams.

Requirements:

9.	Drafting and vetting minutes of meetings and policy papers for decision/approval.

Advance the data-driven, evidence-based and citizen-centric approach to health promotion through state-of-the-art data best practices to maximize data quality and internationally-recognised governance and policies to promote safe usage of data.

Overview of Data Operations & Architecture Department

Recognising the efficacy of big data and artificial intelligence in optimising sharper insights and outcomes for public health, the Data Operations and Architecture Department will take a proactive role to drive the design of a 360-view citizen-centric data architecture and the implementation of data operations to support and facilitate an evidence-based, data-driven approach to programme delivery. The department will also be involved in strategic collaborations with partners (e.g. public healthcare and data science institutions, academics and technology players) to bring in their data and expertise onto the data operations to benefit citizens.

You will be pivotal in helping to set up and implement a robust data engineering pipeline that can integrate the vast wealth of data HPB has through its numerous data sources. A robust data pipeline ensures that changes from the data sources does not impact the timely delivery of high quality data to our business users.

Given the diversity of data collected from our lifestyle programmes, data science approaches such as machine learning will also be deployed to support the data engineering process. For example, we have build and included machine learning ops to help with standardising event names.

  • Design optimal data structures for strategic datasets and drive data engineering processes related to data ingestion, data imputation, data transformation and integration to facilitate data science and analytics use cases

• Central Administration: Ensure effective and efficient use of resources and help develop a consultative and customer-centric Public Service.

• Central gateway for mid-career entrants to apply for Leadership Programmes in the Public Service
- Candidates may be considered for the PSLP Sectoral Phase (SP) or the Administrative Service (AS), where they would be supported in deepening their competencies either within a sector (PSLP SP) or across 2-3 sectors (AS).

- Candidates can apply without needing to choose to join the AS/PSLP or any specific government agencies. Successful candidates will be placed onto the appropriate leadership programme, where their past work experiences will be taken into account when curating relevant postings / developmental opportunities, based on the assessed calibre, readiness and seniority.

- The AS aims to develop multi-sectoral leaders with whole-of-government perspectives and capabilities, to formulate and implement policies that will improve the lives of Singaporeans. The career path of the AS can be found here.

- The PSLP aims to develop sectoral leaders for key leadership positions within the Public Service. There are 2 phases in this talent development programme. You will go through structured rotations during the General Phase to explore and gain experience in at least two different sectors of the Public Service, while at the Sectoral Phase, you will focus your development within a sector, building deeper competencies and networks. The career path of the PSLP can be found here.

• Structured job placement and onboarding support to support mid-career officers’ transition to the Public Service 

- For their first one or two postings, officers on the MCLT will select from a list of curated jobs that provides developmental exposure while having adjacencies to their previous work experience. This allows officers to leverage their expertise and experiences in making substantive contributions, while supporting their learning and transition into the Public Service. Officers can look forward to a meaningful career journey across a variety of postings such as job roles in policy-operations as well as stakeholder mobilisation and engagement, which will tap on officers’ knowledge, skills and perspectives. 

- A tailored onboarding experience with structured and personalised onboarding process to support officers’ transition on the MCLT. This is especially for working professions without any prior experience working in the Public Service.

You can apply for the MCLT by clicking on the "Apply" button. 

For more information on the PSLC, please visit https://www.psd.gov.sg/leadership/public-service-leadership-careers for further clarification.

jobDescription:
The Fair Consideration Framework sets out requirements for employers to consider the workforce in Singapore fairly for job opportunities. Employers are expected to adhere to the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices, to recruit and select employees on the basis of merit, and not discriminate on characteristics that are not related to the job, such as age, gender, nationality or race.

The upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation (WFL) will strengthen protections against discrimination and help ensure that workers are fairly considered for job opportunities. 
As an Investigation Officer, you are primarily responsible for investigating companies’ and individuals’ possible non-adherence of the Tripartite Guidelines on Fair Employment Practices (as well as the upcoming WFL when it is implemented) and recommending the appropriate actions to be taken against errant employers.
jobResponsibilities:

•	Assist with the formulation and review of operational policies, processes and communication strategies, including for the upcoming WFL.

5) Incident Responder
You will monitor our environment and investigate suspicious activities on our systems. This includes optimising the detection rules of our security platforms to ensure that our security operations are effective and sustainable.

6) Penetration Tester
You will conduct tests using a variety of tools to discover vulnerabilities in our systems and networks. You will also run incident management exercises to put our incident response readiness to the test.

agencyDescription:
Working at METI places you at the heart of Singapore’s economic policy-making. We drive productivity-led growth, safeguard and expand our economic space, and build a future-ready economy where firms can thrive. Together, we create a Singapore which is a city of possibilities, a home to great firms, and a place where the world connects — with people at its heart.

When you join METI, you contribute to our mission of creating good jobs and opportunities for Singaporeans, enabling them to improve their lives and secure a better future.
jobDescription:
METI’s Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division plays a key role in creating an energy system that is secure, resilient, cost-competitive, and ready to transition to a low carbon future. Our work keeps the lights on today, and builds the power system for tomorrow. 

Energy is an existential issue for Singapore. We import almost all our energy supply and are exposed to global energy market movements. Recent energy crises due to the war in Ukraine and ongoing conflict in the Middle East have upended the global energy ecosystem. The climate crisis compels all countries to accelerate their pace of decarbonisation, even as they struggle with energy costs and unpredictable supply chain shocks. At the same time, our energy system is an enabler for economic growth, as speed to power is critical to capture strategic and economically significant investments.

Amidst this backdrop, Singapore needs a stable, reliable, and cost-competitive energy system that safeguards our economic competitiveness and dynamism.
jobResponsibilities:
METI’s Energy and Carbon (E&C) Cluster leads initiatives to reduce emissions and drive the transition to a low-carbon economy, while ensuring energy security and cost-competitiveness, and enabling Singapore to sustain economic growth. Officers in this cluster develop energy and carbon markets, plan energy infrastructure, build Singapore’s capabilities to harness low-carbon energy sources, and manage emission trajectories and carbon budgets. You will collaborate with stakeholders across Government, industry, and international partners to support sustainable economic transformation and green growth through strategic planning, policy analysis, and partnerships.

The Energy Markets and Infrastructure Division within the E&C Cluster takes the lead in ensuring energy remains a key enabler of Singapore’s competitiveness, climate goals and national resilience via the five ‘Cs’: 

•	Confidence. Ensure our system resilience continues to be a source of confidence for our people, through multiple lines of defence to safeguard energy security, resilience, and reliability. These include diversifying our fuel sources and strengthening our fuel reserves.
•	Competitiveness. Harness energy to bolster our economic competitiveness, through scaling our generation and grid capacity to meet growing needs and attract electricity-intensive investments. This also involves reviewing our energy system planning models and leveraging flexibility assets to secure speed to power while maintaining system reliability. 
•	Carbon. Ensure our power system infrastructure and electricity market are ready for a low-carbon future to meet our climate commitments. Infrastructure and markets are critical to ensuring Singapore can pursue every possible pathway to develop a diversified and affordable portfolio of low-carbon energy options.
•	Connectivity. Deepen connectivity with our partners and ensure new imported energy sources can enter Singapore’s grid and electricity market. 
•	Costs. Keep costs in check to ensure we strike the right balance in the energy transition. This involves right-pricing energy and infrastructure, and ensuring our market frameworks continue to support a competitive and commercially sustainable generation sector.

Your responsibilities include one or more of the following workstreams: 
•	Formulate robust strategies and policies to regulate and develop the gas and electricity sectors. This involves working with key stakeholders to develop and implement regulatory and market structures, to strike a balance among our objectives of economic competitiveness, energy security and environmental sustainability. 
•	Formulate and review strategies and policies to enhance our energy security by diversifying Singapore’s energy sources, including those for electricity and gas imports. 
•	Formulate and review policies and strategies to develop supporting enablers for the electricity and gas sectors, including infrastructure and financing. 
•	Develop and implement communications and engagement plans to support electricity and gas market changes. 
•	Monitor developments in global energy markets and analyse implications for domestic energy policies.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for driven and capable individuals who thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, have a keen interest in energy markets and policies, are adept at working with multiple stakeholders within and outside the public sector, and are equipped with the following qualities and competencies:

•	0 to 6 years of relevant experience in policy, sustainability and energy-related fields 
•	Ability to pick up new content areas quickly, and assimilate knowledge from a wide variety of sources to provide policy recommendations 
•	Comfortable working with a wide range of stakeholders, both within and beyond the public service, which requires strong interpersonal, organisational and communication skills 
•	Ability to work well both independently and as part of a team 
•	Driven, meticulous and resourceful

The climate crisis requires us to quickly transition to low-carbon energy sources to avoid the devastating impact of rising temperatures. Decarbonising our power sector, which contributes 40% of current emissions, is key to realising Singapore’s commitment to achieving net zero emissions by 2050.

Even as we take steps to secure a low-carbon energy supply, we will also need to safeguard our energy security and affordability. Navigating the energy trilemma successfully will be one of the defining policy challenges of our generation and hold far-reaching implications for our economy and society.

1)	Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (EFMA);
2)	Employment Agencies Act (EAA);
3)	Foreign Employees Dormitories Act (FEDA); and
4)	Prevention of Human Trafficking Act (PHTA).

Through investigations, you play a key role in upholding in maintaining a high level of compliance to MOM’s work pass framework and protecting the basic interests of the migrant workers. An Endearing Home, A Distinctive Global City

Develop World-Class Infrastructure
