jobResponsibilities:
As a BA/Senior BA, you will be embedded in a product team and play a central role in bridging business needs with technical delivery. Your responsibilities will include:

a)	Requirements and Process Design: You will gather, analyse, and document business requirements through workshops, interviews, and stakeholder engagements. This includes developing a thorough understanding of existing "as-is" workflows to identify inefficiencies and co-designing optimised "to-be" processes. You will translate these requirements into clear user stories and acceptance criteria that keep product development aligned with business objectives.

b)	Stakeholder and Vendor Management: You will serve as the primary liaison between non-technical business stakeholders (including senior management), IT engineering teams, and third-party vendors. This involves facilitating decision-making, managing competing priorities, communicating trade-offs clearly, and proposing practical implementation options.

c)	Testing and Quality Assurance: You will define test cases, coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT), validate system outputs, and manage defect resolution in close collaboration with the technical team.

As an integral member of a product team, you will also:
•	Provide timely input and clarifications to the development team before and during sprints to ensure shared understanding of requirements, and verify that completed features meet business intent
•	Work with users to develop test scenarios and support UAT
•	Support product showcases to management and channel continuous feedback from business stakeholders back to the development team
•	Monitor post-production performance and track customer feedback to inform product iterations
•	Lead After Action Reviews to surface learning points, identify issues, and drive corrective actions
jobRequirements:
•	At least 4 years of relevant experience across the following areas:

a)	Requirements Gathering — Experience eliciting, analysing, and documenting business and functional requirements using techniques such as interviews, workshops, and surveys.

b)	Stakeholder Management — Demonstrated ability to liaise between non-technical stakeholders, engineering teams, and vendors; facilitate decision-making; manage expectations; and communicate complex ideas to diverse audiences.

c)	Process Improvement — Experience in business process modelling, analysis, and re-engineering, including applying process improvement methodologies to design optimised workflows in the context of system enhancements.

d)	Testing and Quality Assurance — Experience defining test cases, coordinating UAT, validating system outputs, and managing defect resolution with technical teams.

e)	Experience working with Large Language Models (LLMs) would be advantageous - Demonstrated understanding of how to integrate, govern, and prompt LLMs in a product or delivery context. This includes the ability to translate business problems into AI-ready requirements, and to design effective prompts that generate user stories, surface insights, or automate workflows.

•	Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences and vice versa. You should be comfortable with making informed decisions on product direction and feature prioritisation, including pushing back on requests where necessary with clear and reasoned justification.

•	Strong analytical skills — able to break down complex problems, identify patterns, and draw meaningful conclusions from diverse data sources — and ability to quickly pick up new domains, technologies, and methodologies as business needs evolve.

This will include working with partners to develop and operationalise meaningful volunteer opportunities that enable seniors to conduct community-based AAPs across Active Ageing Centres (AACs) nationwide, and progressively building capability of AACs to independently design, implement and sustain physical activity initiatives of their own.

You will support the development of practical training curriculum, learning resources and implementation guides for senior volunteers to be equipped with the skills and confidence to support volunteer-led low-barrier physical activities like brisk walking activities and simple exercise workouts. You will also work with partners to identify future capability needs and implementation models that would enable AACs to independently recruit, train and deploy volunteer-led physical activity programmes.

You will contribute to capability development efforts by translating policy intent into practical and meaningful volunteer opportunities in the community, whilst enabling AACs and community partners with capabilities to independently design and sustain physical activity initiatives. Through this, you will support HPB’s mission to extend healthy life years through national directives under Age Well SG and Healthier SG, enabling residents to age-in-place and enjoy better quality of life.

  • Liaison with other key Ministries and government agencies in embracing new space economy, especially in the emergence of non-geostationary satellite network and systems

You will own the whole loop in a selected post-training domain: the reinforcement learning (RL) environments and harnesses the model learns in, the sandboxes where its actions run safely, the training tasks and the checkers that score them, and the fine-tuning and RL runs themselves.

This is not a role building chatbots or applications on top of LLM APIs; your work forms the core agentic capabilities of our models. 

LLM Post Training:
•	Run SFT and multi-turn RL on our GPU cluster, tune training recipe, while mitigating catastrophic forgetting
•	Read agent transcripts to find where the model fails, and fix it through changes to environments, data, rewards or training recipes
•	Check with our product team that gains hold up in real use
•	Contribute to our technical reports and papers

Environments and harnesses:
•	Build and scale tool-use and use-case-driven environments for agentic RL training, including tool servers and the automatic checkers that score the model's work
•	Maintain the harnesses that run our models through agentic tasks and benchmarks, used for both training and evaluation
•	Build containerised sandboxes on our GPU cluster, and own their security. That means code review, access controls - and testing that nothing escapes

• Maritime and Ports

Securities Settlement and Trade Support

Portfolio Compliance

  • Monitor portfolio compliance against investment guidelines, mandate parameters, and applicable regulatory requirements on an ongoing basis. Flag and escalate breaches and assist in their resolution.

Legal and Counterparty Documentation

  • Work with external counsel to review, negotiate, and execute investment management agreements, subscription agreements, side letters, and other legal documentation with investment counterparties.
  • Maintain a well-organised repository of all executed agreements and track key terms and obligations.

Tax and Regulatory Obligations

  • Review and monitor tax obligations arising from the investment portfolio, including withholding tax, GST, and fund-level tax considerations.
  • Liaise with tax advisors and counterparties on tax documentation such as W-8BEN and FATCA/CRS requirements.

Technology and Systems Implementation

  • Contribute to the evaluation, selection, and onboarding of operations and portfolio management systems appropriate for the Division's needs.
  • Work with internal stakeholders and vendors to configure systems, map workflows, and ensure data integrity across platforms.
  • Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency through technology as the Division's activities scale.

Governance, Process Enhancement, and Audit Support

  • Identify gaps in existing operational processes and controls and implement enhancements to strengthen investment governance.
  • Contribute to the development of operational policies, procedures, and frameworks.
  • Liaise with internal audit and support periodic reviews of the Division's control environment, ensuring findings are tracked and remediated in a timely manner.

  • Experience with custodian and fund administrator reconciliation processes.
  • Exposure to investment management agreements and subscription documentation is an advantage.
  • Working knowledge of compliance monitoring and investment guideline frameworks.
  • Familiarity with tax documentation requirements (e.g. FATCA, CRS, withholding tax) is an advantage.
  • Strong attention to detail and a high degree of accuracy in handling data and documentation.
  • Ability to work independently and take ownership in a lean team environment, with the initiative to build processes from scratch rather than simply follow established ones.
  • Good interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to manage external counterparties professionally.
  • A collaborative, can-do attitude and genuine interest in contributing to the broader success of the Investment Division.

The Group keeps Singapore’s digital connectivity secure,
trusted, and robust against an evolving and increasingly

jobResponsibilities:
You will be part of the Risk Assurance Division within IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group. The Holistic Assessment team in this Division assesses the overall cybersecurity risk posture of critical digital networks and systems and the cyber capabilities of organisations operating these networks.

This includes integrating diverse sources of information, across the organisation’s external environment, its internal capabilities and the performance of its networks and systems. The team adopts an evidence-based approach to develop an objective assessment of the organisation and network’s key strengths and vulnerabilities. It also recommends key areas that senior management should track to uplift its cybersecurity risk posture.

The Holistic Assessment team works with teams across IMDA’s Resilience and Cybersecurity Group, and in partnership with industry stakeholders. It regularly engages senior management in both IMDA and the industry, to review its findings and recommendations. Through these, the Holistic Assessment team plays a critical role in ensuring that the critical digital networks and systems which underpin Singapore’s Digital Economy remain secure and resilient.

  • Conduct research and sense making of the evolving cybersecurity landscape in relation to Singapore’s digital infrastructure. This includes integrating threat intelligence information as well as international industry best practices for defending against current and emerging cyber threats.
  • Review and assess key priorities that inspections should focus on, based on the current and emerging threat landscape, as well as potential vulnerabilities surfaced in cyber audit reports and remediations implemented.
  • Design technical tests to validate the effectiveness of cybersecurity measures within these priority areas. This requires a deep understanding of the network design, what the cybersecurity measures are intended to protect against, as well as how they contribute to the overall cybersecurity of the digital network and systems as a whole.
  • Conduct the technical validation tests.
  • Synthesise key findings from the inspections, on the strengths and vulnerabilities of the network. Recommend remediations that should be implemented to improve the overall cybersecurity of the digital network and systems inspected.
jobRequirements:
• Background in Information Security, Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent with 8 years of experience in relevant fields or capacity.
  • Possess relevant OSCP, CREST or GIAC certification in offensive operations or equivalent.
  • Good understanding of the digital landscape and appreciation of how the different facets of cyber threats and defence interact and impact the cybersecurity of digital networks and systems.
  • Possess strong analytical skills and an attention to detail.
  • Have an inquisitive mind to explore and evaluate novel methods of testing.
  • Excellent writing and communication skills. This includes translating technical findings to their strategic and business impact.
  • Enjoy working in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
  • Able to work independently as well as in a team/cross-team setting.

The position offered will be commensurate with experience.

Only shortlisted candidates will be notified.

The Southeast Asia and Oceania Division (SEAO) is a division in the Singapore Economic Development Board. SEAO plays a critical role in strengthening linkages between Singapore and the immediate region, and expanding Singapore’s economic hinterland. SEAO (i) develops and executes on government-to-government (G2G) partnerships; (ii) actively engages the region’s top private sector players – including major conglomerates, sectoral champions, and high growth startups, and (iii) facilitates the growth of global MNCs in Southeast Asia via Singapore. This positions Singapore as the choice location for companies to site their regional control tower, research and innovation, and advanced manufacturing operations, as they expand in the region.

Roles and Responsibilities

As a Manager/Senior Manager in the SEAO Division, you will operate at the unique intersection of bilateral economic policy, inter-agency stakeholder engagement, and investment promotion. You will have operational oversight over core cross-border economic initiatives, and support EDB’s corporate engagement in key regional markets including Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines. You will work with both global MNCs and regional conglomerates to best harness Singapore’s strengths and the complementary advantages of our immediate neighbours. You will need to understand and assess Singapore’s strategic interests, needs and develop the right solutions catered to Singapore’s position as a global business centre. You will also cultivate and maintain close ties with key influencers or decision makers in Singapore and the region ranging from government officials, industry leaders and company executives.

Bilateral Frameworks & G2G Policy Coordination

  • Drive Cross-Border Initiatives: Lead the operationalization and policy coordination for Singapore’s key regional partnerships, specifically the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and Batam-Bintan-Karimun region (BBK).

  • Inter-Agency Stakeholder Engagement: Work across multiple Singapore Government stakeholders to balance various interests and develop win-win solutions.

  • Bilateral Diplomacy: Work closely with bilateral government counterparts to align economic priorities, address cross-border regulatory frictions, and attract new investments into the region.

Corporate Account Management & Market Strategy

  • Portfolio Account Management: Support the management and engagement of strategic corporate relationships in Malaysia and the Philippines.

  • Engagement of key executives: Cultivate trusted relationships with senior company executives and next-generation business leaders to understand their regional expansion roadmaps and long-term priorities.
jobRequirements:
To succeed in this role, you should possess:

  • A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, International Relations, Public Policy, Engineering, or a related discipline.

  • At least 3 to 5 years of relevant working experience in corporate strategy, investment promotion, management consulting, public policy, or international trade relations.

  • Deep Regional Context: Strong understanding of the Southeast Asian macroeconomic landscape, with specific familiarity regarding the corporate governance, regulatory environments, and market dynamics of Malaysia, Indonesia and the Philippines.

  • Excellent Interpersonal & Influencing Skills: Ability to navigate complex government-to-government sensitivities with absolute discretion, and influence internal and external stakeholders at all levels of seniority.

  • Keen Business Acumen: Exceptional conceptual and analytical thinking, with the ability to translate complex public policy frameworks into high-yield commercial incentives for private enterprise.

• End-to-End Project Support: Manage the full lifecycle of applied research and proof-of-concept initiatives, including data preparation, rigorous experimentation, performance evaluation, comprehensive documentation, and post-deployment technical support.

• Educational Mentorship: Support curriculum development and actively mentor student capstone and research projects in robotics and applied AI domains.
• Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner closely with internal researchers and external industry stakeholders on collaborative innovation initiatives.
• Technology Advocacy: Lead and support engaging AI and robotics demonstrations for lab visits, innovation showcases, and executive partner engagements.

Programme and Content

As an open country constantly exposed to an interconnected world, Singapore faces complex issues in public healthcare. MOH constantly grapples with new challenges brought on by an increasingly globalised world, a rapidly ageing population and rising expectations. MOH’s responses to these challenges include preventing and managing the outbreak of diseases such as SARS and Influenza A (H1N1), designing a healthcare system that delivers care in an integrated and effective manner, growing the capacity and capabilities within the sector, and managing healthcare inflation.

As an MOH officer, you will be involved in formulating and implementing policies that guide Singapore’s healthcare ecosystem. You will work alongside a team with varied skills and backgrounds, but with the common goals of (i) promoting good health and reducing illnesses; (ii) ensuring that Singaporeans have access to good and affordable healthcare; and (iii) pursuing medical excellence. Your work will have far-reaching impact on the health and lives of Singaporeans.
jobDescription:
Shape Singapore’s Health at the National Level

Are you a medical doctor looking to make an impact beyond a clinical setting? Whether you are a junior doctor exploring your career options, or an established clinician contemplating new challenges to contribute at the national level, consider a career at the Ministry of Health (MOH).

Under the MOH Medical Service Scheme employment, you will bring your clinical lens and expertise to national healthcare policies and influence decisions that shape the health of Singapore. You will work at the intersection of medicine and policy to design the healthcare systems and frameworks that aim to improve the health outcomes for the nation, and be part of the national health leadership. 

You will be working in a fast-paced environment that would require the ability to manage multiple priorities and stakeholders at the same time. This is a role for doctors who are energised by complexity, motivated by purpose, and ready to drive healthcare transformation at a national scale.
jobResponsibilities:
You will contribute across four key domain areas:

•	Healthcare Regulation — Safeguarding standards and ensuring the safety, quality, and integrity of Singapore's healthcare system.
•	Manpower Development & Capability Building — Shaping the pipeline and professional development of Singapore's healthcare workforce.
•	Population Health & Health Services — Designing and delivering health programmes and services that keep Singaporeans healthy across their life course.
•	Quality, Value & Informatics — Driving innovation, data-driven decision making, and value in healthcare delivery.

At more senior levels, you may also lead and manage a team.

As part of your development, you may also be rotated to other public sector agencies and organisations within the broader healthcare ecosystem — such as the Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Health Promotion Board (HPB), Communicable Diseases Agency (CDA), or the public healthcare clusters. Your postings will be carefully designed to broaden your exposure and deepen your understanding of how policy translates into operations on the ground, equipping you with a well-rounded perspective to grow and contribute meaningfully throughout your career with MOH. 

While you will mostly be involved in healthcare policy work, you may also continue with sessional clinical practice, if you prefer, at the public healthcare institutions, so that you can maintain your clinical currency and familiarity with ground operations.
jobRequirements:
We welcome applications from medical doctors who are registered with the Singapore Medical Council (SMC) and remain in good standing. Beyond your medical qualifications, we are looking for doctors who embody the following:

•	Collaborative Spirit: You work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and are energised by cross-agency initiatives that drive system-wide change.
•	Critical Thinking: You bring your medical perspectives to bear on complex policy questions, evaluating evidence rigorously to inform national healthcare decisions.
•	Capacity for Change: You are adaptable and responsive to evolving health priorities, emerging challenges, and shifting policy landscapes.
•	Commitment to Continuous Learning: You are passionate about growing beyond clinical practice — into the domains of healthcare policy, regulation, and population health strategy.
•	Compassion: You connect with diverse stakeholders with empathy, and understand how policy decisions translate into real outcomes for real people.

We are also looking for doctors who demonstrate strength in systems thinking — the ability to understand complex healthcare ecosystems as a whole— as well as strategic thinking and the leadership capacity to inspire and guide teams through transformation.

Project & Product Delivery: Own the full project lifecycle with rigour — from initial requirements gathering and scoping through to final deployment — ensuring all geospatial solutions are fit for purpose, delivered on time, and within scope.

Platform Oversight & Administration: Oversee the technical management of the solutions on ArcGIS Enterprise Portal, including platform administration, user access control, content management, and configuration, ensuring a seamless and secure experience for government users.

Technical Consultation & Solutioning: Engage with senior stakeholders across the Healthcare, Social, Education, and Government sectors to translate organisational needs into structured geospatial workplans and clearly defined technical requirements, including identifying opportunities where AI can augment geospatial analysis and decision-making.

Solution Configuration: Drive the development and configuration of geospatial applications, applying your technical depth to solve spatial problems for agencies across the public sector.

Capability & Training: Lead the design and delivery of geospatial programmes and technical workshops, effectively upskilling both technical and non-technical audiences in modern GIS workflows and emerging AI-augmented geospatial capabilities.

Strategic Communication: Champion geospatial technology as a persuasive advocate, translating technical complexity into clear, value-driven business cases for senior management and decision-makers.
jobRequirements:
The ideal candidate is a technically grounded professional with 8 to 10 years of relevant experience, with a proven track record of bridging technical development and executive-level project and product management. A forward-looking awareness of how AI and machine learning are reshaping the geospatial landscape is strongly desired.

Technical Requirements & Expertise

ArcGIS Platform Knowledge: Advanced, hands-on experience with ArcGIS Enterprise Portal administration and configuration is mandatory. You should be deeply familiar with the ESRI suite, including ArcGIS Pro, ArcGIS Online, and associated extension tools, as well as the ArcGIS API for Python for workflow automation.

Development & Automation: Proficiency in Python and JavaScript is required to drive automation and support geospatial solution development. Familiarity with R is an advantage.

Geospatial Analytics: A solid technical understanding of geospatial concepts, data fusion techniques, and advanced spatial analytical methods.

AI & Machine Learning Awareness: A working understanding of how AI and machine learning techniques can be applied in a geospatial context is highly desirable. This includes familiarity with spatial predictive modelling, automated feature extraction from imagery, or the use of Python-based AI/ML libraries. Hands-on experience in this area is a strong advantage, though candidates with a clear aptitude and willingness to develop these skills will also be considered.

Open Source: Experience with QGIS is considered a bonus.

Project Management & Leadership

Process-Driven Management: Strong organisational skills with demonstrated experience managing full project lifecycles and vendor relationships. A formal project management certification (such as PMP, etc) is highly advantageous.

Business Analysis: Strong skills in requirements gathering, solution scoping, and stakeholder alignment, ensuring that technical solutions are grounded in practical business needs.

Communication: Ability to produce compelling, high-quality presentation decks and articulate complex geospatial and AI concepts clearly to non-technical stakeholders at all levels.

Collaborative Leadership: Proven ability to build and manage diverse, cross-functional working relationships across multiple government agencies and teams, driving delivery in a collaborative environment.

jobDescription:
The Economics Department (ED) in the Ministry of Manpower advances evidence-based and data-driven policymaking through robust labour research, analysis and analytics. ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Data Analysts work closely with economists, research analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate data-driven insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
As a Data Analyst in ED, you will help to shape manpower policies in Singapore through the application of data science, advanced analytics and clear policy communication.

You will use a range of data analytics techniques – including machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling, statistical analysis, data visualisation and other frontier data science approaches – to examine traditional and emerging issues relating to manpower policies and the labour market.

Your work will contribute to strengthening the evidence base for policymaking, uncovering new insights from complex datasets, and supporting better outcomes for workers, businesses and Singapore’s labour market.
Your responsibilities will include:

•	Applying advanced analytics to manpower policy issues
Use data science techniques to analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, skills mismatches, job transitions, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Developing new analytical approaches and datasets
Identify, process and analyse novel datasets, including structured and unstructured data, to generate new insights on labour market trends, policy issues and operational challenges.

•	Using frontier data science methods
Apply methods such as machine learning, natural language processing, text analytics, network analytics, predictive modelling and simulation techniques to support policy analysis and decision-making.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and policy monitoring
Develop indicators, dashboards and analytical tools to monitor labour market developments, workforce trends and emerging risks in a timely and policy-relevant manner.

•	Strengthening policy design and operational effectiveness
Work with policymakers and operational divisions to translate data insights into practical recommendations that improve policy design, programme implementation and operational outcomes.

•	Collaborating with economists and researchers
Work closely with economists, research analysts and external partners to combine data science techniques with economic theory, empirical research and policy domain knowledge.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex analytical findings into clear, intuitive and policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.
jobRequirements:
We are looking for candidates who are intellectually curious, analytically rigorous and passionate about using data science to improve public policy.

•	Strong analytical and critical thinking skills, with the ability to frame policy problems and translate them into data analytics projects.

jobDescription:
We are seeking applicants to join the Architecture & Land Planning Division to help on architectural conservation and urban design strategies for the Greater Sentosa Master Plan (GSMP) and related projects.

This will include conceptualisation & delivery of architectural conservation planning strategies and urban design policies & guidelines, and coordination with planning & technical agencies to ensure that the planning intent is in line with the broader Greater Southern Waterfront plans. Part of the role involves managing of stakeholder engagements, regulatory approvals, budget unlocking, experience-driven implementation, execution of tender processes & assisting in the project management for heritage developments & infrastructure enablers required for the implementation the masterplan vision.
jobResponsibilities:
Key Responsibilities

Architecture Conservation & Urban Design

  • Develop Architecture & Conservation Urban Design strategies to drive masterplanning work for delightful, attractive & sensitive heritage-related developments and design excellence as part of the Greater Sentosa Master Plan (GSMP).
  • Coordinate with planning & technical agencies on architectural conservation planning works for GSMP with the broader GSW as well as national planning policies.
  • Plan, formulate and execute heritage research, heritage impact assessments, conservation management, adaptive reuse & urban design strategies to conserve, restore & rejuvenate built heritage elements including the Fort Siloso National Monument, the Sentosa Conservation Precinct, the Sentosa Heritage Trail and other heritage-related developments at the masterplanning, precinct & building scale for the various phases of the GSMP, including rejuvenation of Sentosa and bringing in the next game changer attraction for Pulau Brani.

Integrative Design Development & Implementation

  • Establish, coordinate and implement development plans taking into consideration strategic goals, appropriate development densities, attractive tourism strategies, sustainable transport, district & infrastructural enablers, sensitivity towards built & natural heritage, green & blue spaces, sustainability efforts, coastal protection efforts, placemaking strategies and phasing timelines.

  • Degree in Architectural Conservation, Architecture, Urban Design, Urban Planning, or related field.
  • Minimum relevant 5-years experience in conservation redevelopment works, urban planning & design processes.

  • Proficiency in software such as AutoCAD, BIM, rhino, sketch up Photoshop, and ArcGIS.
  • Proactive and creative approach, with a passion for architectural heritage & conservation.
  • Strong understanding of international preservation & conservation principles, Singapore's architectural conservation framework and conversant with local building codes & regulations.

agencyDescription:
Established in 2001, the Health Promotion Board’s (HPB) vision is to build a nation of healthy people.

We aim to empower residents in Singapore to attain optimal health, increase the quality and years of healthy life, and prevent illnesses, disability and premature death.

To achieve this, HPB drives national health promotion and disease prevention programmes, spearheads health education initiatives and creates a supportive environment in Singapore where healthy lifestyle options are available and accessible for healthy living every day.
jobDescription:
The Health Promotion Board’s vision is to make Singapore a nation of healthier people.

Come be a part of this journey if you’re passionate about creating boundary-pushing work that drives behavioral change.

You will be part of HPB’s Integrated Outreach team, which aims to create a Health Living Environment (HLE) where we make healthy living as part of every day life in Singapore. We aim to do so by place making, activating communities and empowering community leaders to play a role in health promotion. This transformative project shifts HPB's role from traditional programme provider to community enabler, embedding health promotion into citizens' lived environments across entire neighbourhoods. We are seeking a dynamic and strategic Manager/Senior Manager to spearhead community activation and drive sustainable behavioural change together with healthcare cluster (SingHealth, National University Hospital Systems, National Healthcare Group) and other community partners at the town level.
jobResponsibilities:
As a core member of the HLE initiative, you will be responsible for operationalising an innovative approach to community health that reaches the unreached and transforms neighbourhoods into health-promoting ecosystems. This role represents HPB's strategic pivot towards citizen-centric, place-based health interventions that integrate clinical care with lifestyle support anchored in local communities. You will develop skills in translating data insights into clear strategies and practical actions, data storytelling, stakeholder engagement and negotiation, project management, and cross-agency coordination.

Key Responsibilities

Regional Roll out and Coordination of HLE

  • Support the rollout of the HLE initiative within the assigned region(s), ensuring consistency with national direction while allowing for regional/local adaptations

  • Apply HLE standards (e.g. digital wayfinding standard, engagement playbook, and collaboration manual) during initiative rollout and guide grassroot leaders and community partners (e.g. AACs) in using these resources effectively

  • Utilise community health dashboards and local data insights to empower grassroots and community leaders in identifying priority health needs and co-creating targeted interventions that address specific neighbourhood health gaps

  • Coordinate and support HLE implementation, including meeting facilitation and general project management tasks

Stakeholder Partnership and Capability Building

  • Work with grassroot advisors/leaders, clusters, and community partners to co-create and coordinate neighbourhood-level activities and strengthen community-led health agendas, building community ownership and optimising community spaces into vibrant, health-promoting environments

  • Deliver training sessions and provide practical support to grassroot leaders and community partners (e.g. AACs) in applying the playbook, message house, menu of actions, wayfinding guides, and dashboards

  • Support the team in collaborating with key healthcare partners in their planning and implementation of regional health promotion activities

Programme Activation and Targeted Outreach

  • Coordinate community and regional health programmes, ensuring they are relevant to residents and responsive to their needs

  • Utilise data to prioritise high-need groups, working with GRAs to apply targeted outreach models, outreach quadrants, and activation toolkits in local contexts

  • Connect residents to healthy living assets and programmes by enlivening the lived environment and the Healthy 365 online-offline resident journey, through local mapping that guides them from discovery to sustained participation.

Monitoring, Feedback and Continuous Improvement

  • Track ground-level progress of HLE initiatives, consolidate feedback from residents, local stakeholders, and share insights with the project team and data teams to strengthen impact measurement

  • Collate, utilise and evaluate data from other sources where required, to create a comprehensive picture of the precinct's health profile and its target segments
jobRequirements:
An ideal candidate will be a collaborative leader with a passion for community health promotion transformation and systems thinking. You should have experience in community engagement, partnership management, or public health programme implementation, with the ability to work effectively across diverse stakeholder groups.

While a degree in a specific field is not mandatory, candidates with backgrounds in business administration/management, public health/public policy/public administration, sociology/psychology, health sciences, communications/media, or related field often possess relevant skills. Trained in project or account management is an added advantage.

The candidate should also possess:

  • A driven and resilient nature; comfortable with challenges and able to work effectively under pressure, both independently and as part of a team

  • Strong collaborative and interpersonal skills with the ability to build rapport with diverse stakeholders

  • Adaptability and the ability to work cohesively in fast-paced teams whilst navigating complex, ambiguous situations positively

  • Analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a result-oriented mindset

  • Comfort working effectively in matrix and highly dynamic team environments

  • Basic data analysis and evaluation capabilities

Successful candidates will be offered a 1-year contract.

agencyDescription:
The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors so as to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

• Civil Aviation and Air Transport
• Maritime and Ports
• Land Transport

What You Will Do

  • Architect secure, scalable, and high-availability solutions for AFC and payment systems, including those built on EMV, open-loop standards, account-based ticketing, and card-based ticketing models in the GCC2.0 AWS environment.

  • Design and govern end-to-end system integration architectures across distributed, multi-vendor environments, leveraging event-driven patterns and message-oriented middleware including messaging protocols such as MQ and MQTT, communication protocols such as HTTP/S and WebSockets, and integration patterns such as REST APIs, webhooks, and pub/sub architectures, to support both real-time and asynchronous processing needs.

  • Lead security architecture design to ensure compliance with Govtech’s IM8 and security requirements to safeguard sensitive payment and commuter data.

  • Lead network infrastructure design, including the planning and governance of network topology, connectivity, and security controls across cloud and hybrid environments to ensure scalable, resilient, and secure deployments

  • Produce and maintain system architecture and networking infrastructure diagrams, API and interface specifications, and integration designs with clear documentation of network infrastructure components.

  • Translate business and system requirements into high-level and detailed technical specifications, interface designs, and integration patterns suited to complex multi-system environments. Perform technical impact analysis for change requests and system enhancements, ensuring minimal disruption to mission-critical AFC operations.

  • Conduct solution walkthroughs, architecture reviews, and technical presentations for internal and external stakeholders. Collaborate with internal stakeholders (project teams, software development, operations) and external partners (vendors, financial institutions) to develop robust and future-ready solutions.
jobRequirements:
• Knowledge in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, or related field.

  • At least 5 years of experience in solution architecture, systems analysis/design, or complex enterprise IT infrastructure.

  • Networks and Protocols — working knowledge of common network and communication protocols such as TCP/IP, HTTP/S, FTPS, and SFTP, and the OSI model as applied to enterprise system design.

  • Enterprise Integration Patterns — experience designing solutions using APIs, webhooks, WebSockets, message queues, MQTT, and pub/sub or event-driven architectures across complex, multi-system environments.

  • Data and Interfaces — familiarity with data serialisation formats such as JSON and binary, and how these are applied across system integration touchpoints.

  • Network Infrastructure — understanding of IP addressing, CIDR, subnets, firewalls, routers, MPLS, and availability zone design in cloud and hybrid environments.

​Bonus Skills:

  • AWS certifications (e.g., AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate/Professional) are strongly preferred

  • Experience in Automatic Fare Collection (AFC) systems, open-loop payment architecture, or financial-grade transaction systems.

  • Strong knowledge of security architecture, including secure data flows, tokenisation, encryption, and compliance standards (e.g., PCI DSS).

  • Hands-on exposure to DevSecOps, CI/CD, containerisation (e.g., ECS, EKS), serverless architecture, or data streaming pipelines.

  • Security and Compliance — experience embedding a defence-in-depth approach across all layers of solution design, encompassing network security, identity and access management, data protection, encryption, vulnerability management, and threat detection and response, with a strong understanding of government and industry compliance standards such as IM8 and PCI-DSS.

  • GCC AWS — familiarity with Singapore's Government Commercial Cloud on AWS, including its governance requirements and deployment constraints.

jobDescription:
The Economics Department (ED) in the Ministry of Manpower advances evidence-based and data-driven policymaking through robust labour research, analysis and analytics. ED undertakes economic surveillance and forecasting, ex-ante policy analyses, ex-post impact evaluations, applied economic research and advanced analytics to inform manpower policies that shape Singapore’s labour market, workplaces and retirement outcomes.

Research Analysts work closely with economists, data analysts, policymakers and operational divisions to generate evidence-based insights that support policy formulation, implementation and evaluation. ED’s work spans key areas such as labour market dynamics, productivity and human capital development, wages and inequality, labour security and retirement adequacy, and labour market policies and regulations. 

ED is organised into three sub-units:

•	Economic Research Unit (ERU)
Supports manpower policies that optimise workforce allocation, strengthen human capital and drive business outcomes.

•	Socio-Economic Research Unit (SRU)
Supports manpower policies that strengthen workplace outcomes, improve inclusivity and enhance retirement adequacy.

•	Analytics Research Unit (ARU)
Supports manpower policies by leveraging big data and advanced analytics to uncover deeper labour market insights, strengthen policy design and enhance operational effectiveness.
jobResponsibilities:
•	Conducting policy-relevant research and analysis
Analyse a diverse range of manpower issues, including workforce allocation, foreign and local manpower policies, retirement adequacy, lower-wage workers, vulnerable workforce segments, workplace outcomes and business impacts.

•	Supporting economic surveillance and forecasting
Contribute to ED’s monitoring of labour market developments, workforce trends and economic indicators to support timely policy assessments and decision-making.

•	Undertaking ex-ante and ex-post policy analysis
Assess the likely impact of proposed policies before implementation, and evaluate the actual impact of policies and programmes after implementation.

•	Applying quantitative and empirical methods
Use econometric, statistical, data analytics and modelling techniques to derive insights from administrative data, surveys and other datasets.

•	Building domain expertise in labour economics
Develop specialist knowledge of labour economics, public policy, empirical methods, data sources, analytical frameworks and relevant academic literature.

•	Collaborating across Government and with external researchers
Work with researchers, economists, policymakers and operational teams within and outside MOM to support policy thinking and strengthen evidence-based policymaking.

•	Communicating insights clearly and effectively
Translate complex research findings into clear, policy-relevant insights for senior management, policymakers and other stakeholders.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

You will be part of the team that develops the specialised engineering capabilities required to establish EMA as an informed technical lead on advanced nuclear power systems. What you will be working on:

1. Engineering Benchmarking & Technical Modelling

  • Technical Specialisation: Build specialised institutional expertise in advanced thermal-hydraulic systems, core physics, and material behaviour for next-generation nuclear energy technologies.

  • Multi-disciplinary Assessment: Conduct engineering research across Civil, Mechanical, and Electrical disciplines to verify the technical claims of emerging global technologies.

  • Technical Standards Governance: Build frameworks to evaluate how design modifications might affect the overall integrity of a technology's safety envelope.

3. Strategic Technical Partnerships

  • Technical Collaboration: Coordinate with international engineering consultants and research organizations to facilitate knowledge transfer and capability building.

  • Standards Advocacy: Act as a technical lead in researching how international engineering standards can be applied to optimise advanced technology for compact land-use constraints.

  • Technology Horizon Scanning: Monitor global trends in advanced nuclear technology (e.g., SMRs and Generation IV systems) to provide data-driven technical insights to senior leadership.

agencyDescription:
The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

The Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) is a uniformed organisation under the purview of the Ministry of Home Affairs. The main role of SCDF is to provide fire-fighting, rescue and emergency ambulance services; mitigating hazardous materials incidents, as well as formulate, implement and enforce regulations on fire safety and civil defence shelter matters.

In 1982, the National Civil Defence Plan was launched which spearheaded the emergency preparedness for the nation. With the enactment of the Civil Defence Act in 1986, the SCDF was established as an independent organisation under the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA). In the same year, the Hotel New World collapse paved the way for joint operations between the SCDF and Singapore Fire Service (SFS). Due to the similarity in roles and functions, the SCDF and SFS were formally integrated on 15 April 1989.

Over the years, the SCDF has improved its life saving operations through innovations and programmes to enhance her fire-fighting, rescue capabilities and public education plans. The Light Fire Attack Vehicle (The Red Rhino) and Tracked Fire-Fighting Vehicle are some of the customized solutions which the force has developed to increase its operational capabilities. The SCDF also actively engages the local community through its wide-ranging public educational programmes and community-based activities to enhance the resilience and emergency preparedness of the civilian population.

Today, the Force is recognised by the population as a professional body of well-trained officers and men geared to respond to all types of life-threatening emergencies round-the-clock. An operationally ready SCDF, working hand-in-hand with a prepared and resilient population, helps to ensure that the nation is capable of handling any untoward eventualities.

This assessment encompasses, but is not limited to, secure configurations, insider threats, vendor risks, data leakage, malwares including ransomware, account hijacking, and compliance risks.

GovTech Data Practice


The Data Practice drives innovation and sets best practices for the effective and responsible use of data across the Whole-of-Government (WOG). We work at the intersection of data engineering, AI, privacy, and governance - developing standards, platforms, and tools that enable agencies to build high-quality data products and unlock the value of data for public good.

Today, most organisations still struggle with data that is fragmented, inconsistent, and hard to use, alongside AI that is powerful but brittle without strong data foundations, and privacy policies that are difficult to operationalise. We are changing that at a national scale.

We are reimagining data engineering itself through AI for Data Engineering (AIDE), which introduces self-improving data pipelines that detect, fix, and optimise themselves, AI-assisted data modelling and quality management at scale, and semantic, context-aware data layers that make data instantly usable for AI. Underpinned by standardised, AI-native architectures, this ensures every agency can build strong foundations from day one.

At the same time, a Trusted Data Nation only works if data can be used without compromising privacy or security. We operationalise Privacy-Enhancing Technologies (PETs) into real capabilities, including federated computing to unlock insights without moving data, differential privacy and synthetic data to enable safe sharing, and trusted execution environments to compute on sensitive data securely. Alongside this, we build the golden paths for Singapore by creating reference architectures, reusable components, standard data platforms, and engineering playbooks that scale quality across government.

jobDescription:

The challenge

What happens when technology, delivery and threats move faster than an organisation’s ability to see and respond to risk?

And what could become possible if risk management moved just as quickly?

Every organisation needs a way to detect warning signs, connect the dots and act before problems spread.

That is the role of governance, risk and control.

Think of it as the organisation’s nervous system. It picks up signals from across the organisation, helps leaders make sense of them and enables a timely response.

When that system works well, teams can move faster, take smarter risks and deliver with greater confidence. When it does not, warning signs are missed, decisions slow down and governance becomes a barrier rather than an enabler.

GovTech has strong platforms, talented people and an important mission. As our role and public impact grow, the risks we manage are becoming more interconnected, fast-moving and consequential.

We are looking for Deputy Directors and Assistant Directors in Enterprise Risk Management who want to help build what comes next.

You will have the opportunity to challenge established practices, experiment with data and AI, influence senior decisions and shape how one of Singapore’s most important technology organisations manages risk.

[What you will be working on]

This is a role for people who want more than a steady portfolio. It is for those who want to build, push boundaries and leave the system better than they found it.

What you will have the chance to change. We want to move enterprise risk management:

  • from periodic reporting to more continuous risk visibility

  • from manual collation to data and AI-enabled insight

  • from risk registers to clearer decisions and action

  • from unclear accountability to risks with active owners

  • from retrospective assurance to earlier intervention

  • from compliance activity to practical support for delivery


This is not simply a reporting role. You will help shape how risk is understood, discussed, owned and acted upon across GovTech.

Your mandate

Your job is to make enterprise risk management useful.

You will work with senior leaders, risk owners and teams across GovTech to identify what matters, make trade-offs visible and support action before issues become incidents.

Depending on your experience and appointment level, you will lead or take ownership of significant ERM portfolios and initiatives.

You will have room to test ideas, challenge established practices and build better approaches. You will also need to influence people you do not manage and create clarity where risks, priorities or accountabilities are contested.

That is part of the job.

Break the Frame

Modern risk management cannot rely only on inherited frameworks, templates and periodic reporting.

We want people who are prepared to question established practices, test better approaches and rethink how risk management should work in a technology organisation.

You will explore how data, AI and automation can help GovTech:

  • detect weak signals and emerging risks earlier

  • connect information across the organisation

  • reduce manual reporting and administrative work

  • give leaders more timely and useful risk insight

  • strengthen judgement without removing human accountability

This requires an experimental mindset. You should be comfortable testing ideas, learning from what does not work and turning successful experiments into practical capabilities.

The aim is not to use AI to perform old processes faster. It is to ask whether those processes are still needed and design better ones where they are not.

We call this Break the Frame: looking beyond established ways of working, pushing boundaries responsibly and building an ERM function that can keep pace with modern technology.

What you will do

Strengthen our ERM approach

Develop and improve GovTech’s enterprise risk framework, methodology and governance arrangements.

Clarify who owns each risk, how issues should be escalated and where decisions should sit.

Make sure the approach works for a modern technology organisation rather than forcing teams into processes that add little value.

Build a forward-looking view of risk

Maintain a current view of GovTech’s key risks across strategy, technology, operations, delivery, vendors, regulation, data, reputation and organisational capability.

Look beyond known issues and past incidents. Identify emerging threats, dependencies and concentrations of risk before they become larger problems.

Keep GovTech’s enterprise risk profile, register and monitoring approach relevant and useful to decision-makers.

Support better leadership decisions

Provide clear and practical advice to senior leadership, Board-level committees, auditors and oversight bodies, including SNDGO and relevant central agencies.

Turn complex risk issues into straightforward choices, trade-offs and recommendations.

Help leaders understand what matters most, what needs to be done, who should act and where attention is required.

Modernise how risk management is done

Improve processes that are too manual, retrospective or disconnected from day-to-day operations.

Use data, AI, automation and emerging technologies to improve the timeliness and quality of risk information.

Run practical experiments, test new approaches and turn successful ideas into reusable capabilities.

Develop tools and guidance that help teams manage risk as part of their work, not as a separate compliance exercise.

Work across GovTech

Partner with product, engineering, cybersecurity, operations, policy, procurement and corporate functions.

Help leaders balance delivery speed, resilience, governance and risk appetite.

Build trusted relationships and support honest conversations, especially where risks or accountabilities are unclear or contested.

Represent GovTech in relevant cross-agency risk and governance forums.


What good looks like

Success will not be measured by the number of reports produced.

You will know the role is making a difference when:

  • leadership has a clearer view of GovTech’s most important risks

  • risks are surfaced earlier and acted on faster

  • ownership and accountability are clear

  • risk insight improves strategic and operational decisions

  • governance supports responsible delivery rather than slowing it down

  • manual reporting is reduced

  • successful experiments lead to better ways of working

  • teams see ERM as a practical partner

  • GovTech is better prepared for disruption and emerging risks

We are looking for people who want to improve how things work, not simply maintain existing processes. You should bring:

  • experience in a technology-intensive, operationally complex or regulated organisation

  • a strong understanding of risk appetite, governance, accountability and assurance

  • sound judgement and the confidence to challenge constructively

  • the ability to turn complex issues into clear choices and actions

  • credibility with senior leaders, auditors, regulators and technical teams

  • experience influencing across organisational boundaries

  • curiosity about how data, AI and automation can improve risk management

Candidates considered for the Assistant Director level should have strong delivery capability, sound risk judgement and the ability to lead significant portfolios and stakeholder engagements.

jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better where we empower our people to master their craft through robust learning and development opportunities all year round.

Play a part in Sigapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

[What you will be working on]

Some problems are easy to walk past. Others keep nagging at you.
Why are we still doing this manually?
Why does sensible policy become painful when it meets the real world?
Why do we discover risks after the fact when the signals were already there?

How should government govern AI systems that increasingly make decisions and take actions for themselves? And why, when technology can change in minutes, does governance sometimes still move in months?

If questions like these bother you enough that you want to get underneath them, experiment with better answers and solve the real-world problem, we should talk.

We are rethinking what modern governance, risk and assurance could look like across GovTech and, ultimately, the wider Singapore Government.

GovTech is where we can design, build, test and learn. The ambition is bigger.

Why this matters

We are modernising Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) so government can use technology and AI with greater confidence, improve services faster, and keep the essential systems people rely on dependable and resilient.

Ultimately, the test is bigger than GRC: Can government use technology better, serve citizens better, and retain their trust when things go wrong?

That is the problem behind this role. And we do not expect to solve it by designing the perfect framework in a room.

We expect to work on real systems, with real users and real constraints. To experiment. Test assumptions. Prototype, understand behavior and incentives. Learn from what does not work.

And turn what does into something that can work at government scale. One role. Multiple archetypes. This is one modern GRC role, not six separate jobs or six career tracks.

The six archetypes below describe different capabilities a Modern GRC Practitioner can develop and create a problem.

You might begin with strength in one. Over time, you can acquire additional archetypes without giving up the ones you already have. An engineer might combine GRC Platform Engineering with Policy Engineering and AI Governance. An assurance practitioner might bring together Threat-Informed Risk Intelligence, Enterprise Risk Management and Systems Architecture. A policy practitioner might combine Policy Engineering with behavioral insights, systems thinking and platform capability.

Which archetypes you draw on depends on the problem. Some practitioners will build deep expertise in one or two. Others will develop a broader combination across several. Neither is a prescribed progression. The archetypes are not boxes to move between. They are capabilities you can accumulate, combine and apply. The ambition is to build practitioners with an increasingly powerful repertoire for understanding and solving difficult problems. Six capabilities you could build and combine.

Make policy work in the real world

Policy Engineering

How do we design policy that survives contact with engineers, users and actual organisational behavior?

Bring together domain expertise, behavioral insights, human-centered design and technology to create controls that people can understand, systems can implement and organisations can actually operate.

A technically correct policy that everyone works around is not a successful policy.

Turn uncertainty into decisions

Enterprise Risk Management

How do we help leaders decide which risks matter, what needs intervention and what we can deliberately live with? Connect signals across the organisation, expose dependencies and concentration risks, translate risk appetite into practical choices and bring better analysis to difficult decisions.

The output is not another register. It is a better decision.

Build assurance into the technology

GRC Platform Engineering

How do we make governance and assurance part of the delivery environment rather than another checkpoint around it? Build Policy-as-Code, automated evidence, continuous control verification and other infrastructure that makes safer behavior easier and assurance more timely.

Sometimes the answer is automation. Sometimes the smarter answer is removing the process first.

Govern systems that increasingly act for themselves

AI & Agentic Governance

What can an AI agent decide? Where must humans intervene? How should decision boundaries, accountability and assurance work when autonomous systems act at scale?

How do we govern model drift, changing behavior and GRC's own use of AI? Some answers exist. Many do not. You could help develop them.

Find the signal before it becomes the incident

Threat-Informed Risk Intelligence

How do we understand what is changing now rather than explain months later what went wrong? Connect cyber, data, resilience, platform, supply-chain and operational signals to identify patterns and emerging risks earlier.

Less: “Did the control pass?” More: “Is it working now, what changed, and what does that tell us?”

See the system everyone else sees in pieces

GRC Systems Architecture

How do policy, risk, controls, evidence, engineering and assurance fit together?

Design the taxonomies, information flows, feedback loops and operating models that allow them to work as one system. Ask some people about one control and they will explain the other three things it affects.

We like those people.

[What we are looking for]

Break the Frame

We are not looking for people to make yesterday's processes 10% faster. We want people willing to ask:

  • Why does this exist?

  • What risk are we actually managing?

  • What evidence says it works?

  • What behavior are we creating?

  • Could technology remove this step?

  • Could we design the problem away?

Sometimes the answer is better policy. Sometimes automation. Sometimes a different operating model. Occasionally, the right answer is to stop doing something altogether.

The expectation is not to challenge everything. It is to know what deserves to be challenged, why, and what should replace it.

What working here may feel like:

  • You will not always inherit a neatly defined problem.

  • Evidence may be incomplete. People may disagree about what is wrong.

  • A process may have existed so long that nobody quite remembers why.

  • Sometimes the problem you were asked to solve will turn out not to be the real problem.

That is part of the work.

Investigate before recommending. Prototype before standardising. Sit with engineers and users before writing policy. Use evidence before forming conclusions. Connect signals that others have not put together. And be willing to change your mind when your first hypothesis is wrong. We consider that progress.

What good looks like

Success is not the number of policies, findings, reports or dashboards produced. We are making progress when:

  • important risks are seen earlier

  • leaders make difficult decisions with better evidence

  • teams encounter fewer unnecessary governance touchpoints

  • policy is easier to understand, implement and verify

  • more assurance comes from live evidence

  • recurring problems are solved at system level

  • safer behavior happens increasingly by design

  • government can adopt AI and emerging technologies with greater confidence

  • governance helps delivery move faster rather than becoming the reason it slows down

And ultimately: Government uses technology better, essential services remain dependable, and citizens experience better public services without sacrificing trust. That is the measure that matters.

Who might find this interesting

There is no single background we are looking for.

You may come from engineering, cybersecurity, risk, assurance, resilience, AI, architecture, digital policy, product delivery, behavioural science, service design, design research, or somewhere less obvious.

Depth matters. But so does what happens when you reach the edge of what you know.

  • Do you get curious?

  • Can you make sense of messy information?

  • Can you work with people who see the problem differently?

  • Can you connect technical, organisational and human factors?

  • Can you turn an idea into something testable?

  • And when something clearly could work better, do you find it difficult to simply walk past?

For some of the problems we are tackling, the answer does not exist yet. That is precisely what makes them worth working on.

This may not be for everyone

If you are looking for a mature playbook, tightly defined boundaries and a portfolio that mainly needs maintaining, there are probably better roles. This work involves ambiguity, experimentation, difficult trade-offs and the occasional failed idea. But if a stubborn problem bothers you enough that you want to understand it, challenge assumptions and build something better, we should probably have a conversation.

Why GovTech

GovTech is in an unusual position. We help shape government technology policy. We build and operate major digital platforms. We can engineer governance and assurance into real delivery environments. We can test ideas against real-world problems and see whether they actually work. And what works here can become capability that benefits the wider Singapore Government.

So, this is not simply a chance to practice GRC differently. It is a chance to help discover what modern governance, risk and assurance needs to become.

As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government’s capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity.

Play a part in Singapore’s vision to build a Smart Nation and embark on your meaningful journey to build tech for public good. Join us to advance our mission and shape your future with us today!

The Government Digital Products (GDP) team builds and operates the digital products and platforms that power the Singapore Government's digital services. Within GDP, the Information Services Program (ISP) builds the shared platforms behind information discovery, publishing, accessibility, analytics, and AI-powered experiences — foundational capabilities that enable agencies to deliver trusted digital services.

Why Join Us?

Imagine building platforms that become part of a nation's digital infrastructure. At the Information Services Program (ISP), that's exactly what we do.

Our products—including SearchSG, VICA, WebSG, Optical, WOGAA, and Oobee—help citizens find information, enable agencies to publish trusted content, improve accessibility, measure digital service quality, and power AI-assisted experiences. Used across the Singapore Government, every improvement you make has a multiplier effect.

Instead of building for a single product or customer segment, you'll build platforms that enable hundreds of government teams to deliver better digital services. You'll tackle challenges in search, chat assistant, content infrastructure, accessibility, analytics, and distributed systems while making architectural decisions that shape how millions of people interact with the Singapore Government every day.

If you're passionate about platform products engineering and building technology that amplifies the impact of other teams, you'll find plenty of meaningful and technically challenging problems here.

The Role

We are looking for a Technical Lead / Engineering Manager to lead the next evolution of our platforms.

You'll own the technical direction and delivery of a cross-functional engineering team, balancing long-term platform investments with rapid product delivery. This is a hands-on engineering leadership role where you'll shape architecture, raise engineering standards, mentor engineers, and foster a culture of ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Working closely with Product Managers, Designers, and fellow Engineering Leaders, you'll tackle complex engineering problems while building reliable, secure, and scalable platforms that underpin digital services across government.

Your impact extends well beyond a single product or team. Every improvement you make enables hundreds of government teams to build better digital services, ultimately improving how people discover information, access public services, and engage with the Singapore Government.

What You'll Do:

Lead and Nurture a High-Performing Team.

  • Lead, coach, and grow a cross-functional engineering team through technical mentorship, regular feedback, and a culture of ownership and continuous improvement.

  • Provide hands-on technical leadership to unblock complex engineering bottlenecks while empowering engineers to do their best work.

Drive Technical Strategy and Platform Evolution

  • Define the technical vision and architecture for platforms used across the Singapore Government.

  • Balance rapid product delivery with long-term platform reliability, maintainability, and scalability.

  • Evaluate and implement technical solutions that meet strict Whole-of-Government security and compliance standards.

  • Actively identify and mitigate technical risks, maintaining a healthy balance between delivering customer value and reducing technical debt.

  • Partner with Product, Design, Infrastructure, and Platform teams to align on product roadmap execution, system dependencies, and cross-team technical initiatives.

Raise the Engineering Bar

  • Champion best practices in system design, code quality, automated testing, and comprehensive code/architecture reviews.

  • Drive strong operational ownership. Champion robust CI/CD pipelines, containerization, infrastructure-as-code, and comprehensive test automation.

  • Utilize engineering and operational metrics (e.g., system reliability, performance, delivery flow) to continuously optimize team’s effectiveness and system stability.

  • Establish scalable engineering processes such as design reviews, architecture discussions, and effective code reviews.

  • Explore practice applications of AI and GenAI to improve both product capabilities and internal engineering workflows.

How to Succeed:

Experience

  • 7+ years of experience engineering, scaling, and delivering production-grade web applications, with a heavy emphasis on robust backend systems.

  • Demonstrated experience operating as a Technical Lead or Engineering Manager within an agile environment. Proven ability to align engineering squads and manage vendor deliverables or hybrid teams is a strong plus.

  • A solid track record of designing, architecting, and operating scalable distributed systems, ideally within multi-tenant SaaS platforms or enterprise-grade applications.

Technical Skills

  • Strong production-tested expertise in Node.js and TypeScript / Go.

  • Solid understanding of cloud platforms (AWS preferred), container technologies (Docker), and establishing or operating modern CI/CD pipelines.

  • Strong software engineering fundamentals, including automated testing, system design, and architectural reviews.

  • Strong hands-on experience building web applications and robust APIs using React or Next.js.

  • Exposure to or a strong interest in GenAI technologies and incorporating AI-powered capabilities into product features is highly advantageous.

Leadership & Mindset

  • Strong technical judgment with the ability to make practical architectural trade-offs between rapid product innovation, system stability, and strict security guardrails.

  • An excellent communicator who can seamlessly translate complex technical challenges into clear business contexts for product, design, and agency stakeholders.

  • Invests in growing engineers through coaching, feedback, and creating an environment where teams can thrive.

  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity, making informed trade-offs, and leading teams through complex technical decisions.

  • Motivated by building technology that creates meaningful public impact at national scale.
