About Singpass

Singpass is Singapore’s national digital identity platform, enabling citizens and businesses to securely access digital services across government and the private sector. As a critical part of Singapore’s digital infrastructure, Singpass must remain trusted and resilient while continuously improving the experience of millions of users and thousands of partners.

Data and AI help us detect fraud, understand product performance, make better decisions, automate operations and develop new capabilities.

This is not traditional analytics or reporting role.

You will lead Singpass’ Data Science and AI function across:

  • Trust and Safety
  • Data Platform
  • Product analytics
  • Applied AI and automation

Your mission is to make Singpass:

  • Safer, through better fraud detection and real-time intervention
  • More data-informed, through meaningful metrics and actionable insights
  • More effective, through responsible use of AI and automation
  • Better equipped to innovate, through reusable data and machine-learning capabilities

You will set the direction for how data science and AI are applied across Singpass, while ensuring the function remains grounded in real product and operational problems.

What you will be working on

Data Science & AI Strategy

  • Define and lead Singpass’ Data Science and AI strategy.
  • Identify and prioritise the areas where data science, machine learning and AI can create the greatest impact.
  • Build a coherent portfolio across fraud detection, product analytics, automation and emerging AI use cases.
  • Measure initiatives by their outcomes, not their technical novelty.

Trust & Safety

  • Advance Singpass’ fraud detection capabilities using machine learning, graph methods and other emerging techniques.
  • Improve detection accuracy while reducing false positives and unnecessary user friction.
  • Develop capabilities for real-time risk assessment and intervention.
  • Strengthen collaboration between data scientists, engineers and fraud operations to improve detection and response.

Data Platform & Product Analytics

  • Establish trusted product and mission metrics, supported by strong instrumentation, experimentation and backtesting.
  • Build reusable data capabilities, such as data products, feature stores and querying services, that enable better product and operational decisions.

Applied AI

  • Identify and deliver practical AI use cases with clear measures for the value delivered by AI, such as time saved, quality improved or cases automated.
  • Turn successful prototypes into reliable, maintainable production capabilities built on reusable infrastructure and patterns.

Capability & Responsible AI Leadership

  • Lead, hire and develop Singpass’ data scientists and AI practitioners.
  • Build a flexible function where data scientists remain close to product teams while contributing to Singpass’ highest-priority problems.
  • Ensure Singpass’ use of data and AI remains secure and responsible.
  • Establish standards for model development, evaluation, deployment and monitoring, in partnership with Security, and Governance & Risk teams.

Who We’re Looking For

We are looking for a leader who combines strong technical depth with product judgement and organisational leadership.

You should have:

  • At least 8 years of experience leading data science, machine learning or applied AI teams, with at least 3 years in a supervisory capacity including hiring and developing technical talent.
  • Strong technical foundations in statistical modelling, machine learning, experimentation and modern data platforms.
  • Strong product judgement, and ability to prioritise based on user and operational outcomes.
  • Experience taking data science and AI capabilities from exploration into reliable use.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills, with sound judgement in balancing innovation, delivery, security, privacy and responsible use.
  • Experience in trust and safety, fraud detection, digital identity or public-sector technology will be an advantage.

You will be seconded to the Information Technology (IT) Audit Department of the Auditor-General’s Office (AGO) and be responsible for carrying out IT audits to support the audit of the Government Financial Statements (GFS), other Financial Statements audits, thematic and selective audits of public sector entities. These IT audits are to ascertain the adequacy and effectiveness of controls in Government ICT systems and processes.

You will begin with an intensive three to six months training programme under our experienced IT Audit Shared Services Central team in GovTech, where you will build essential skills before taking on IT Audit Officer role at AGO.

You will formally report to GovTech Director, ICT Audit Shared Services for performance appraisal, with inputs from AGO Audit team.

  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by supervisor.

Government Commercial Cloud (GCC) is a key platform within Singapore Government Technology Stacks that enables government agencies to build and operate digital services on commercial cloud. The GCC Engineering team develops platform automations, landing zones, and security tooling across AWS, Azure, and GCP — serving thousands of government systems and thousands of public officers.

Security at GCC is not a side function — it's core to the platform's value proposition. Government agencies trust GCC to be secure by default.

You are the single named owner of security outcomes across all engineering teams in GCC. You define how security works — the standards, processes, escalation paths, and technical approaches — and drive adoption through influence, not authority. You operate through a Security Champions network: persistent, named engineers in each product team who own security judgment locally, coordinated by you. Your accountability is whether GCC is actually secure — measured through process health, incident response quality, and security posture metrics you define.

This role is part of the organisation's domain leadership structure — you join alongside Engineering Managers as a peer, not as a report to any EM. The Security domain is being stood up fresh. The previous model (centralised security team gatekeeping all decisions) has been retired. You inherit a Champions network in early stages, documented runbooks, and interim coverage from a senior security advisor. Your job is to take it from "interim bridge" to "sustainable, scalable security function."

The domain scope will evolve. Today it centres on the areas listed above — but we expect the role to grow into adjacent areas (AI security, detection engineering) as the organisation's needs develop. Adaptability and willingness to define your own frontier matters more than deep expertise in every area on day one.

[What you will be working on]

Security Architecture & Posture

  • Own the organisation's security posture across all product teams and cloud environments
  • Architect security frameworks that integrate into engineering workflows without creating bottlenecks
  • Design and evolve threat modelling methodologies adapted to the organisation's multi-cloud, multi-tenant context
  • Define escalation paths, severity frameworks, and incident response playbooks
  • Own the relationship with GCSOC, shaping how external security signals translate into internal action
  • Drive security tooling strategy — selecting, configuring, and setting alert thresholds that distinguish signal from noise

Standards & Process Design

  • Define security standards, runbooks, and compliance approaches that teams can self-serve against
  • Design the Security Champions model: training curriculum, forum cadence, escalation criteria, and what "good" looks like for a champion
  • Replace gatekeeping with enablement — move from "security reviews everything" to "teams self-certify against clear criteria, you spot-check and consult"
  • Own security decision records: all posture choices documented, auditable, and transferable
  • Reform compliance processes (e.g. IMR8) to reduce ceremony while maintaining assurance

Cross-Org Influence

  • Drive security adoption across 5-6 engineering teams through the Champions network
  • Run a regular cross-org security forum: shared learning, emerging threats, pattern reviews
  • Consult on high-risk designs and architectural trade-offs when teams escalate
  • Handle genuine security incidents personally, with Champions as informed participants
  • Build security judgment across the engineering organisation — not by centralising decisions, but by raising the floor
  • Serve as the organisation's authoritative security voice on technical matters — advising on vendor evaluations, platform-level policy design, and cross-programme security decisions that require deep domain expertise beyond any single team's scope

Technical Depth

  • Maintain hands-on capability in at least two of: cloud security architecture, application security, supply chain security, detection engineering
  • Evaluate and prototype security tooling; make build-vs-buy recommendations grounded in the org's actual threat model
  • Contribute to or lead security incident post-mortems with root cause analysis that drives systemic improvement
  • Stay current on emerging threats and translate external signals into organisational action

[What we are looking for]

Must-Have

  • Deep security engineering expertise (architecture, not just operations) — you've designed security frameworks, not just followed them
  • Demonstrated ability to influence without authority across multiple engineering teams
  • Experience designing security processes that scale through enablement rather than gatekeeping
  • Strong enough as an engineer to review designs, read code, and earn credibility with senior SWEs
  • Clear, structured communication — you'll write strategies, runbooks, and decision records that outlive you
  • Comfort operating with ambiguity: this role is being stood up for the first time, and you'll shape what it becomes
  • Proficiency in scripting (Python, Bash) and working with APIs — you'll build and review automation, not just specify it
  • Solid understanding of identity, networking, logging, monitoring, and data security in cloud environments

Strong Signals

  • Experience with cloud security across multiple CSPs — ideally hands-on with native security services, not just console-level familiarity
  • Background in both offensive (threat modelling, VAPT, red team) and defensive (SIEM, detection engineering, incident response) security
  • Track record of building security champion or embedded security programs
  • Experience with CNAPP/CSPM platforms and vulnerability management tooling
  • Experience integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps workflows
  • Familiarity with compliance and threat frameworks and the judgment to know when compliance ≠ security
  • Experience working in government or highly regulated environments
  • Awareness of AI security risks and emerging governance frameworks

Technology Landscape

You'll encounter the following in this role. We don't expect mastery of all of these on day one — what matters is the ability to learn quickly and form sound judgment across unfamiliar tools.

| Area | Technologies |

|------|-------------|

| Cloud providers | AWS, Azure, GCP (multi-account/subscription/project at scale) |

| Security posture | Wiz, AWS Security Hub, Azure Defender, GCP Security Command Center |

| Vulnerability management | Nessus, Trivy, AWS Inspector, container scanning |

| SIEM & detection | Elastic SIEM, GuardDuty, Sentinel, CloudTrail/Activity Log |

| Identity & access | IAM (all CSPs), Entra ID, workload identity, RBAC/ABAC patterns |

| IaC & pipelines | Terraform, GitLab CI/CD, policy-as-code (OPA, Sentinel) |

| Secrets & supply chain | Vault, AWS Secrets Manager, SBOM tooling, dependency scanning |

| Compliance frameworks | IMR8, CIS Benchmarks, NIST CSF, ISO 27001, MITRE ATT&CK |

| Scripting & automation | Python, Bash, REST APIs |

| Emerging | AI/LLM security (OWASP LLM Top 10, NIST AI RMF), detection-as-code |

Preferred Certifications

Not required, but signal depth in relevant areas:

  • Cloud security: AWS Security Specialty, Azure Security Engineer Associate, GCP Professional Cloud Security Engineer
  • Security generalist: CISSP, CCSP, or relevant GIAC certifications
  • Offensive: OSCP, GPEN, or equivalent hands-on security testing credentials

Dealbreakers

  • Pure compliance/audit background with no engineering depth — this role requires technical credibility with senior engineers
  • Preference for centralised control ("everything goes through security") — the operating model is distributed enablement
  • Inability to document and codify decisions — if you leave, someone else must be able to pick up without an information gap

About the division:

At Singpass, we aim to provide reliable digital identity for Singapore that streamlines transactions, enables businesses, and protects against fraud. This involves improving the online transaction experience with Singpass and Corppass while keeping it secure. It includes everything from building better frontend applications for residents and keeping an eye on fraudulent transactions to improving internal operations and working with our partners.

What you will be working on:

As an Lead Cybersecurity Engineer, your job will be to:

  • Determine what assurance gaps exist across our product portfolio and decide what assessment approaches best surface real risk and drive meaningful remediation
  • Shape the strategic direction of our cybersecurity assurance programme and prioritise activities based on the threat landscape, product criticality, and organisational risk appetite
  • Work with people from engineering, product, policy, and operations to ensure security assurance is embedded as a rigorous and trusted function across our digital services
  • Measure and track the effectiveness of our assurance activities, from assessment coverage and finding severity trends to remediation rates and compliance posture
  • Wear multiple hats to keep our systems honest. You may be leading a penetration test, conducting a secure architecture review, facilitating a threat modelling exercise, or advising on a governance/risk/compliance matter
  • Build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement with the people you work with

What we are looking for

We are looking for someone who can independently lead a credible and effective assurance function that gives the organisation confidence in the security of its products and practices, and who can operate effectively across a complex, multi-product environment.
In this role, you will:

  • Own and drive assurance impact across the digital identity space
    Take end-to-end ownership of the cybersecurity assurance function across our product portfolio, shaping direction in alignment with Singpass' broader security strategy. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.

Lead Product Manager — Access to Justice & Regulation, Ministry of Law (MLAW)

As Lead Product Manager for Access to Justice and Regulation at the Ministry of Law (MinLaw), you will lead the product strategy and transformation of two of MinLaw's major business verticals.

Your portfolio will span four product domains:

Assess to Justice

  • Legal — helping people who need legal assistance obtain and navigate representation.
  • Community — helping people resolve disputes early and turn legal outcomes into real-world resolution and compliance.

Regulation

  • Licensing — enabling legitimate operators to receive timely permission to operate without compromising regulatory safeguards.
  • Enforcement — helping regulatory teams detect and address risks before they cause serious harm.

Together, these products touch important moments for individuals, businesses and professionals — from seeking legal help and resolving disputes to entering and operating within regulated sectors.

You will help MinLaw rethink how these services should work, organise technology around enduring user problems and policy outcomes, and build the product teams and common capabilities required to deliver them.

In This Role, You Will

  • Own the product strategy across two domains: Access to Justice and Regulation, translating MinLaw's policy outcomes, user needs, operational challenges and technology opportunities into a coherent portfolio direction.
  • Lead and coach Product Managers, giving teams sufficient autonomy to solve their respective problems while ensuring that product strategies reinforce the outcomes of the wider vertical.
  • Define and use outcome measures, establishing meaningful measures of product success and using evidence to understand whether interventions are improving outcomes rather than simply delivering features.
  • Drive the transition from projects to products, establishing enduring ownership and continuous discovery and development instead of treating digitalisation primarily as a sequence of fixed-scope system implementations.
  • Partner deeply with policy and operations, understanding the intent behind legislation, regulation and government programmes while challenging historical processes that unnecessarily constrain user experience or operational effectiveness.
  • Work in close partnership with Engineering and Design leadership, ensuring that product strategy is desirable for users, feasible to build, operationally viable and technically sustainable.
  • Navigate complex product trade-offs, balancing accessibility, regulatory safeguards, policy intent, operational realities, security, cost, delivery risk and long-term sustainability.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You can lead at multiple levels of abstraction. You are comfortable moving from a conversation about MinLaw's strategic outcomes to a product strategy, an investment decision or a specific user problem — without losing sight of how they connect.
  • You think in portfolios, not just products. You understand that good product leadership sometimes means investing in one product, sharing capabilities across several, consolidating existing solutions or deciding not to build something at all.
  • You are an experienced product leader. You have led complex digital products or platforms and can coach Product Managers rather than needing to personally make every product decision.
  • You bring clarity to ambiguity. You can take complex policy, operational and user problems and turn them into clear product choices that multidisciplinary teams can act on.
  • You think in outcomes rather than systems. You naturally ask what problem we are solving and how we will know whether people's lives or regulatory outcomes have improved, rather than starting with a system, feature or predetermined solution.

Experience in government, legal services, regulation or similarly complex domains is advantageous, but not essential. We value demonstrated product leadership, judgement and the ability to learn complex domains over familiarity with a particular industry.

What Success Looks Like

You will have succeeded when:

  • MinLaw is managing Access to Justice and Regulation as products, not collections of systems and projects. Teams have clear ownership of enduring problems and outcomes, with strategies that persist beyond individual initiatives or technology refreshes.
  • There is evidence that the products are making a difference. Teams have meaningful measures of success and can demonstrate how their work is improving outcomes for the people, businesses and officers who rely on MinLaw's services.
  • MinLaw makes better portfolio choices. Investment decisions are increasingly driven by user and policy outcomes, evidence and strategic priorities — including deliberate decisions about what to build, reuse, consolidate, change or stop.
  • The portfolio becomes simpler over time. Common needs across products and regulatory regimes are solved through shared capabilities and platforms where appropriate, reducing unnecessary duplication and fragmentation.
  • Product teams can respond more quickly to change. New policies and emerging needs can increasingly be addressed by evolving existing products and capabilities rather than starting new technology projects from scratch.

Why This Role Is Different

This role sits at an unusual intersection of product leadership, law, regulation, public policy and technology.

You will not be responsible for a single application or transformation programme.

You will lead product strategy across two major areas of MinLaw's mission and work with multiple Product Managers and multidisciplinary teams to transform how those outcomes are delivered.

Some of the problems will require excellent individual products. Others will require common platforms or capabilities spanning several products. Some may be solved through data or AI. And sometimes the right product decision will be to simplify a process or change an operating model rather than build more technology.

The challenge is to see these connections and make deliberate choices about where product teams and technology can create the greatest public value.

The product portfolio, teams and practices you establish will shape how MinLaw delivers access to justice and regulation for years to come.

  • Bring together the data, instrumentation, analytics and research capabilities that already exist within the Software Engineering Practice and partner teams. Establish a coherent measurement approach, address important gaps and extend the capability where needed.

AI is being adopted across government at pace — and with that comes real risk. Models hallucinate. Prompts get injected. Outputs can be unsafe. And AI-generated media is getting harder to spot and easier to produce at scale.

You’ll be part of AssuranceAI — the AI Programme’s function focused on AI behaviour and AI risk — and you’ll own an assigned product area spanning evaluation, runtime safeguards, assurance reporting, and AI manipulation detection.

[What you will be working on]

  • Execute on the product roadmap for AI evaluation — covering groundedness, citation quality, safety and adversarial testing, and regression evaluation.

  • Work with engineering to build and maintain reusable evaluation sets that product teams across the AI Programme can rely on, reducing duplicated effort.

  • Use AI observability data to support groundedness evaluation, unsafe output analysis, and AI risk reporting.

2. Runtime Safeguards

  • Contribute to the development of runtime safeguarding capabilities — including unsafe prompt and output detection, sensitive-content controls, prompt-injection indicators, and policy-based AI controls.

  • Work with engineering to embed safeguards into development workflows, following the assurance-by-design approach established by the team.

  • Support real-time monitoring for model drift, unsafe outputs, and prompt-injection attempts — flagging issues and working with engineering to resolve them.

3. Assurance Reporting

  • Maintain and improve AI assurance reporting — evaluation history, risk and remediation records, and assurance status — contributing to the team’s overall view of AI risk posture.

  • Track and report on defined KPIs: evaluation coverage, guardrail efficacy, mean time to detect vulnerabilities, and policy coverage.

4. AI Manipulation and Online Safety

  • Execute on the product roadmap for a whole-of-government platform that benchmarks and integrates AI detection solutions across image, video, and audio.

  • Support continuous evaluation as the deepfake threat landscape evolves — gathering performance data, surfacing findings, and contributing to decisions on which detection capabilities to onboard, refresh, or retire.

  • Work with capability developers and partner agencies to keep the platform operationally effective as a shared government service.

  • Participate in the Community of Practice across government — sharing benchmarking lessons, datasets, and evaluation insights.

5. Translating Policy into Product

  • Translate defined policy direction and requirements into concrete product specifications, evaluation criteria, and platform features.

  • Work with the AI Practice to keep teams current on the evolving AI risk and vulnerability landscape, and contribute to playbooks and guidance materials.


[What we are looking for]

  • Product experience — You’ve owned products or feature areas end-to-end and know what it takes to ship things that actually work for users.

As a Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. Your core responsibilities include:

Product Manager (Future Courts Management System)

Shape the future of justice in Singapore

Justice is one of Singapore's most important public services. Every year, almost 200,000 cases pass through our courts, involving individuals, families, businesses, lawyers and public agencies. Behind every case is someone seeking a fair, timely and accessible resolution.

The Judiciary's transformation into One Judiciary brought together the Supreme Court, State Courts and Family Justice Courts under a shared vision of delivering justice that is trusted, accessible and ready for the future.

Realising this vision requires more than organisational change. It requires rethinking the digital systems, processes and services that underpin how justice is delivered.

The Future Courts Management System (fCMS) is the Judiciary's flagship digital transformation programme, developed in close partnership with GovTech. You will join GovTech's product management community while working deeply with the Judiciary to shape products that support the administration of justice across Singapore's Courts.

This is not simply a like-for-like replacement of legacy systems. It is an opportunity to reimagine how court services should work: making them easier to use, more responsive to changing legislation and policies, and better able to serve everyone who depends on them.

This is a rare opportunity to help shape how justice will be delivered in Singapore for years to come.

The Role

As a Product Manager, you will be close to these problems and the people experiencing them. You will turn that understanding into product decisions and work with your team to make those decisions real.

You will work as part of a product trio with Engineering and Design, you will own a product problem space within fCMS — understanding the people and processes involved, discovering what should be built, prioritising what matters most, and working with your team to deliver measurable improvements.

As part of GovTech, you will be supported by a wider product, design and engineering community while working deeply with the Judiciary to build long-term digital capability.

In this role, you will:

  • Discover what problems are worth solving, working directly with judges, judicial officers, lawyers, court administrators, partner agencies and members of the public to understand their needs and pain points.

  • Prioritise based on evidence and outcomes, making decisions about what to build now, what to learn more about and what not to build.

  • Deliver value incrementally using modern product and engineering practices that reduce delivery risk, support learning from real usage and avoid big-bang replacement.

  • Measure whether the product is working, defining meaningful measures of success and using qualitative and quantitative evidence to understand where the product should improve.

  • Build alignment around product decisions, communicating the problem, evidence, priorities and trade-offs clearly to stakeholders and your delivery team.

You'll Thrive in This Role If...

  • You are curious about users and their problems. You want to understand why something works the way it does before deciding what should be built.

[About Giant Robots Labs]

Giant Robots Labs is the experimental technology lab inside GovTech's Government Technology Office. We turn ambitious ideas into working products quickly, test them with real users, and operate the promising ones through prototype and limited beta. We also experiment with the lab itself: how small teams are organised, how software gets built when agents do much of the work, and what a product operation needs to look like when a pilot can reach real users in weeks.

Product operations usually exists because coordination, documentation and reporting are expensive manual work. Much of that work is now automatable, and we would rather automate it than staff it. So this is not a role that administers a process, maintains a backlog on someone else's behalf, or turns status into slides. It is the role that makes the lab run: deciding which problems become pilots, clearing the unglamorous path that stands between a working prototype and a real government user, and making sure we can tell whether any of it worked.

[What you will be working on]

  • Run pilot intake. Help decide which problems become pilots, what question each pilot is actually testing, and when it has been answered.
  • Clear the path to real users. Data sharing, security and classification review, agency sponsorship, accounts and access: a pilot team should spend its weeks building, not waiting.
  • Own the operational side of limited beta, including user onboarding and support, incident response, cost and quality monitoring, and the dull reliability work that decides whether an agency trusts us with the next thing.
  • Instrument pilots so that continue-or-kill decisions rest on usage and evidence rather than on who argues hardest.
  • Keep the lab's context legible. Decisions, hypotheses, results and abandoned approaches, recorded in a form that both people and agents can read and act on.
  • Build the lab's internal tooling and automation, agentic where that is the right answer, for the coordination and reporting work that would otherwise eat a team's attention. Where you can build it yourself, build it.
  • Design the lab's ways of working, keep them light, and retire them when they stop earning their keep.
  • Hold the GovTech interfaces: platform teams, identity, data infrastructure, procurement, legal, security. Know who answers which question, and be owed enough favours that the answer arrives in a day.
  • Prepare successful pilots for what comes next, with the evidence, runbook, cost picture and open risks that a productisation team needs in order to pick one up.
  • Notice when a pilot is drifting. No users, an untestable hypothesis, a prototype quietly becoming a system somebody has to run forever. Raise it early, including when nobody wants to hear it.
  • Run the lab's own measurement. How fast pilots move, how many reach real users, what they cost to operate, and which of our decisions turned out to be wrong.
  • Help new people and new teams get productive, which in a lab like this means tools and context more than induction decks.
  • Experiment with the organisation itself. Team shapes, role boundaries, where agents sit in a team, and an honest read on whether last quarter's experiment worked.
You will thrive here if
  • You would rather build or automate an operation than administer one, and you reach for a script, a workflow or an agent before a recurring meeting.
  • You are comfortable that the process does not exist yet and that part of your job is deciding how little of it we need.
  • You enjoy the unglamorous blockers. Approvals, access, classification, procurement and support are where pilots quietly die, and you find it satisfying to kill those delays permanently rather than route around them each time.
  • You can hold an opinion about whether a product is working, and defend it with evidence in a room full of people who built it.
  • You are willing to say that a pilot should stop.
  • You work comfortably with engineers and designers as a peer rather than as coordination between them.
  • You are hands-on with AI tools and curious about what they make unnecessary, including parts of your own job.
  • You are energised by lean teams, broad ownership and problems that change shape every few months.

[What we are looking for]

  • Around 5 to 8 years in product operations, programme or product management, business operations, delivery or a similar role, in an environment where software actually shipped.
  • Evidence you have built or materially changed how a team works, rather than maintained how it already worked. We will ask what you introduced, what you removed, and how you knew which was which.
  • Comfort with data. You can get to the numbers yourself, through SQL, spreadsheets, a BI tool or an analytics stack, and you know the difference between a metric that drives a decision and one that decorates a report.
  • Technical fluency sufficient to work closely with engineers: you can read a system diagram, follow a deployment, understand what an API or an integration implies, and automate your own work.

  • Clear writing. Much of this role is making a decision, a risk or a result legible to people who were not in the room.
  • A track record of high agency: things that happened because you decided they should.
Public sector experience, zero-to-one product environments, or having been the first operations hire somewhere are all strong pluses. None is required.

The Data Platform team builds and operates the foundational data capabilities that power Singpass products and services. Our platform enables secure, reliable, and scalable data ingestion, processing, governance, and analytics, supporting use cases such as operational intelligence, fraud detection, real-time decision-making, business intelligence, and data-driven product innovation.

You will work across data engineering, software engineering, distributed systems, and platform engineering to ensure that data can move securely and reliably across Singpass.

You will:

  • Design, build, and operate scalable data platforms and distributed data systems that support both real-time and batch workloads.
  • Build and evolve event-driven architectures and stream-processing systems, modelling complex event flows to support fraud detection, product insights, business intelligence, and real-time capabilities.

  • Improve developer experience through better tooling, automation, platform abstractions, and engineering workflows.
  • Manage technical debt and continuously improve the reliability, performance, and operability of the platform.

  • Provide technical leadership for complex data platform initiatives from design through production.
  • Lead architecture and technical design discussions, helping teams navigate trade-offs across scalability, reliability, security, performance, and delivery.
  • Establish and champion engineering and DataOps best practices across the platform.
  • Identify opportunities to simplify architectures, strengthen platform capabilities, and improve engineering productivity.
  • Mentor engineers and raise engineering standards through technical guidance, design reviews, code reviews, and knowledge sharing.
  • Influence technical decisions beyond your immediate area and collaborate across teams on shared platform and architecture challenges.

We value strong engineering fundamentals and technical judgment over experience with any particular technology.

  • Have experience designing and operating event-driven architectures, messaging systems, and/or stream-processing systems.

The AI Programme at Singapore’s Ministry of Education (MOE) develops AI products and shared capabilities to support teaching, learning and the work of schools. Our teams bring together product management, engineering, design and data science to identify useful applications, test them with users and improve them through evidence.

Our work spans personalised learning support, feedback and assessment, tools that help teachers plan and carry out their work, and applications that improve school operations. We also develop shared capabilities for AI evaluation, observability and governance, helping teams assess quality, understand failures and build dependable products.

We are looking for a hands-on Senior Data Scientist to build, evaluate and improve these applications. You will work closely with product teams and education-domain colleagues to translate user needs into practical AI solutions, improve their behaviour and establish whether they deliver meaningful benefits in real settings.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with substantial hands-on delivery. You will own selected workstreams, contribute reusable methods and tools, and provide technical guidance and mentoring to colleagues.

What you will be working on

  • Work with product managers, engineers, designers and domain experts to understand user needs, identify suitable AI approaches, and define measurable outcomes and quality expectations

  • Improve AI behaviour through prompt development, structured experimentation and error analysis. Identify whether failures are best addressed through data, prompts, retrieval, model choice, workflow design or human review

  • Design evaluations that reflect how products are used. Develop representative datasets, quality rubrics and test cases with domain experts, including challenging scenarios and important failure modes

  • Use product data, user feedback and targeted experiments to assess usefulness and outcomes. Distinguish improvements in model performance from improvements in the experience and work of users

  • Translate findings into clear recommendations on product priorities, release readiness and further improvements. Communicate limitations, risks and trade-offs to technical and non-technical stakeholders

  • Mentor colleagues, review evaluation approaches and analyses, and share practical methods that other teams can reuse

  • Hands-on experience building and evaluating AI applications, including LLM-based systems, and a practical understanding of their capabilities, limitations and common failure modes

  • Strong Python programming skills and working proficiency in SQL. Experience developing reusable, tested code and reproducible analyses using version control and code review

  • Sound foundations in statistics and experimental design, including sampling, metric selection, uncertainty and assessing whether an observed improvement is meaningful

  • Experience translating product goals and subjective quality expectations into measurable criteria, useful evaluations and actionable findings

The Singapore Judiciary plays a fundamental role in upholding the rule of law and ensuring that justice is accessible, effective and trusted.

For many people, navigating the justice system can be unfamiliar and complex. They may be representing themselves, dealing with a difficult personal situation, or interacting with the Courts for the first time. For lawyers, judicial officers and court staff, complex processes and systems can create a different set of challenges that affect how efficiently and effectively justice is delivered.

As the Senior Designer, you will help make the justice system easier to understand, navigate and participate in — while respecting the legal and procedural safeguards that underpin it.

You will work across the Judiciary with judges, judicial officers, court staff, lawyers, members of the public, self-represented persons, policy and technology teams to understand where people encounter barriers and design better ways for them to interact with the justice system.

This is not simply a role designing digital products. You will help shape how the Judiciary administers, adjudicates and delivers justice, using design, technology and service thinking to improve outcomes for both the people who use the system and the people who operate it.

The Opportunity

The opportunity is to make the justice system easier to understand, navigate and participate in — for the people who use it and the professionals who help deliver it.

This includes members of the public and self-represented persons who may have little or no experience with the Courts, as well as lawyers, paralegals, judges, judicial officers, court administrators and other agencies that interact with the justice system.

For users, accessibility can mean being able to find the right information, understand what they need to do, complete processes with greater confidence, and know what to expect next. For those delivering justice, it can mean having systems and processes that reduce unnecessary administrative burden and allow them to focus on the work that matters.

The challenge is not simply to make every process simpler. Some complexity is necessary because of legal, procedural and institutional requirements. The opportunity for design is to distinguish necessary complexity from accidental complexity — removing avoidable barriers while preserving the safeguards and integrity of the justice system.

Technology, digital services and the systems that support the Judiciary are important enablers of this transformation. By improving how information, processes and services work together, they can help the Judiciary respond more effectively to changing needs, procedures and legislation.

Ultimately, the goal is not the technology itself. The goal is a justice system that works better for the people who depend on it.

What you would do

Understand people and the system

You will research how people and professionals experience the justice system, identifying barriers, pain points and opportunities across services, processes and organisational boundaries. You will use research, workshops and prototyping to turn complex problems into clear opportunities and practical solutions.

Shape better ways of delivering justice

You will work with judicial, legal, policy, operational and technology stakeholders to shape how justice services should work in the future. You will identify whether problems are best addressed through technology, service or process redesign, information, policy or a combination of these. You will design systems and services that help the Judiciary administer, adjudicate and deliver justice more effectively, while making the experience easier to understand and navigate.

Bring people together

You will facilitate co-design and working sessions with judicial, legal, operational, technology and user groups to build alignment around better solutions. You will challenge assumptions constructively, communicate design decisions using research, data, prototypes and user perspectives, and create shared artefacts that help teams work from a common understanding.

Raise the bar for design

You will enforce design standards, patterns and practices that enable consistent, accessible experiences across Judiciary services. You will coach and mentor designers while improving how the team researches, designs, critiques and communicates its work. You will champion responsible use of AI and emerging tools to accelerate design while maintaining quality, accuracy and human judgement.

[What we are looking for]

Experience and craft

  • 8+ years of experience in product design, service design, systems design or a related field, with significant experience leading complex products, services or systems

  • Strong portfolio demonstrating research, synthesis, interaction design, prototyping and delivery.

  • Experience designing complex workflows, professional users or high-stakes environments.

  • Strong systems-thinking ability and experience connecting user needs with organisational, operational and technology considerations.

Stakeholder leadership

  • Proven ability to facilitate alignment across groups with competing priorities and deeply held views.

  • Experience working with senior stakeholders and domain experts who are not design-literate.

  • Comfortable challenging assumptions and presenting design decisions with clarity and conviction.

  • Skilled at translating research and user needs into compelling narratives without oversimplifying complex issues.

  • Able to build trust and lead through influence rather than authority.

  • You are kind, direct and courageous in equal measure — willing to surface difficult problems while bringing people with you towards a better solution.

Ways of working

  • You think in systems but move quickly when the opportunity calls for it.

  • You maintain clear and accessible design artefacts so teams and stakeholders can work from a shared understanding of the current state.

  • You communicate problems early, propose solutions and take ownership of outcomes.

  • You thrive in ambiguity and can turn an unclear problem into a structured approach.

  • You value evidence over assumptions and are willing to change direction when the evidence changes.

  • You can balance user needs with legal, policy, operational and technology constraints.

Nice to have

  • Experience designing services that improve accessibility, inclusion or participation.

  • Experience working in or with the Singapore public sector.

  • Experience designing for people with different levels of digital literacy, professional knowledge or ability.

  • Experience using AI-assisted tools and emerging technologies in design.

  • You have successfully brought people with competing priorities around a shared direction and built design capabilities, systems or practices that create lasting value beyond your own involvement.

Designated as critical IT infrastructure, we favor simple, durable technology choices over the latest trends. We prioritize systems that are easy to reason about, operate, and maintain for the long term.

Success in this role means deploying a platform that is defensible and reliable by design, rather than relying on reactive fixes.

Secure and resilient architecture (core mandate)

  • Own the reference security architecture for the TradeNet CII: trust boundaries, identity architecture, segmentation and trust-zone strategy, east-west controls, encryption and key management, and blast-radius containment for the CII boundary.

We're looking for a Product Manager to own Data Provisioning Standards (DPS) — the rules, schemas, contracts, and governance processes that determine how data enters, moves through, and gets consumed across our platform. This is a foundational, cross-cutting role: you won't own a single user-facing feature, you'll own the standards that every data producer and consumer downstream depends on to trust the data they're working with.

[What you will be working on]

This role sits at the intersection of product, data engineering, and governance. You see policy as a product — DPS is a government mandate, but mandates don't implement themselves.

You'll work closely with Policy stakeholders to shape & operationalise standards, Data Providing Agencies (DPAs) to implement DPS, GovTech's engineering team to build toolings & systems, and Data Consuming Agencies (DCAs) to ensure the data reaching them is consistent, well-documented, and trustworthy for their operations and service delivery.


If you've worked on data contracts, schema governance, API standards, data quality/observability tooling, or consent-and-compliance-driven data exchange, this role will feel familiar.


What You'll Do

  • Define and own what good data provisioning looks like across WOG — spanning Data Quality, Data Delivery Performance and Data Interfacing Standards — and iterate those standards in close collaboration with policy stakeholders, ensuring they remain grounded in what agencies can realistically implement as the ecosystem matures.

  • Design and own the agency support packages for DPS implementation — matching the right level of guidance, tooling, and support to each agency's technical maturity so that compliance is achievable for every agency regardless of where they start.

  • Work with data engineering team to translate standards into tooling that data providers can actually use — spanning data quality validation, metrics computation, pipeline integration, and centralised monitoring.

  • Own the roadmap for data quality and provisioning tooling, prioritizing against data provider pain points through requirements-gathering sessions, downstream consumer needs, and adoption risk (e.g., silent schema drift, incomplete metadata, inconsistent semantics across providers).

  • Define and track success metrics for provisioning health: onboarding time, data quality incident rate, schema compliance rate, time-to-detect for drift/anomalies.

  • Write and maintain clear, versioned documentation of every standard — the standard itself, the rationale, migration guidance for changes, and worked examples.

  • Where standards intersect with regulatory or consent requirements, work with legal/compliance to ensure provisioning rules satisfy consent, data minimization, and audit requirements.

  • Represent the provisioning standards function in cross-team and (where relevant) external/industry forums.

[What we are looking for]

  • 4+ years of product management experience, with meaningful time spent on a data platform, data infrastructure, API platform, or developer-facing product

  • Demonstrated experience defining standards, contracts, or schemas that other teams had to adopt — and successfully driving that adoption across teams you didn't manage.

  • Strong technical fluency with data concepts: schemas, APIs, data contracts, ETL/ELT pipelines, data quality dimensions (completeness, timeliness, accuracy). You don't need to write production code, but you need to be credible in a room with data engineers.

  • A track record of balancing governance rigor against provider/developer experience — you know that a standard nobody can practically comply with is worse than no standard at all. So you'll be as invested in the tooling, templates, and any support that make compliance achievable by data providing agencies.

  • Excellent written communication — this role lives and dies by documentation quality. Comfortable writing specs, migration guides, and decision records that other teams will follow without you in the room.

  • Strong stakeholder management skills: you'll be negotiating with data provider teams who don't report to you and don't always want to change how they work.

  • Comfortable operating with ambiguity in a space that's still maturing — you'll be building some of these standards from scratch, not just maintaining existing ones.

The Mission of Ministry of Transport is to develop Singapore's land, sea and air transport sectors to enhance our economic competitiveness and quality of life in a knowledge-based economy. MOT oversees the development and regulation of the following sectors:

  • Land Transport

As Senior Product Manager for GovTech's Agentic Ecosystem, you will own Console capabilities enabling authorised agents to safely take action across products. Responsibilities include defining roadmaps, partnering with engineering and operations to design guardrails and audit trails, and leading discovery to ensure agents complete end-to-end journeys successfully.

GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore's Smart Nation initiative and digital transformation in the public sector.

DPS programme is building the Central Product Marketplace, the platform where agencies discover, evaluate, subscribe to and run GovTech's central products. We are also exploring how solution agents can help agencies turn problem statements into working digital solutions.

We already have early examples of agents helping teams configure and use digital products through natural-language requests. The next challenge is making it possible for authorised agents to take action across the product lifecycle through Console.

What you'll own

You'll own the Console capabilities that let authorised agents take safe, auditable action across GovTech products on a user's behalf. You will start with a live use case, learn from it, and expand the approach as it proves its value.

The teams responsible for identity, shared agent infrastructure, engineering standards and operational observability own the pieces these capabilities depend on. You will work closely with them to unblock dependencies and keep priority journeys moving. Success means an agent can complete a real journey from start to finish.

You are expected to

  • Own the roadmap for the Console capabilities agents need. Start with the journeys that matter most. Prioritise and build progressively.

  • Define and validate the minimum viable scope before committing to build: what matters for early use cases, and what can wait.

  • Run structured discovery with partner product teams to understand what a solution agent needs from Console to complete a real journey.

  • Set outcome measures for the journeys these capabilities enable, including whether an agent can complete a priority journey from start to finish.

  • Track adoption, reliability and the time needed to enable new capabilities.

  • Design the guardrails for these capabilities: which actions require explicit human approval, and how agent activity is audited. Work with identity and operations partners to get this right.

  • Work with engineering partners on a clear, reusable way for product teams to make their capabilities available to agents. Where a priority journey breaks across product boundaries, spot the gap early and work with the accountable partner to fix it.

You do this by

  • Partnering hands-on with product teams to identify what an agent needs next, and shipping that first, rather than building the full solution speculatively.

  • Tracking early journeys from day one, so usage, failures, approval requests and hand-offs to partner capabilities are measurable, not assumed.

  • Bringing clear product requirements, not coordination requests, to platform partners so agents can use Console reliably.

  • Communicating progress and trade-offs clearly to your product leadership, especially where your roadmap depends on a partner team's timeline.

You'll ultimately be responsible for making it possible for authorised agents to safely subscribe, provision and operate GovTech products through Console, one capability at a time.

You have:

  • 5 to 10 years in product management. Years of experience are a rough guideline.

  • You have owned a product area from problem framing through to shipped, measured outcomes, ideally involving APIs or platform capabilities used by other teams or systems, not just end users.

  • Strong product sense, particularly around scoping a minimum viable capability set and validating it with real usage before expanding.

  • Comfortable with ambiguity. This is new territory, and you can make sensible calls before every detail is settled.

We are looking for a Product Manager to explore and build high-value use cases for AI context layers across government.

AI systems are only as reliable as their understanding of the underlying data. The same term or data field may have different meanings or calculation logic across different government agencies. Without that context, people and AI tools misinterpret data, give wrong answers, or fail to combine sources.

Context layers capture that missing meaning by organising the definitions, business rules, relationships and provenance around government data, in a form both people and AI systems can use.

In this role, you would:
1. Agency context layers — help government agencies identify use cases where context matters most, pilot and build their own context layers, and ensure these can be easily maintained and repeatable across other agencies.
2. A cross-agency context layer — work out how shared meaning can be established across agencies, so data and AI applications work across domain boundaries.

This is an early-stage, zero-to-one product role. You will work closely with agencies, policy owners, data teams, engineers, and users to test hypotheses, deliver practical prototypes, and determine which capabilities should be scaled as common government products or standards.

[What you will be working on]

As a Product Manager, you will hold significant ownership over your product domain, driving it from concept to reality while aligning with the broader programme goals. Your core responsibilities include:

Set the product strategy

  • Define the vision for government context layers and the use cases they should enable.

  • Translate an ambiguous problem space into testable product hypotheses, priority user journeys, and a sequenced roadmap.

  • Define the relationship between agency-specific context layers and shared cross-agency capabilities.

  • Decide what GovTech should build centrally, offer as reusable components, set as standards, or leave to agencies.

  • Align product, engineering, data, AI, policy and agency leadership.

Help agencies build their own context layers

  • Build a network of partner agencies willing to co-develop and test use cases

  • Lead discovery into agencies' data, terminology, business rules, user needs and existing knowledge assets

  • Prioritise high-value operational, analytical, service-delivery and AI use cases, and define success measures for each

  • Ground every context layer in a real product or workflow, not a documentation exercise

  • Define how context layers connect to data platforms, AI systems, search tools, analytics environments and digital services, while meeting security, performance and data governance standards.

  • Test operating models, from agency-led to centrally supported to shared services, and identify adoption barriers such as unclear ownership, maintenance effort and skills gaps.

  • Turn lessons from pilots into reusable playbooks, patterns, tools and onboarding.


Build a cross-agency context layer

  • Identify use cases that need concepts, entities and relationships understood across agency boundaries.

  • Explore how differing definitions, taxonomies, identifiers and data models can be mapped or reconciled.

  • Build and validate prototypes that combine context from multiple agencies for discovery, decision support, analytics or AI applications.

  • Agree ownership, stewardship, contribution and maintenance models for shared context.

  • Work with agencies on trust, provenance, access controls and accountability.

Measure and iterate

  • Define and track product metrics that show real value (e.g. AI answer accuracy, time saved, reuse of context) rather than vanity metrics.

[What you will be working on]

The AI Programme builds shared AI infrastructure that agencies can run in production, instead of rebuilding the same foundations independently. It sits within Government Digital Products, and it owns a small number of central products that a lot of other people's work now depends on.

Three of them shape the job. There's the agent surface public officers use to get through the day: it reaches into their mail, their documents and their case systems, so it has to be quick, honest about what it just did on their behalf, and safe to point at real records. Underneath sits the developer platform, where teams across government bring their own agents, MCP servers and skills and move them into production through review, approval and audit. And there's the model and capability layer that most agencies meet first: a compliant gateway to multiple production-approved models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, alongside shared speech, vision and document capabilities (live transcription, image and video classification, key information extraction) that every agency would otherwise go and procure separately, with guardrails, quotas and cost attribution already attached.

Building an agent demo is easy now, and that's fine, because it means the hard parts have moved. Most of what we work on lives after the demo. An agent decides to call a tool that sends an email on someone's behalf, and the approval gate for that has to be enforced by the runtime, not requested politely in a system prompt. A tool loop needs a stop condition that doesn't depend on the model deciding it's done. Token spend has to trace back to the team that caused it, and when an agency's agent gets slower this week, someone has to be able to say why. Rollback gets interesting when the artefact is a prompt, a tool schema and a model version rather than a binary. Very little of that is model work. It's orchestration, platform and operations, which is roughly the job.
You'll work across all of it: the surfaces officers see, the runtime underneath, the platform other engineers build on, and the unglamorous business of keeping the whole thing up. Your user is a public officer with something to finish today. Your customer is often another engineering team in another agency.

What you'll do

  • Build and run the surfaces officers use daily. Streaming, approval interrupts, resumable sessions, and interfaces that stay readable when an agent is doing four things at once

  • Build the runtime beneath them: tool orchestration, approval gates enforced in code, loop limits, per-turn tool filtering, memory and checkpointing, model routing and fallback

  • Work on the platform half, where the job is to let other teams onboard their own agents, MCP servers, skills and models, with the policy checks and promotion workflows that let them move to production safely and repeatedly

  • Extend the shared capability APIs (speech, vision, document extraction) and keep them fast and cheap enough that agencies reach for them instead of building their own

  • Integrate with what government already runs: identity, mail and calendar, document stores, agency line-of-business systems, the existing CI/CD pipelines

  • Instrument the things you'll want to argue about later. Tool call traces, latency, error taxonomies, cost per team and per feature

  • Build evaluation into delivery, so changing a prompt, a tool or a model becomes a measurable decision instead of an argument

  • Run it. Deployments, incidents, capacity, cost, and the support queue of officers who found the case nobody thought of

  • Work with agency teams as users and as builders, and turn the third bespoke request into a platform feature

  • Take part in security and privacy reviews on the assumption that these systems get audited, because they do

You'll thrive here if

  • You want the thing you wrote to be used by someone doing real work the next morning

  • You're interested in what happens after launch, not only up to it

  • The constraints (classification, audit trails, approvals, cost accountability) read to you as design problems rather than obstacles to route around

  • You have a view on what belongs in a prompt and what belongs in the backend, and you'll defend it

  • You'd rather ship something narrow and run it properly than demo something broad

  • You use agentic coding tools every day and have opinions about where they help and where they quietly cost you

  • You can talk to a policy officer in the morning and debug a streaming protocol after lunch

  • You expect the model layer to change under you every few months, and you design so that's survivable

[What we are looking for]

We're deliberately open on background. This is a broad role, and the strongest signal is something you built, shipped and then had to keep running, not a number of years.

  • Strong engineering fundamentals and fluency in TypeScript or Python (we mostly write React and Node on the front, Python and Node behind it, Postgres, AWS)

  • Comfort moving across frontend, backend, data and cloud rather than settling into one layer

  • Something you've taken end to end: designed it, built it, deployed it, watched it break, fixed it

  • Working knowledge of containers, CI/CD and infrastructure as code (Terraform or similar), or the appetite to pick them up quickly

  • Understanding of authentication, authorisation and careful data handling, which matter more than usual when an agent is the one holding the credentials

  • Practical experience with LLM APIs, tool calling, retrieval or agentic workflows is welcome. Strong engineering and real curiosity will beat an AI-heavy CV with nothing shipped behind it

  • Fluency with agentic development tools such as Claude Code, Codex or Cursor

  • Writing you'd be happy to put in front of someone who will never read the code

  • Reliability with data that belongs to the public


Useful, but genuinely not expected: evaluation harnesses for AI systems, MCP server authoring, streaming protocols (SSE, WebSockets), managed agent runtimes on AWS or GCP, Kubernetes, observability stacks, or any prior public sector work.


If you've built one substantial thing you're proud of and can walk us through the decisions inside it, we'd like to talk. You don't need to have worked on AI systems before.


What you can expect

  • Users from the first week, across agencies with genuinely different needs and maturity

  • An unusual split, where you build the platform and also build on it, so you live with your own abstractions

  • Ownership from design through operations, and the autonomy that has to come with it

  • Colleagues across GovTech's AI Practice, Government Technology Office and product teams, and a mandate broad enough that good work travels

jobDescription:
GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore's Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. As the Centre of Excellence for Infocomm Technology and Smart Systems (ICT & SS), GovTech develops the Singapore Government's capabilities in Data Science & Artificial Intelligence, Application Development, Smart City Technology, Digital Infrastructure, and Cybersecurity. At GovTech, we offer you a purposeful career to make lives better, and we help our people master their craft through learning and development opportunities all year round.

Singpass is Singapore's national digital identity system. It provides high-assurance authentication, digital signatures, corporate identity (Corppass) and government-verified data sharing (Myinfo) to millions of residents and thousands of government and private-sector services. Because it is critical national infrastructure, Singpass is audited continuously against strict security and regulatory controls. Today, most of that audit evidence is collected by hand, point in time, in screenshots and spreadsheets. We want to replace that with continuous, machine-verified compliance: every control measured live, every piece of evidence produced automatically, and every drift detected within minutes instead of at the next audit cycle.

This is a hands-on software engineering role. You will design, write and operate production code and data pipelines. It is not a GRC analyst, audit management or policy-writing role. We are looking for engineers who treat compliance as a software problem: controls as code, evidence as data, audits as queries.

[What you will be working on]

You will join the Singpass GRC engineering effort, working with the Core Platform team, which runs the shared foundations that every Singpass product team builds on: multi-cluster OpenShift on AWS, Istio Ambient service mesh, GitLab CI, ArgoCD GitOps, OpenBao secrets management and YugabyteDB distributed SQL. Your job is to instrument these systems so that their compliance posture can be observed, measured and proven continuously, and to bring the results together in a single pane of glass that auditors, security and engineering leadership can query 24/7.

Continuous Controls Monitoring & Evidence Automation

  • Integrate with the delivery pipeline: Build integrations into GitLab CI and ArgoCD to capture change-management evidence automatically: who changed what, who reviewed and approved it, which tests and security scans ran, and what was deployed where. Target outcomes include signed artefacts, SBOMs, provenance attestations and separation of duties.
  • Instrument the container platform: Collect and normalise control signals from OpenShift clusters, such as Compliance Operator / CIS benchmark results, admission and policy-engine decisions, RBAC and privileged-access state, network and authorization policies, image provenance and Kubernetes audit logs.
  • Instrument the data tier: Build collectors for YugabyteDB clusters that cover database audit logs, role and privilege inventories, encryption and backup posture, and access reviews, while keeping overhead low on production workloads.
  • Extend to the wider estate: Bring in signals from OpenBao (secret lifecycle, lease and rotation compliance), AWS (CloudTrail, Config, Security Hub, IAM), identity providers and SIEM, as the platform grows.

Compliance Data Platform & Single Pane of Glass

  • Design the evidence data model: Build a normalised, tamper-evident, time-series evidence store that maps raw technical signals to control objectives across frameworks (e.g. IM8, ISO/IEC 27001, NIST SP 800-53, CIS). Wherever possible, a single signal should satisfy many controls.
  • Build the pipelines: Write reliable, idempotent ingestion and transformation pipelines with clear lineage, so that every metric on the dashboard can be traced back to its raw evidence.
  • Deliver live audit views: Build dashboards and APIs that show real-time control status, drift, exceptions and remediation SLAs. Auditors should be able to self-serve point-in-time and period-of-time evidence without filing a ticket.
  • Close the loop: Turn failing controls into actionable alerts, tickets or pipeline gates for the owning team, and push fixes upstream into golden paths so that the compliant path is also the default path.

Engineering Leadership

  • Write secure, production-ready code in Go. All GRC services, collectors, pipelines and tooling are written in Go. TypeScript is used only for frontend applications such as the audit dashboard. You will also work with SQL and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/OpenTofu, Helm, Kustomize).
  • Author Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and RFCs, and turn ambiguous regulatory requirements into precise, testable technical controls together with Security, GRC and product teams.
  • Own what you build in production, including SLOs, monitoring, on-call and incident follow-up.
  • Mentor engineers, contribute to technical hiring, and help raise the security and reliability culture across Singpass.

[What we are looking for]

We value strong engineering fundamentals over specific tools. Prior GRC experience is a bonus, not a requirement. If you have built serious platform or data systems and care about proving they are secure, we can teach you the frameworks.

Technical Capabilities

  • Engineering depth: 5+ years of professional software engineering, building and operating production backend, platform or data systems. Strong proficiency in Go, including concurrency, testing and building production services and CLIs.
  • Kubernetes / OpenShift: Hands-on experience running workloads on Kubernetes or OpenShift, including a working understanding of the API server, RBAC, admission control, operators/controllers and audit logging. Experience writing controllers or operators is a strong plus.
  • CI/CD & GitOps: Practical experience extending CI/CD systems (GitLab CI preferred) and GitOps tooling (ArgoCD), including APIs, webhooks, runners, and pipeline-level policy or attestation.
  • Data engineering: Experience designing data models and ingestion pipelines for event, log or time-series data, with strong SQL skills and good judgement on correctness, idempotency and lineage.
  • Security fundamentals: Solid grasp of identity and access management, least privilege, encryption, secrets handling, logging integrity and secure software supply chains.

Ways of Working

  • Translation: You can read a control statement and turn it into a precise, automatable check, and you can explain a technical result clearly to an auditor or policy officer.
  • Ownership: You don't wait for a ticket. You find gaps, ask why, and ship improvements end to end.
  • Documentation first: You write clear designs, runbooks and developer guides that scale knowledge beyond yourself.
  • Integrity: You understand the responsibility of working on national identity infrastructure and handling sensitive audit data.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with policy-as-code (OPA/Rego, Gatekeeper, Kyverno) or compliance-as-code frameworks (OSCAL, OpenSCAP, Compliance Operator).
  • Experience with software supply-chain security, such as Sigstore/cosign, SLSA, in-toto attestations, and SBOM generation and analysis.
  • Exposure to distributed SQL databases (YugabyteDB, CockroachDB, PostgreSQL at scale), including database auditing and access governance.
  • Experience with secrets management platforms (OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault) and AWS security services (CloudTrail, Config, Security Hub).
  • Familiarity with control frameworks and audit regimes such as IM8, ISO/IEC 27001, SOC 2, NIST SP 800-53, PCI DSS or MAS TRM.
  • Experience building observability or analytics products (Grafana, OpenSearch, ClickHouse, or similar) used by non-engineering audiences.
  • Experience building frontend applications in TypeScript (React or similar), for the audit dashboard.
  • Prior experience in highly regulated, high-availability environments (government, defence, fintech).

[What it is like working here]

  • Security-first mindset: National identity infrastructure demands strong engineering discipline, attention to detail and a proactive approach to risk.
  • Greenfield with real stakes: You will help define how Singpass proves its security posture, working on live production systems that the whole nation depends on.
  • Ownership: Engineers shape product direction, argue for robust technical choices, and influence how national systems evolve.
  • Go-first engineering: Go is the only language we use for services and tooling, and TypeScript is reserved for frontend applications. One toolchain means shared libraries, consistent security review and code that any engineer can pick up.
  • Continuous learning: You will work across platform engineering, security, data and regulation alongside diverse teams across government.

About Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF)

The Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) is Singapore's lead ministry for social and family policies, working to build a caring and inclusive society where every individual and family can thrive.

We deliver essential services through our network of Family Service Centres, Social Service Offices, and industry partners, supporting vulnerable populations across all life stages. Our work encompasses family services, early childhood, social assistance, disability support, mental health initiatives, and community development programmes.

We are actively expanding our team to drive impact for our key initiatives including but not limited to:

  • Case Central for integrated case management for Social Service Sector
  • ComLink+ for enhanced community support programme
  • Social Service Coordination Centre for Whole-of-Govt insights
  • Early Childhood programmes that give our youngest citizens the best start in life
  • Sectors Futures Technology to look ahead on sectoral digitalisation and transformation efforts
  • These innovative platforms represent our commitment to leveraging technology and coordinated approaches to better serve Singaporeans.
  • Join our dedicated team of professionals and help make a meaningful difference in the lives of Singaporeans as we work together to nurture strong families and build resilient communities.

[What you will be working on]

We are looking for an experienced Software Engineer to work on technically challenging problems in a modern, product-focused environment, solving important underserved problems in the public sector. The problems we work on include the modernisation of digital services that support Singaporeans on their parenthood journey.

  • Designing and implementing robust, scalable software solutions using modern full-stack web application technologies, with a focus on performance, security, and maintainability
  • Collaborating with product managers, designers, and other engineers to translate business requirements into technical solutions that align with architectural standards and best practices
  • Writing clean, well-tested code and conducting thorough code reviews to maintain high engineering standards across the team
  • Contributing to technical decision-making processes, including technology selection, architectural design, and implementation approaches for complex systems
  • Participating in the full software development lifecycle, from requirements gathering and system design through deployment, monitoring, and maintenance
  • Mentoring junior engineers and sharing knowledge through documentation, technical discussions, and pair programming sessions
  • Working with various teams to ensure smooth deployment pipelines, monitoring, and incident response procedures
  • Contributing to the MSF Engineering Landscape by implementing Infrastructure-as-Code practices, CI/CD pipelines, and compliance requirements across multiple systems and vendor partnerships
  • Staying current with emerging technologies and industry best practices and advocating for their adoption where appropriate to improve engineering effectiveness and system reliability
  • Participating in on-call rotations and incident response to ensure high availability of critical government services

[What we are looking for]

  • 5+ years of professional software development experience with a track record of delivering impactful solutions
  • Extensive experience building and maintaining large-scale, high-availability software systems that serve significant user bases
  • Strong proficiency in modern full-stack web application technologies, particularly Next.js/React.js for frontend development and Java/Python/TypeScript for backend services
  • Deep understanding of software engineering principles including design patterns, data structures, algorithms, and system architecture
  • Experience with cloud platforms, containerisation, and modern deployment practices including CI/CD pipelines and Infrastructure-as-Code
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently on complex technical challenges while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams
  • Commitment to engineering excellence with a focus on code quality, testing, documentation, and maintainable software design
  • Experience working in agile development environments with rapid iteration and continuous delivery practices
  • Familiarity with security best practices and compliance requirements, particularly in government or regulated environments
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders
