WINS (Workpass INtegrated System) is a large-scale Ops-Tech setup in MOM, to implement a multi-year initiative to replace the existing legacy systems and consolidate all work pass transactions into a one-stop integrated workpass system, via an Agile delivery approach.

We provide our customers (MOM users and employers) with reliable, adaptive and simple e-Services to facilitate their work pass transactions. This supports a complementary and sustainable workforce, and anchors Singapore as a global talent hub.

  • (For internal WPD operations) Increasing operational efficiency to reduce operational overheads and increase efficiencies
  • (For internal MOM policy-makers) Support implementation of manpower-related schemes
  • (For external Employment Agencies / HR of Companies) Ensuring reliable e-services to transact with MOM for their employment pass-holders
  • (For external employment pass-holders) Increase customer experience/satisfaction by allowing more direct transactions with MOM, for eligible pass-types

As a Software Engineer, you will lead implementation on critical features as part of the WINS development teams, building the internet eService for company's HR and Employment Agencies to transact with MOM.

MSF is seeking a Software Engineer to work on technically challenging problems in an environment running like a modern product company, solving important underserved problems in the public sector. Some of the problems are related to different programs including healthcare, manpower transformation, trade facilitation, national development, HR and Finance products.

As a Software Engineer, you will take ownership of features end-to-end from building performant, accessible user interfaces with React and Next.js, to designing robust backend services with Java and Spring Boot. You will be a key contributor to engineering quality, championing code reviews, enforcing best practices, and upholding high standards across the codebase.

[What you will be working on]

  • Designing, developing, and maintaining full-stack web applications using React, Next.js (frontend) and Java with Spring Boot (backend).

  • Implementing server-side rendering (SSR) and leveraging the Next.js App Router to deliver fast, SEO-friendly government digital services.

  • Designing and building clean, well-documented RESTful APIs and/or GraphQL endpoints that serve internal and public-facing applications.

  • Conducting thorough and constructive code reviews — ensuring code quality, consistency, readability, and adherence to team standards across every pull request.

  • Championing software engineering best practices including SOLID principles, clean architecture, design patterns, and DRY/KISS principles within the team.

  • Defining and enforcing Git branching strategies (e.g., Gitflow, trunk-based development) and ensuring the team follows disciplined branching, merging, and release workflows.

  • Writing comprehensive automated tests (unit, integration, end-to-end) and advocating for meaningful test coverage as a quality gate.

  • Proactively identifying and resolving technical debt, performance bottlenecks, and security vulnerabilities in the codebase.

  • Collaborating with DevOps and platform teams to maintain and improve CI/CD pipelines, automated linting, and quality checks.

  • Mentoring junior engineers through pair programming, knowledge-sharing sessions, and setting an example of engineering craftsmanship.

  • Participating in architecture discussions, sprint planning, and retrospectives to continuously improve team delivery and engineering practices.

[What we are looking for]

  • Minimum 4+ years of hands-on experience in full-stack software development, working on production-grade web applications that serve real users at scale.

  • Strong proficiency in modern full-stack web technologies; deep experience with React and Next.js on the frontend, and Java with Spring Boot on the backend.

  • Good knowledge of PostgreSQL

  • Proven track record of conducting high-quality code reviews — you can identify bugs, suggest improvements, enforce consistency, and provide constructive feedback that elevates the entire team's output.

  • Strong understanding of Git workflows and branching strategies (Gitflow, trunk-based development, feature branching). You can define and enforce branching conventions, manage release branches, and resolve complex merge conflicts with confidence.

  • Deep commitment to software engineering best practices — you naturally apply SOLID principles, clean code, meaningful naming, proper error handling, and thoughtful abstraction. You write code that others can easily read, maintain, and extend.

  • Experience writing and maintaining automated tests (JUnit, Mockito, Jest, Playwright, Cypress, or equivalent). You understand the testing pyramid, know when to write unit vs. integration vs. E2E tests, and treat testing as a non-negotiable part of the development workflow.

  • Comfort with TypeScript for frontend development and Java for backend development , you leverage TypeScript's type system and Java's strong typing to catch errors early and improve developer experience.

  • Strong understanding of application security fundamentals (OWASP Top 10, input validation, authentication/authorisation patterns, secure API design).

  • A quality-first engineering mindset, you take pride in shipping clean, well-tested, and well-documented code. You do not cut corners, and you hold yourself and your peers to a high standard.

  • Passion towards working for public good with a collaborative, team-oriented attitude. You understand that software engineering is a team sport and invest in making others around you better.

  • Familiarity with Docker, CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, SHIP-HATS), and automated quality gates (linting, static analysis, test coverage thresholds).

  • Experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies and working in cross-functional product teams.

  • A product mindset — you think about the user, not just the ticket.

[Bonus Points]

  • You have worked with Singpass/Corppass integration or government identity systems.

  • You have experience with the Singapore Government Tech Stack (SHIP-HATS, GCC).

  • You are familiar with the Singapore Government Design System (SGDS) and have built accessible interfaces (WCAG 2.1 AA).

  • You have experience with microservices architecture, event-driven patterns, or message queues (SQS, RabbitMQ, Kafka).

  • You have contributed to open-source projects or actively participate in the developer community.

  • You have experience with Infrastructure-as-Code (Terraform, Pulumi) and cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCC).

People's Association (PA) is a statutory board that builds community bonding and promotes racial harmony in Singapore. GovTech partners PA to deliver a suite of digital services that connect residents to grassroots organisations, community programmes, and government services island-wide.

[What you will be working on]

We are seeking an experienced and technically strong engineer to join People's Association (PA). You will serve as the technical authority bridging business strategy and engineering delivery — translating complex requirements into robust, scalable, and secure architectures that underpin citizen-centric digital services.

We are looking for senior and experienced candidates who can hit the ground running and make an immediate impact.

Responsibilities

  • Define and own solution architecture: Produce clear, well-reasoned architecture blueprints that align business requirements with technical implementation across systems, platforms, and integrations.
  • Lead architectural decision-making: Evaluate design options, document trade-offs, and make authoritative decisions on technology choices, integration patterns, and platform strategies.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams: Work closely with product managers, engineers, UX designers, and agency stakeholders to ensure architectures are feasible, aligned, and deliverable.
  • Provide technical governance: Conduct architecture and design reviews, enforce standards, and ensure solutions comply with security, data, and government ICT policies.
  • Guide and mentor engineering teams: Coach engineers on architectural best practices and cultivate a culture of quality and sound design thinking.
  • Manage technical risks and dependencies: Proactively identify architectural risks, integration complexities, and legacy constraints; propose mitigation strategies and pragmatic solutions.
  • Documentation and communication: Produce and maintain architecture artefacts — reference architectures, decision records, integration maps — ensuring they remain current and accessible to stakeholders.
  • Shape technical strategy: Define the multi-year technical roadmap, set organisation-wide architectural standards, and represent PA in whole-of-government technology forums.
  • Stay current with technology trends: Continuously evaluate emerging technologies, cloud-native patterns, and industry best practices to improve PA's technical posture.

[What we are looking for]

Educational Background

  • Bachelor's degree or higher in Computer Science, Information Technology,
    Engineering, or a related field.

Professional Experience

  • 6-12+ years of relevant experience in software engineering or IT, with at least 3 years in a technical lead or principal engineer role.
  • Demonstrated track record of owning end-to-end architecture for production systems at scale.
  • Candidates are expected to have led architecture across multiple teams or platforms and managed stakeholder relationships at the agency level.

Technical Expertise

  • Strong proficiency in cloud architecture, with hands-on experience on at least one major cloud platform (AWS, Azure, or GCP); familiarity with AWS services (ECS/Fargate, Lambda, S3, RDS, API Gateway) is a plus.
  • Deep understanding of microservices, event-driven architecture, API design (REST, GraphQL), and system integration patterns.
  • Experience designing secure systems — encompassing identity and access management, authentication flows, data protection, and compliance with security standards.
  • Familiarity with containerisation and orchestration technologies (Docker, Kubernetes).
  • Knowledge of DevSecOps practices, CI/CD pipelines, and infrastructure-as-code.
  • Understanding of data architecture, including relational databases (MySQL, PostgreSQL) and data integration approaches.
  • Ability to read and review code across relevant technology stacks (e.g., Node.js, React, Python) to ensure architectural intent is faithfully implemented.

Architecture and Design Skills

  • Ability to produce high-quality architecture documentation — C4 diagrams, sequence diagrams, data flow diagrams, and architecture decision records (ADRs).
  • Strong grasp of non-functional requirements: scalability, reliability, observability, performance, and maintainability.
  • Experience facilitating architecture workshops, design reviews, and technical spike sessions.

Problem-Solving Skills

  • Ability to decompose ambiguous business problems into structured, actionable architectural solutions.
  • Pragmatic judgment in balancing ideal design against delivery constraints, technical debt, and operational risk.

Additional Skills (Bonus Points)

  • Experience working with Singapore's whole-of-government ICT systems and platforms (e.g., Singpass, MyInfo, NDI, GovTech shared services).
  • Familiarity with IM8 policies and government ICT security standards.
  • Knowledge of disaster recovery planning and business continuity architecture.
  • Relevant certifications (e.g., AWS Solutions Architect Professional, TOGAF, GCP Professional Architect).
  • Experience with Sitecore CMS for content management and digital experience platform delivery.
  • Familiarity with Imperva for web application security, DDoS protection, and data security.

Character Traits We Look Out For

  • Team player who builds trust and works effectively across engineering, product, and business stakeholders
  • Drive for learning and self-discovery — stays intellectually curious in a fast-moving technology landscape
  • Openness to new ideas and willingness to challenge assumptions constructively
  • Strong sense of ownership and proactiveness in 'making things happen'
  • Willingness and capability to share, document, and impart knowledge
  • Good verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences

We are the GTO – Software Engineering Practice within GovTech, dedicated to uplifting engineering standards, tools, and practices across the organization.   • The GovTech Developer CLI, a unified command-line experience for onboarding and day-to-day tasks

  • Starter Kits and Software Libraries to accelerate secure, consistent development

  • The GovTech Developer Handbook, a central source of truth for engineering practices and guidelines

Drive Infrastructure and DevOps Patterns

Collaborate and Mentor

Contribute to Strategic Engineering Initiatives

GovTech is the lead agency driving Singapore’s Smart Nation initiatives and public sector digital transformation. [What you will be working on]

As a Senior/Staff Software Engineer in Platform Engineering, you will be the principal architect for our multi-cluster container infrastructure. You will shape the technical direction of the core foundations that every Singpass product team builds upon—focusing on resiliency, security compliance, observability, and developer velocity at a national scale.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Architecture & Resilience

  • Architect Multi-Cluster Foundations: Design and evolve a resilient, hub-and-spoke multi-cluster OpenShift / Kubernetes infrastructure on AWS, optimizing for zero downtime, multi-region failover, cost efficiency, and performance.
  • Advance Zero-Trust Infrastructure: Drive the implementation of Istio Ambient mesh, SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity federation, mTLS, and fine-grained authorization policies across complex network topologies.

Platform Engineering & Developer Experience

  • Build Golden Paths: Enable product teams by transforming tenant onboarding and infrastructure management into self-service workflows backed by modular, reusable Terraform/OpenTofu code and clear reference architectures.
  • GitOps at Scale: Standardize declarative continuous delivery using ArgoCD (ApplicationSets, multi-cluster synchronization) and modern CI/CD pipelines.

Security, Compliance & Governance

  • Fortify Security Posture: Lead platform security assessments and penetration test remediations; integrate SIEM logging, privileged access management (PAM), and tight egress controls.
  • Drive Technical Governance: Author Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and technical RFCs, leading cross-functional architecture reviews to set technical standards across Singpass.

Technical Leadership & Mentorship

  • Build Engineering Capability: Mentor senior and mid-level engineers across teams, elevating technical craft, fostering shared ownership of critical systems, and cultivating a strong engineering culture.

[What We Are Looking For]

Technical Capabilities

  • Scale & Expertise: 6+ years in software/platform engineering, with 3+ years architecting and operating mission-critical production Kubernetes/OpenShift (OCP 4.x) platforms used by multiple engineering teams.
  • Service Mesh & Identity: Proven production experience with Istio (Ambient or sidecar topologies) and workload identity systems (SPIFFE/SPIRE or equivalent trust domain federation).
  • Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Expert proficiency in Terraform or OpenTofu, with a track record of building reusable, well-documented module libraries adopted across organizations.
  • Cloud & Networking Depth: Deep expertise in AWS enterprise environments (multi-account landing zones, VPC design, Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, egress filtering, and managed databases).
  • Modern Operations & Security: Practical experience with GitOps (ArgoCD), security remediation, SIEM integration, and architectural compliance in high-security environments.

Leadership & Influence

  • Cross-Team Alignment: Proven ability to establish technical standards and build consensus across disparate teams via RFCs, architecture forums, and clear trade-off analysis.
  • Documentation First: A natural habit of producing clear, accessible runbooks, system designs, and developer guides that scale institutional knowledge.
  • Active Mentorship: Demonstrated commitment to growing engineers outside your direct team structure, helping them achieve measurable career progression.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with enterprise secrets management platforms (OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault).
  • Exposure to distributed SQL databases (YugabyteDB, CockroachDB, or Google Cloud Spanner).
  • Prior experience operating in high-availability, highly regulated environments (government, defense, or fintech).
  • Hands-on experience with Reliability Engineering (SLO/SLI design, incident management leadership).
  • Familiarity with guardrails and tooling for AI-assisted software development.
  • Active contributions to CNCF or open-source infrastructure projects.

About TradeNet

TradeNet is Singapore’s National Single Window for trade permit processing. It processes over 9 million permit applications annually across import, export and transshipment. As one of Singapore’s key trade systems, TradeNet is being brought in-house to strengthen technology ownership and long-term sustainability.

Dsignated as critical IT infrastructure, we favor simple, durable technology choices over the latest trends. We prioritize systems that are easy to reason about, operate, and maintain for the long term.

We operate with high autonomy. Engineers are expected to think deeply, exercise sound judgement, and take ownership of technical decisions. You own the code from technical design through to production. We practice and value honest feedback, practical decision-making and real impact.

In the role of Senior/Staff Software Engineer within Platform Engineering, you will direct the technical evolution of the underlying platform that underpins all TradeNet product development, placing a strong emphasis on resilience, security compliance, observability, and developer efficiency at scale.

Operating horizontally across product squads, Platform Engineering delivers core infrastructure, standardized tooling, reliable runtime environments, automated deployment guardrails, and deep operational visibility. This framework empowers product teams to deliver software safely, efficiently, and autonomously without facing routine operational friction.

You will collaborate closely with software engineering squads, security, and architecture teams to establish scalable platform practices, automate infrastructure delivery, enhance production resilience, and ensure high system availability.

Teams here use AI-assisted development workflows daily. You need to be comfortable with that and will drive adoption of these practices across TechOps.

Platform Architecture & Resilience

  • Advance Zero-Trust Infrastructure: Drive the implementation of Istio Ambient mesh, mTLS, and fine-grained authorization policies across complex network topologies.
  • Observability & Reliability: Establish comprehensive observability, logging, metrics, and alerting to proactively identify and resolve performance bottlenecks, participating in incident response and blameless post-mortems to strengthen MTTR.

Platform Engineering & Developer Experience

  • GitOps at Scale: Standardize declarative continuous delivery using ArgoCD/ Rollouts (ApplicationSets, multi-cluster synchronization) and modern CI/CD pipelines.
  • Governed self-service: Squads deploy independently within approved guardrails, owning the release metrics (deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate, MTTR).

Security, Compliance & Governance

  • Fortify Security Posture: Lead platform security assessments and penetration test remediations; integrate SIEM logging, privileged access management (PAM), and tight egress controls.
  • Drive Technical Governance: Author Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and technical RFCs, leading cross-functional architecture reviews to set technical standards across TradeNet while ensuring compliance readiness (audit evidence, CSA/CSG/IM8 accreditation).

Technical Leadership & Mentorship

  • Build Engineering Capability: Mentor senior and mid-level engineers across teams, elevating technical craft, fostering shared ownership of critical systems, and cultivating a strong engineering culture.

  • Cross-Team Alignment & Leadership: Proven ability to establish technical standards, author clear documentation/runbooks, and build consensus across teams via RFCs and architecture forums.

GovTech’s Culture, Community and Youth Cluster (CCYC) partners with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and its statutory boards — including the National Arts Council, People’s Association, Sport Singapore, and MUIS — to deliver digital products that strengthen community life across Singapore. Singaporeans across community engagement, cultural participation, youth development, and sports and active lifestyle.

This role sits within CCYC and will be working on MUIS products, specifically Muslim.SG.

MUIS (Majlis Ugama Islam Singapura) is the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, the statutory body that looks after the interests of Singapore’s Muslim community. Muslim.SG is its Muslim lifestyle platform — available as a website and on iOS and Android — that aims to inspire and empower Singaporeans through Islamic religious content.

Who We Are Looking For
We are looking for a Senior UX Designer to own the end-to-end design of Muslim.SG — across the web portal and both mobile platforms — from discovery through to launch and continuous improvement.

This is a full product design role. You will conduct research, shape product direction, design the interface, and stay close to whether your work is actually landing with users. You will be the design voice your squad relies on, and the person accountable for the experience quality
of a platform that serves Singapore’s Muslim community every day.

You bring strong craft, clear product thinking, and the ability to navigate the particular design considerations of Muslim.SG — a platform where content is religiously and culturally significant, users span a wide range of digital literacy, and the relationship between the product and its community requires care and sensitivity.

[What you will be working on]

Own the Full Design Arc
Lead design from 0 to 1 to 100 across the Muslim.SG web and mobile products. This means shaping initial concepts, designing and shipping the first version of features, and continuously improving the experience based on data, user feedback, and evolving community needs. You stay accountable to the outcome — you do not hand off and move on.

Design Across Web and Mobile
Muslim.SG lives across three surfaces: a web portal and native apps on iOS and Android. You will maintain design coherence and quality across all three, understanding where the experiences should diverge — in navigation patterns, interaction models, and platform conventions — and where they must converge, in content hierarchy, information presentation, and community tone.

Conduct Continuous, Embedded Research
Run user interviews, usability tests, and contextual checks as a regular part of your workflow— not as a separate phase. Muslim.SG’s user base is genuinely diverse: different levels of digital confidence, different levels of religious literacy, different languages. You stay close to that reality and let it shape your design decisions rather than designing from assumptions.

Bring a product mindset to every design decision. Think about retention, activation, and adoption alongside usability. Use design as a lever for impact: improving onboarding, reducing friction in high-drop-off moments, and creating experiences that make the platform feel valuable enough to return to — especially for users who are developing their own digital habits.

Take ownership of the Muslim.SG design system across web and mobile. Keep components consistent, well-documented, and scalable as the platform grows. You balance system rigour with the pragmatism needed to move at product pace.

Manage Stakeholders and Communicate Design Decisions
Work directly with MUIS stakeholders — community officers, religious officers, operations teams — as well as internal product and engineering partners. Present your work clearly. Advocate for the user. Navigate competing priorities without losing design integrity. When you disagree, you say so with evidence, not volume.

Contribute to Design Culture
As a senior IC, you help set the quality bar. You give constructive feedback, share what you know, and contribute to shared design practices within CCYC. The standard of work you produce, and how you work, shapes what the team collectively considers good.

  • UX Research & Design: Strong UX fundamentals — user research, journey mapping, information architecture and usability — applied pragmatically within a fast-moving product team.

  • UI & Interaction Design: High-craft visual and interaction design skills, including a strong eye for typography, layout, visual hierarchy and microinteractions.

  • Design Systems: Hands-on experience owning or contributing significantly to a component-based design system.

  • Communication: Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills — you can present design rationale confidently, handle pushback constructively, and build trust with non-designers.

  • Autonomy: Self-directed and comfortable with ambiguity — you can manage your own workload, set priorities and deliver independently without close supervision.

Who We Are

We are the Culture, Community and Youth Cluster (CCYC), a team of GovTech designers, engineers, product managers, and business analysts embedded across the statutory boards and autonomous agencies under the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY). Our mission is to partner Singaporeans to build a caring, cohesive and confident nation, across Arts and Heritage, Community, Youth, Sports, and Giving.

Our designers sit within a central CCYC design team, each embedded in their respective agency and reporting to the Head of Design. The portfolio spans products such as:

  • CulturePass: A national platform that democratises access to arts and culture for all Singaporeans.

  • Permanent Resident Journey: A digital platform that helps new permanent residents settle into and integrate with Singapore.

  • NYC Discover Portal: An opportunities portal for youth to explore career paths, connect with mentors, and engage with programmes across life stages.

  • PA Community App: A mobile app connecting residents to local community spaces, happenings, and volunteering opportunities.

You will join this established design team as the first designer embedded in the National Arts Council (NAC). Day-to-day, you will be embedded within NAC's IT Division, whose mission is to strengthen the arts sector's digital capabilities through two pillars: building shared digital infrastructure for a data-driven and resilient arts sector; and supporting technology-driven innovation in artmaking to create new audience experiences.

[What you will be working on]

Your primary focus is NAC's centralised data platform, an integrated environment that consolidates fragmented arts datasets from across the sector. The platform equips NAC and partner agencies with tools to track participation, monitor funding outcomes, and make evidence-based decisions on resource allocation and policy development.

This is a cross-sector product serving both internal NAC officers and external partner agencies, across varying levels of data literacy and distinct workflows. You will gather design requirements together with product managers, engineers, and NAC stakeholders, translating data and policy needs into clear, testable design direction.

As the first designer on the ground, you will also help establish design practice within NAC ITD and shape what comes next as the portfolio grows.

Design Data-Dense Experiences

Design dashboards, visualisations, and analytical interfaces that make complex datasets legible and actionable across a diverse user base. Apply deliberate information architecture and cognitive load management, not just visual design.

Gather and Translate Requirements

Work with product managers, engineers, and stakeholders across NAC and partner agencies to surface the actual need behind a stated request. Translate data and policy requirements into clear, testable design briefs.

Own the Full Design Lifecycle

Take features from concept to production: user flows, wireframes, high-fidelity UI, prototypes, and engineering handoff. Move efficiently across the full stack of UX without needing to be managed through each stage.

Conduct Continuous Research

Run focused usability tests and user interviews to validate how different user groups interpret and act on data. Synthesise findings quickly and feed them back into the design without waiting for a formal research cycle.

Manage Stakeholders Across Agencies

Navigate a complex stakeholder environment across NAC divisions and partner agencies. Communicate design rationale clearly and build trust with stakeholders who may not have worked with a designer before.

Contribute to the Design System

Extend shared CCYC design system components and patterns to cover data visualisation and dashboard use cases. Document contributions clearly for the wider design team

Once it has moved, it has to hold up under sustained volume with clearing deadlines that don't wait for a slow query.

You are the person the programme relies on for this. You own the migration approach, the operational health of the estate, and the standards squads follow when they touch data.

Teams here use AI-assisted development workflows daily, including LLM/agentic-AI tooling for spec building, code generation, and test automation. You are expected to push the boundaries of what's possible with these tools.

[What you will be working on]

Legacy Data Migration

  • Own the migration of legacy production data end to end: extraction, transformation, loading, reconciliation, and cutover. You write and run the scripts, not only the plan.

  • Build the reconciliation tooling that proves the migrated data is correct — row counts, financial sums, referential integrity, and business invariants checked on both sides.

  • Design and execute phased cutovers using dual-write, backfill, and shadow-read approaches, with a rollback path you have rehearsed.

  • Work out what legacy data means before you move it, by reading stored procedures, triggers, constraints, and the table relationships nobody wrote down.

  • Execute complex phased cutovers using a 'Co-existence' model for user cohorts, prioritizing batch-based migration over integrated strangler patterns to minimize legacy dependency risks.

  • Perform detective work to reverse-engineer undocumented business logic from legacy Oracle stored procedures and triggers before migration.

Performance and Tuning

  • Find and fix slow queries. Read execution plans, correct the bad ones, and tell the owning squad what to do differently next time.

  • Own indexing across the estate: add what's needed, remove what isn't, and watch the write cost.

  • Tune instance and server configuration — memory, work_mem, checkpoints, autovacuum, parallelism, connection limits.

  • Diagnose contention under production load: lock waits, long-running and idle-in-transaction connections, deadlocks, hot rows.

  • Own connection pooling and pool sizing, table and index bloat, vacuum strategy, and partitioning of large history tables.

  • Do capacity planning and cost tuning. Right-size instances and storage instead of scaling up by reflex.

Database Operations and Reliability

  • Own backup and recovery, including scheduled test restores and point-in-time recovery. Verifying that backups ran is not the same as knowing you can restore.

  • Own high availability and disaster recovery: streaming replication, read-replica routing, lag monitoring, and failover drills you actually execute.

  • Plan and run major and minor version upgrades with minimal downtime.

  • Build observability for the data layer so problems surface before users report them — slow queries, replication lag, bloat and vacuum health, pool saturation.

  • Take part in on-call for database incidents, lead root-cause analysis, and publish the written follow-up.

Schema, security, and governance

  • Review and approve schema changes and migrations from squads before they reach production, especially on shared and high-volume tables.

  • Run schema change safely against live traffic: online index builds, non-blocking DDL, throttled backfills, expand-contract patterns for column changes.

  • Own access control and least-privilege roles across environments, encryption at rest and in transit, credential rotation, and secrets handling.

  • Implement data classification, masking, and anonymisation for non-production environments.

Technical leadership (without headcount)

  • Set the programme's standards for migration safety, schema change, performance, and operational hygiene, and build the tooling that makes those standards easy to follow.

  • Make the trade-off between data integrity and delivery timelines explicit and visible. Some shortcuts are acceptable; some data damage cannot be undone, and you are the one who says so.

  • Advise application engineers on transaction boundaries, isolation levels, idempotency, retry behaviour, and ORM patterns that generate poor SQL.

  • Deep Oracle expertise: query tuning and execution plans, indexing, partitioning, vacuum and bloat management, replication, connection pooling, configuration tuning.

  • Experience with PostgreSQL as a target architecture, including schema transformation, PL/pgSQL conversion, and heterogeneous replication (Oracle to Postgres).

  • A track record migrating large production datasets off legacy platforms, including reconciliation, phased cutover, and rollback planning where losing data is not an acceptable outcome. You've done this before and know where it goes wrong.

  • Strong operational depth: backup and recovery with tested restores and PITR, high availability, failover, monitoring, and incident response as first responder.

[What Cybersecurity TAP is]

As a Technology Associate in Cybersecurity, you'll begin your career protecting the digital services and infrastructure that millions of people in Singapore rely on every day.

Over the three-year Technology Associate Programme (TAP), you'll build a strong foundation in cybersecurity principles while working alongside experienced engineers, security specialists and product teams on real systems that underpin Singapore's digital government. Through structured rotations, mentorship and hands-on project experience, you'll deepen your technical craft, grow your confidence and gain exposure to different security challenges across the public sector.

You'll have the opportunity to shape your own growth in a supportive and collaborative environment. Along the way, you'll receive guidance from experienced GovTech cybersecurity practitioners and technology leaders, learn alongside a cohort of like-minded associates, and benefit from curated development opportunities that help you build both your technical expertise and leadership potential.

You'll kickstart your career with one of three tracks based on your interests and strengths. On the Security Testing track, you'll hunt down vulnerabilities in critical government systems before adversaries can exploit them. On the Cyber Defence track, you'll work on the front lines of threat detection, analysing malware, tracking threat actors and uncovering the story behind security incidents. On the Product Engineering track, you'll design and build scalable security solutions that strengthen the government's cybersecurity posture across the board. Whichever path you take, you'll contribute meaningfully to Singapore's cyber resilience while learning from practitioners who are invested in your growth.

Whether you're conducting user research, shaping product experiences or designing intuitive and integrated service flows, you'll have opportunities to contribute meaningfully while learning from experienced practitioners who are invested in your growth.

[What Data Engineering TAP is]

Data Engineers build trust by unlocking data's full potential and transforming public service delivery for citizens and businesses at scale.

As a Data Engineer, you will play an integral role in designing trustworthy data systems, pioneering modern technologies, and building lasting data capabilities that form a resilient foundation for a more responsive, data-literate and citizen-centric government. The work spans several key areas.

  • Reliable data at every stage. We design and maintain the pipelines, platforms and infrastructure that keep data flowing reliably across the whole data lifecycle, from ingestion through to consumption. That reliability is what the quality of every downstream insight and service depends on.
  • Scalable foundations for data products. We build the infrastructure and components that let data products grow without breaking, designing systems that stay maintainable, performant and adaptable as needs evolve across teams and agencies.
  • Connecting data to decisions. We bridge the gap between raw data and real outcomes. Through sound data modelling, governance and Data Ops practices, we make sure the right data reaches the right people in a form that is accurate, timely and trustworthy.

Through the Technology Associate Programme (TAP), you will build a strong foundation in Data Engineering by working alongside experienced Data Engineers and solving real data problems for the benefit of our citizens. Structured rotations, mentorship and hands-on project experience will deepen your technical craft, build your confidence and expose you to different problem spaces across the Whole-of-Government.

Whether you're modelling data, engineering ingestion and transformation pipelines, embedding data quality and governance, or exploring how AI can create self-detecting, self-healing and self-optimising pipelines, you will contribute meaningfully while building the reusable platforms and reference architectures that raise the standard of data engineering across government.

[What Product Management or Product Operations TAP is]

As a Technology Associate in Product Management (PM) or Product Operations (Product Ops), you’ll start your career learning how digital products and services are built, operated and improved to solve real problems for people in Singapore.

Over the three-year Technology Associate Programme (TAP), you’ll develop the foundational skills expected of a Product Manager or Product Operations Specialist. You’ll work on well-scoped problems with guidance from experienced practitioners, while collaborating with product managers, product operations specialists, designers, engineers and other partners on real government products and services.

As a Product Manager, you will learn to:

  • Understand and clearly describe the problem you are trying to solve.
  • Conduct user and stakeholder research with guidance.
  • Gather evidence and identify basic patterns and insights.
  • Identify assumptions and learn how to test them before building.
  • Define simple measures of success linked to the problem.
  • Write user stories and support backlog and delivery activities.
  • Work closely with design and engineering to deliver well-scoped product improvements.
  • Understand basic technical concepts and participate in technical discussions.
  • Recognise different options and trade-offs, with support in making product decisions.
  • Learn from feedback, results and things that do not go as planned.

As a Product Operations Specialist, you will learn to:

  • Understand and describe operational problems affecting product teams or users.
  • Support improvements to processes, workflows and ways of working.
  • Gather and use operational data and user feedback to understand what is happening.
  • Support user engagement, onboarding and feedback activities.
  • Coordinate activities and information across product, design, engineering and other stakeholders.
  • Contribute to well-scoped operational improvements with guidance from experienced Product Ops practitioners.
  • Recognise different operational approaches and learn how to evaluate basic trade-offs.
  • Collaborate effectively as part of a cross-functional team.
  • Learn from feedback and continuously improve how you work.

You are not expected to already be an experienced Product Manager or Product Operations Specialist. TAP is designed to give you the experience, coaching and opportunities to build these foundations.

[What we are looking out for]

  • You are a Singapore citizen or Singaporean Permanent Resident
  • You will be graduating from university and are able to commence work in 2027, or have less than one year of work experience.
  • You have a degree in any discipline.
  • You are curious about users, technology and how digital products solve real-world problems.
  • You can break down a problem and explain your thinking clearly.
  • You are willing to gather evidence rather than rely only on assumptions.
  • You enjoy working with people from different disciplines and perspectives.
  • You take ownership of the work given to you and follow through on commitments.
  • You are open to feedback and demonstrate a strong learning mindset.
  • You are comfortable asking questions when you do not know something.
  • You are interested in how technology works, but you do not need to be an engineer.
  • You are motivated to use technology to create meaningful impact for people.

Prior Product Management or Product Operations experience is not required. We welcome evidence from internships, coursework, school projects, personal projects, community work or other experiences that demonstrate your ability to solve problems, collaborate and learn.

About the product

Through the GreenGov initiative, the government has committed to the public its aim to achieve net-zero emissions by approximately 2045. Furthermore, it has established clear and measurable milestones to facilitate progress across all agencies. Since the year 2021, agencies have utilised the eGreenGov portal, which is housed within the National Environment Agency’s Waste and Resource Management System (WRMS), to report various environmental data of their respective premises.

The Public Sector Sustainability Office (PSSO) reviews the progress of agencies, provides updates to the Cabinet, and produces the annual GreenGov report championing the GreenGov initiative. They intend to help agencies identify opportunities to improve resource efficiency and climate resilience, and partner them to streamline the process of implementing these improvements.

  • Execute overall aesthetics that align with branding and design principles

  • Help progressively build and adapt a design system, that scales and flexes across a variety of user groups for the product

As a designer on this product, you’ll also get to learn and experiment with green design practices, taking a truly systemic approach towards responsible design and tech for public good.

  • Demonstrated ability in interaction and visual design — ideally 5+ years of experience in digital design

jobDescription:
The Challenge

The Public Service operates in an increasingly complex environment shaped by changing citizen expectations, workforce shifts, technological disruption and greater interdependence across agencies. Public Sector Transformation (PST) seeks to ensure that the Singapore Public Service remains future-ready, effective and trusted by continually reimagining how the Public Service works, develops its workforce and organises itself.

The PST Cluster leads and coordinates Whole-of-Government transformation. Its role spans setting the vision and strategic direction for PST, catalysing deep organisational and business transformation, building the capabilities and ecosystem needed to sustain change, applying AI to the key challenges of today and mobilising leaders and officers around a shared transformation agenda.

As Assistant Director (Strategy), you will provide strategic and organisational leadership across key PST strategic portfolios, covering sensemaking, conceptualising, catalyst and mobilising workstreams. You will translate emerging priorities and senior leadership direction into coherent strategies, governance arrangements, programmes and resourcing approaches that enable transformation across the Public Service.

This is both a strategy and delivery role. You will work at the intersection of policy, organisational transformation, innovation, technology, workforce capability and public-sector governance, while leading teams to turn broad and often ambiguous ambitions into practical, coordinated action.

Key Responsibilities

As a Team Lead to a team of 3-5 officers, you will:

A. Set and steward the strategic direction for Public Sector Transformation

  • Lead the development and continual refinement of the overarching PST strategy, identifying the major shifts required for the Public Service to remain effective and future-ready.
  • Synthesise emerging operating-environment trends, ground sentiment, organisational data and agency experience to surface strategic priorities and areas requiring Whole-of-Government intervention.
  • Translate senior leadership direction into clear transformation outcomes, priorities, implementation pathways and narratives for agencies, leaders and officers.
  • Ensure PST priorities remain aligned with broader Whole-of-Government, Centre-of-Government and Public Service priorities.
  • Oversee the monitoring and reporting of PST progress, surfacing key achievements, implementation challenges and areas requiring leadership attention.

B. Lead cross-cutting and AI-enabled transformation

  • Shape and coordinate major cross-cutting transformation priorities requiring joint ownership across policy, technology, workforce and corporate-function stakeholders.
  • Provide strategic leadership for AI-enabled PST, ensuring technology adoption is connected to business and workflow redesign, organisational change, workforce implications and measurable outcomes.
  • Work with functional and mission leads to identify high-impact transformation opportunities, define the desired picture of success and establish coherent governance and tracking arrangements.
  • Develop proposals for the capabilities, funding, headcount and specialist support needed to implement transformation at scale.

C. Shape resourcing, governance and implementation arrangements

  • Design governance and operating arrangements that clarify accountability, enable timely decisions and provide progress assurance without imposing unnecessary process.
  • Develop and evaluate funding and manpower proposals for Whole-of-Government transformation initiatives, working with finance and policy partners to align transformation funding with strategic outcomes.
  • Establish portfolio-level measures, review mechanisms and reporting arrangements that support learning and course correction.

D. Mobilise and align Whole-of-Government partners

  • Build trusted relationships with Centre-of-Government partners, ministries, statutory boards, transformation offices and delivery agencies.
  • Convene stakeholders around shared outcomes, particularly where responsibilities and resources are distributed across organisations.
  • Develop engagement approaches across multiple levels, from senior leadership forums to working-level communities and agency visits.

E. Lead teams and manage an evolving portfolio

  • Review and assure the quality of key products, including strategies, submissions, briefs, programme designs and senior-leadership materials.
  • Build a collaborative, high-performing team culture that is comfortable with ambiguity, experimentation and constructive challenge.

Performance management and organisation design are two sides of the same coin. High-performing organisations are built not only through how work is organised, but also through how people are recognised, developed and enabled to perform. In this role, you will design HR policies, people systems and organisational structures that enable the Public Service to deliver for Singapore today and into the future.

Join a team shaping the future of Singapore’s largest employer — with more than 150,000 public officers — and the people systems and policies that enable it to deliver for Singapore. You will be part of a high-performing team responsible for shaping Public Service-wide performance management and organisational design policies that strengthen both individual performance and organisational effectiveness.

Shape the Future of Performance Management

  • Lead the review, design and continuous evolution of Public Service-wide performance management frameworks, including appraisal, ranking and promotion.
  • Design policy, operational and digital solutions that keep performance management simple, effective and future-ready, supporting competency-based careers, diverse career pathways and a future-ready workforce.
  • Reimagine the employee and supervisor experience across the appraisal and development journey, strengthening manager capability, performance conversations and employee growth.
  • Partner across HR policy domains to build a coherent, integrated workforce policy ecosystem.

Design High-Performing and Future-Ready Organisations

  • Partner agencies to design organisation structures, job evaluation and workforce models that strengthen organisational effectiveness and build future-ready capabilities, aligned with strategic workforce plans.
  • Develop organisation structure review guidelines and processes which are agile and fit-for-purpose.
  • Design and enable diverse career roles and pathways across generalist, leadership and specialist tracks, empowering officers with different aspirations to grow and contribute meaningfully across the Public Service.
  • Integrate organisation design and performance management policies to ensure organisation structures, jobs and people systems reinforce one another and drive organisational performance.

Drive Evidence-Based Policy Across Government

  • Work with HR practitioners, data specialists and technology teams to develop HR data products, digital capabilities and analytics that improve policy design, implementation and user experience.
  • Use workforce, organisational and performance data to generate insights, evaluate policy effectiveness and inform strategic workforce decisions.
  • Build trusted partnerships across Ministries, Statutory Boards and the HR community to co-create scalable workforce solutions.
  • Lead cross-functional initiatives spanning policy, operations, data and technology to deliver Public Service HR transformation.
